It is better to ask others for help than to ask yourself. Seeing that things could not be done, Ye Shuo did not hesitate. He opened his mouth and shouted with a hoarse voice: “Come here, come here quickly.”
After all, he was a patient, so Ye Shuo’s voice was much quieter and more vague than usual. In addition, since he could speak, he hardly called anyone at night, so the eunuch sleeping in the outer room didn’t hear it at all.However, outside the window, Wu Yi, who was lying on the tree branch, moved his ears.
There seems to be some movement.
Then he heard the little prince shout twice again. After confirming, Wu Yi jumped down without hesitation.
He quietly pushed open the window and saw the little prince with a red face and coughing non-stop.
Wu Yi was stunned for a moment, then his expression changed slightly.
——The little prince is sick!!!
After receiving the news, the whole Qiuwu Palace was shaken, especially the young eunuch in the outer room, who woke up instantly and almost shouted for help.
The candles in the main hall soon lit up. The Sixth Prince was half asleep in the side hall when he heard some noise. He also heard people outside saying that the youngest prince had a fever in the middle of the night. The Sixth Prince, who originally felt sleepy and weak, shuddered and sat up subconsciously.
Concubine Rong had no time to wash and dress, or even change her clothes. She just casually put on shocks and rushed out in her slippers.
The nanny behind her kept shouting, “My queen, be careful not to catch a cold.”
But how could Concubine Rong care about so many things? Her hair was disheveled and the short distance of less than 20 meters had become a torture. Perhaps because she was too anxious, Concubine Rong soon broke out in a sweat.
She pushed open the door of the room suddenly and looked at the little thing with red cheeks, closed eyes, and almost whole body sunk into the quilt. Concubine Rong’s breathing stopped, her legs went weak, and she almost fell to the ground.
Nanny Yu, who was standing by, was quick to reach out and support her: “Madam!”
Nanny Yu was anxious: “No matter what, the queen must not fall down first!”
“…Definitely not.” Concubine Rong clenched her teeth, dispelled the dark intent in front of her eyes, and staggered towards the wooden bed.
After hearing the noise, Ye Shuo, who was originally full of ashamed and trying to escape from reality, quickly opened his eyes.
After seeing her mother’s current state of embarrassment, Ye Shuo was immediately shocked: “Mom, what’s wrong with you!”
Seeing his full-throated voice, Concubine Rong was startled, and then finally couldn’t control herself and broke down crying: “I thought, I thought you…”
God knows how terrified she was when she saw her son lying there with his chest motionless.
She was afraid that her son would be gone.
Now Ye Shuo knew that she had misunderstood, and immediately explained: “I’m fine…”
Apart from a little tonsillitis and fever, Ye Shuo did not feel any other discomfort. If necessary, he could even lift the quilt, stand up and run a few laps.
In Ye Shuo’s opinion, children have poor resistance, so it is very common for them to catch colds and fevers.
However, Concubine Rong did not think so. Hadn’t she seen how many children in the palace died because of sudden fever in the middle of the night?
Anyway, she wouldn’t believe anything Ye Shuo said now.
Imperial Concubine Rong turned around, her expression uncontrollably fierce, “What are you all standing there for! Hurry up and call the imperial physician, and get the imperial physician on duty to come to me!”
The Chief Physician was the highest official position in the entire Imperial Medical Bureau, equivalent to the director of a modern hospital.
Su Yue did not dare to delay upon hearing this. She bent her knees slightly, not caring about anything else, and ran out quickly with her back to the imperial concubine.
There’s no need to mobilize so many troops…
Ye Shuo hesitated and was about to say something, but when he saw his mother’s eyes suddenly become murderous, he tactfully shut his mouth.
Soon, the Sixth Prince followed closely behind.
Looking at his brother’s flushed face, the Sixth Prince pursed his lips tightly, and his chest rose and fell faster.
“Go and get some cold water.”
“Yes.”
The Sixth Prince had some experience with having a fever in the middle of the night. After all, he had experienced it several times at night when he was younger.
This is the constitution of children. They get sick for no apparent reason.
When the cold water came, the Sixth Prince took a handkerchief from the shelf, soaked it in water, wrung it dry, and then placed it on the forehead of his little brother. The Sixth Prince, who was not even eight years old, acted as calmly as if he was meeting an adult for the first time.
Ah…
Being taken care of by a little kid…
Then a cool feeling came over his forehead, and Ye Shuo felt extremely comfortable.
The Sixth Prince was helping him change his handkerchief, while Imperial Concubine Rong was holding his hand tightly, as if she was afraid that he would suddenly disappear, making it difficult for even a thick-skinned person like Ye Shuo to bear it.
“Mom, Xiao Ming, um… I think I’m actually okay now…”
“Call me Sixth Brother.” Even at this time, the Sixth Prince still corrected him instinctively.
As for what he said about feeling okay, the two of them simply ignored it.
How can we take the patient’s words seriously?
But on the surface, the two of them comforted him: “Yes, yes, yes, mother/brother believe in Shuo’er, Shuo’er will be well soon.”
Ye Shuo: “…………”
This kid’s body…Alas!
The commotion in Qiuwu Palace was so severe that soon most of the palace knew about it.
No one knew what the three virtuous concubines were thinking at the moment, but Zhao Chongrong and the other two couldn’t sleep. As for the queen, she felt half happy, but she herself didn’t know what the other half was.
“What happened outside? Why is it so noisy?”
Wang Ziquan at the door was still hesitating, wondering whether he should wake up the emperor and report to him when such a thing suddenly happened in the palace.
As a result, Emperor Jingwen woke up by himself.
Perhaps because he went to bed late, Emperor Jingwen felt a little uncomfortable in his head. Now he was leaning against the head of the bed, supporting himself with one hand, rubbing his temple from time to time, with a worried look on his face.
That’s right, anyone who is woken up in the middle of the night would probably be in a bad mood, and Emperor Jingwen was very restrained by not getting angry on the spot.
Wang Ziquan took this opportunity to quickly tell the story again: “Your Majesty, it was from Qiuwu Palace, it was, it was the little prince…”
After hesitating for a while, Wang Ziquan gritted his teeth and finally finished speaking: “The little prince seems to be in trouble. He said that he suddenly had a high fever in the middle of the night.”
Emperor Jingwen stopped pressing his temple and said, “What?!”
“What happened? Why did you suddenly have a fever?”
“I, I don’t know either…”
Just when Wang Ziquan was unsure whether the emperor would go or not, the emperor in the room suddenly raised his voice: “Someone, change my clothes!”
It looks like the emperor plans to go and take a look in person.
Wang Ziquan first waved to the eunuchs and palace maids nearby, and while they were filing in, he gave orders to prepare to drive the sedan chair immediately.
Emperor Jingwen’s thoughts were a little confused as he opened the curtain in front of him.
He saw the little bastard was fine some time ago, how come he suddenly——
Perhaps because of his relationship with the Duke of Zhen, his youngest son was almost the healthiest prince he had ever seen. From the time he was born to now, which was more than two years, he had only consulted an imperial physician once, but the result was still a mistake.
Emperor Jingwen had never imagined what his youngest son would look like if he were sick.
The little bastard is so good at making people angry, nothing will go wrong.
Thinking of this, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but feel a sense of inexplicable irritation in his heart. Then he lowered his head and felt that the eunuchs and palace maids’ hands and feet seemed to have become particularly clumsy today.
“Get out of the way, I’ll do it myself!”
Unable to wait any longer, Emperor Jingwen kicked the man in front of him, ignored the man’s kneeling begging for mercy, and started fighting himself.
Perhaps because he couldn’t calm down, Emperor Jingwen buttoned a wrong button.
Emperor Jingwen realized it only after he sat in the sedan chair, and then adjusted himself in time.
Then, his heart calmed down.
Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but think a lot along the way. He felt that it was time to clean up the harem.
After one stick of incense, the imperial carriage arrived at the gate of Qiuwu Palace.
“The Emperor has arrived——”
Following the eunuch’s shouts at the door, Emperor Jingwen stepped over the threshold and walked straight towards the side hall where Ye Shuo lived.
“What happened? Why did he suddenly get sick?”
Hearing such a voice behind her, the imperial concubine was startled at first, and subconsciously wanted to salute, but was interrupted by Emperor Jingwen: “No need to be polite, let me see how Shuo’er is first.”
Then he saw his little son with red cheeks under the quilt.
After not seeing my youngest son for a few days, the baby fat on his face has disappeared.
Emperor Jingwen was startled and also frightened by Ye Shuo’s current appearance: “Why did you suddenly become so thin?”
Ye Shuo: “…”
Please stop saying he has lost weight. It’s not that he is too thin now, but that he was too fat before.
My figure now is just right, isn’t it?
While the Sixth Prince was changing his handkerchief, Emperor Jingwen reached out and touched his youngest son’s forehead, which was very hot.
Emperor Jingwen frowned tightly, and he was immediately filled with anger: “What on earth is going on!”
“This is all your fault, Your Majesty.” She didn’t want to say it, but after hearing this, Concubine Rong couldn’t hold it in any longer and tears fell down her cheeks.
“You arranged for Wu Yi to watch Shuo’er for twelve hours a day without stopping for a moment, not allowing him to do this or that, and only allowing him to study. Shuo’er is only two years old now, how can his body bear it!”
Was it because he pushed too hard…
Emperor Jingwen tightened his grip around the beads.
Wu Yi, who was standing in the dark, couldn’t help but feel confused.
Could it be that I really did something wrong?
But, he clearly didn’t push him too hard…
In the gap of silence between the two, Concubine Rong was still crying, and every word she said was sobbing: “I have been in the palace for so many years, and I only have one child, Shuo’er. If Shuo’er gets into trouble this time, what will I do?”
At this moment, the imperial concubine wanted nothing anymore. The crown prince and the throne were not as important as her son being alive.
“What nonsense are you talking about? Are you blaming me?”
Emperor Jingwen didn’t believe that his son, the grandson of the Duke of Zhen, would be so easily swept away by a high temperature.
His son is the son of a dragon, blessed by the gods and Buddhas, how could it be possible that –
Seeing his mother crying so hard, Ye Shuo felt bad too. He tried to persuade her, but it was of no use at all.
After tossing and turning for so long, the noises around him gave Ye Shuo a headache. He was also sick now, so he couldn’t help feeling a little sleepy.
But thinking back to what happened just now, he was afraid that he would scare his mother again after closing his eyes. After thinking for a while, Ye Shuo asked cautiously, “Father, Mother, I am very sleepy. Can I take a nap for a while…”
The child’s red cheeks, weak and hoarse voice, and eyelids that seemed to be about to close in the next second——
Emperor Jingwen had seen such a scene many years ago, but after the child closed his eyes, he never woke up again.
All of a sudden, Emperor Jingwen’s heart sank and he took a deep breath.

chapters.title: Chapter 34: Conscience
chapters.content:
Seeing that the child closed his eyes after he finished speaking, Emperor Jingwen and the Imperial Concubine immediately panicked.
“No sleeping! I order you not to sleep, do you hear me?!”
“Shuo’er, Shuo’er, don’t sleep. Open your eyes and look at your mother, okay?”
Wu Yi, who was standing next to him, was struck by lightning when he saw this scene.
I seem to have…really killed the little prince…
Wu Yi lowered his head and looked at his hands, his mind went blank.
Emperor Jingwen was stunned at first, as if he couldn’t react to the scene before him. He gasped uncontrollably twice and then became furious: “Where’s the imperial physician? Why hasn’t the imperial physician arrived yet?”
The gray-haired imperial physician was caught by Su Yue and rushed over breathlessly. Coincidentally, he just happened to hear crying and shouting coming from the side hall. He was caught off guard and his heart skipped a beat.
It’s over, judging from the noise, could the little prince be dead?
This, this, this… It has only been less than two incense sticks since the people from Qiuwu Palace came to invite us. Even if it is a high fever, it can’t be so fast, right? ?Could it be poisoning, or something else?
At this moment, the Imperial Physician thought a lot and even began to wonder if he had been accidentally involved in the struggle in the harem. In an instant, he even thought about how to escape and save his life.
What should I do?
Crying out in pain in his heart, under the pressure of the emperor and the imperial concubine’s eyes, the imperial physician nervously felt the little prince’s pulse.
After a moment, the imperial physician was stunned.
……Eh??
It doesn’t seem to be a big deal.
The little prince’s pulse was strong, proving that he was in good health. But seeing how nervous the emperor and the imperial concubine were, and the imperial concubine’s eyes were now swollen from crying, the imperial physician felt that things were not that simple.
No, no, no, look at it again.
To be on the safe side, the imperial physician examined the patient several times.
But what he didn’t know was that, because his expression was too serious (he suspected that it was a harem struggle) and his brows were furrowed (he really couldn’t tell anything else and had some doubts about his true level), even Emperor Jingwen couldn’t hold it back, his brows were tightened, and he looked shocked and angry.
Finally, under the almost desperate gaze of the imperial concubine, the imperial physician gave his own judgment very cautiously: “Your Majesty, her Highness, the little prince has caught a cold, and his high fever hadn’t gone away.”
Then what?
Just gone? ?
After waiting for a long time, there was still no follow-up. Finally, the emperor was the first to react: “If that’s the case, then why is Shuo’er still unconscious?”
This……
The Imperial Physician cupped his hands, hesitated for a while, and then answered: “He is not unconscious. The little prince must be too tired, so he went to bed early. The little prince is young and has a weak resistance. He falls asleep much faster than adults due to his physical condition.”
As for children, they may even be talking one moment and fall asleep the next moment when they turn around. This is perfectly normal.
Emperor Jingwen: “…”
Imperial Concubine: “…”
The Sixth Prince: “…”
It turns out that when he said sleepy, he really meant sleepy in the literal sense…
Wu Yi on the side breathed a sigh of relief.
Even though his youngest son was still sick, for some reason, Emperor Jingwen still wanted to pull him out of bed and give him a good beating.
Can’t you just say it clearly?!
Turning his head, out of sight, out of mind, Emperor Jingwen asked again: “The weather has been fine in recent days, how come the little prince got caught in the wind?”
Wu Yi seemed to have remembered something, and spoke with some difficulty: “Your Majesty, there seems to be a wind vent behind the rockery where the little prince and I stayed this afternoon.”
It’s not too far from Qiuwu Palace, and it’s a good place Ye Shuo recently discovered. Anyway, with Wu Yi following him, he can go anywhere in the palace.
The rockery was designed with a hole, and the breeze blew through it, making it very cool. Midsummer had just passed, and the autumn heat was prevalent. Ye Shuo was so afraid of heat that he didn’t think too much about it at the time.
Even Wu Yi didn’t take it seriously. After all, in his opinion, such a small breeze was not even enough to fill the gaps between his teeth. What’s more, if it hadn’t blown his hair up, Wu Yi wouldn’t even feel that there was any wind there.
Unexpectedly, such a small negligence caused the little prince to suddenly have a fever at night.
Wu Yi suddenly had a better understanding of the fragility of children.
Wu Yi, who had fought in the midst of swords and sabers and treated injuries as a common occurrence and had been seriously injured and on the verge of death several times, realized belatedly that a little bit of wind could take the life of a child.
It’s indeed him!
After hearing this, the imperial concubine couldn’t help but glared at Wu Yi fiercely like a knife.
Upon seeing this, Wu Yi lowered his head in silence.
But in fact, it had nothing to do with the wind. After all, it was not the first day that Ye Shuo stayed there. It was just inexplicable and a coincidence.
If you look for excuses after something happens, you will always find them.
The Imperial Physician did not delve into the matter further. He stroked his beard and directly concluded: “That’s it. Children are fragile and cannot withstand the wind.”
Thinking of the rumors in the palace, the imperial physician said, “My lord, don’t push too hard on everything. The little prince is still young and is in the period of growth. He must not be overworked. Reading and writing are important, but if you continue like this for a long time, it may damage his foundation.”
It is now widely rumored that the Emperor assigned the secret guard to the little prince, and that the secret guard stared at the little prince almost non-stop for twelve hours. Then the imperial physician who had never seen the little prince in person actually believed this nonsense.
So in the final analysis, it is still my own problem.
Perhaps he was really too harsh on his youngest son.
Emperor Jingwen remained silent and played with the beads faster.
Wu Yi vaguely felt that something was wrong, but he really couldn’t find it, so gradually, he agreed with what the imperial physician said.
Although the little prince’s pulse is strong, as the imperial physician, the Imperial Physician never likes to make promises. Everyone in the palace is extremely cautious.
Therefore, the imperial physician said: “Although the little prince is not seriously ill at the moment, if the high fever does not subside in the second half of the night, he will still be in great danger.”
Even though the little prince is in good condition now and the possibility of the temperature rising further in the second half of the night is not great, I still have to make it clear in advance, right?
“Well, I understand. Go get the medicine.”
Emperor Jingwen waved his hand absentmindedly at the imperial physician and said nothing more.
Now that he had finished looking at the scene and there was nothing else to do, Wang Ziquan thought that the Emperor was probably about to leave, and he was about to give orders to have the carriage prepared.
Who would have thought that Emperor Jingwen would simply stay in Qiuwu Palace!
Wang Ziquan was shocked.
You know, except for the crown prince, other princes have never had such an honor.
But in fact, this is not a special honor. The main reason is that the previous children’s illnesses had basically nothing to do with Emperor Jingwen. Ye Shuo is the first prince who fell ill because of Emperor Jingwen’s decision, so naturally it is different.
If he hadn’t given such an order, the child wouldn’t have behaved like this.
Thinking of this, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help feeling guilty.
The imperial concubine was guarding the side hall, and since the morning court would begin in an hour or two, Emperor Jingwen had to at least have a rest.
It was natural for them to enter the main hall of Qiuwu Palace. After Wang Ziquan had directed the palace servants to tidy up everything, he suddenly heard these words:
“Wang Ziquan, tell me, is this really my fault?”
Wang Ziquan immediately broke out in a cold sweat.
How should he answer this question?
Fortunately, Emperor Jingwen did not seem to want an answer from him, and after this sentence, he did not mention it again.
But just this one sentence was enough to scare Wang Ziquan.
Even if the emperor really made mistakes, they were all other people’s faults. Since the emperor said so, it shows how deeply shocked he was at the moment.
Others didn’t know, how could Emperor Jingwen not know?
The youngest son almost couldn’t be born because of him, and he almost died after he was born because of him. Now he is seriously ill because of him.
After a long time, Emperor Jingwen slowly closed his eyes.
The next morning, Ye Shuo was still asleep when Emperor Jingwen went to court. When he left the court, he naturally headed towards Qiuwu Palace.
The second prince frowned subconsciously when he saw this. He always felt that his father seemed to care too much about his younger brother. He suddenly wanted to see who his little younger brother was and why he could make his father so worried.
In the past one or two years, the palace has been filled with rumors about this little prince, which are even bigger than the one caused by the imperial concubine before.
But thinking that he was not familiar with this little prince, who was ill, and might get into trouble if something happened, the Second Prince gave up after thinking about it.
Let’s leave it for now and talk about this matter later.
The crown prince didn’t have so many concerns. After the court session, he walked together with Emperor Jingwen: “Father, are you going to Qiuwu Palace to visit my little brother? That’s great. I plan to go with you.”
Emperor Jingwen naturally would not refuse.
At this time, Ye Shuo’s temperature had dropped. The imperial concubine could not bear it any longer, and went to sleep in the main hall after the nanny’s repeated urging.
Reaching out to touch his youngest son’s forehead, he found that it was not so hot anymore, and Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but feel relieved.
Only at this moment did he have time to look at Wu Yi, who had also been guarding all night.
Wu Yi’s heart tightened, but he had no intention of resisting, and immediately knelt down obediently: “I am guilty, please punish me, Your Majesty.”
He was indeed guilty. After all, Emperor Jingwen had only asked him to watch over the little prince and not let him go astray, but he had not asked him to keep an eye on him for 12 hours.
It was because he pushed too hard and used too much force that his youngest son fell ill.
“Wu Yi, in that case, you can do it yourself–“
Ye Shuo vaguely heard the quarrel around him again. As soon as he opened his eyes, he saw Wu Yi kneeling there, ready to be punished. He was immediately shocked and sat up to plead for him without thinking: “Father, wait a moment!”
Regardless of his dry and hoarse throat, Ye Shuo hurriedly said: “This matter has nothing to do with Wu Yi. This son accidentally caught a cold, so…”
“Ahem…”
Halfway through his words, Ye Shuo couldn’t bear it anymore and started coughing violently.
Seeing this, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but stepped forward to help him, and habitually patted his back with his other hand: “Slow down, slow down, lie down quickly, the fever has finally subsided, what if you catch a cold again?”
Noticing that his stepfather’s tone was exceptionally gentle, Ye Shuo felt as if he had seen a ghost, his heart filled with fear.
Is this really his father? Has he really not been replaced by someone else? ? ?
Later, Ye Shuo discovered that something even more terrifying was yet to come.
Wu looked up subconsciously, then froze.
He thought that the little prince would hate him after suffering such a great crime, but in the end, he was not angry at all…
Wu Yi couldn’t help but feel even more guilty: “Your Highness, this is my fault alone. Your Highness, you don’t have to beg for mercy. I am willing to accept the punishment.”
Even though he treated the little prince like this, he was willing to forgive him.
Wu Yi turned his eyes away, not daring to look at him again. Then Wu Yi couldn’t help but kowtow to Emperor Jingwen again.
Seeing Wu Yi’s guilty expression, which looked like he wanted to commit suicide to apologize, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but take a breath.
Hiss–
Help, my conscience hurts!

chapters.title: Chapter 35: Master
chapters.content:
After a while, Ye Shuo recovered and tried to persuade him: “It’s me who wants to go to the rockery, and it’s me who wants to enjoy the breeze there. What does it have to do with you?”
Wu Yi lowered his eyes and said, “It is my fault that I did not stop the young prince in time.”
Ye Shuo: “…”
You talk as if you can really make the decision for me, and I don’t even think about when have I ever listened to you.
Covering his aching chest, Ye Shuo choked, then continued to guide him: “You also said that I am the master, and you are the servant. If I insist on doing it my own way, you will have no way to stop me. Can you really force me to make a choice that I don’t like?”
“Naturally.”
Unexpectedly, Wu Yi did not think it was wrong after hearing it, but nodded very affirmatively: “I only listen to Your Majesty and obey Your Majesty’s orders. Your Majesty has instructed me before, so when I sense danger, I can take the little prince away from there regardless of his objection.”
However, he did not. He failed to realize in time that the wind from the rockery would hurt the little prince’s body. This was a dereliction of duty.
The more he talked, the guilt in Wu Yi’s heart not only did not subside, but became heavier.
Ye Shuo stared at this scene in amazement, his whole body trembling violently.Did Wu Yi really not think carefully about the question: apart from reading stories to himself, working part-time as a storyteller, and accompanying himself on adventures, had he really done anything else from beginning to end?
He studied for an entire afternoon and his voice became hoarse. If I were adventurous, he would almost accompany me around the entire palace. When I was tired, I would have to ask him to carry me back. Moreover, if I could read a few more new words, I would have to find ways to get some reward from him.
The first reward was shooting darts, the second reward was shooting flying needles, the third was shooting flying knives, the fourth, the fifth… Soon Ye Shuo would have learned all his hidden weapon skills, and even now Wu Yi still felt like he was coaxing a child.
Even so, Wu Yi still felt that the little prince was very easy to satisfy. Just sticking two needles into a tree could make him excited for a long time. He was so easy to deal with.
Therefore, there will definitely be no problem with such a sensible little prince. The only one with a problem is himself.
Ye Shuo: “…”
Stop talking, stop talking. Ye Shuo was almost overwhelmed by guilt.
Even someone as thick-skinned and black-hearted as Ye Shuo couldn’t stand it, which shows how innocent Wu Yi is.
Seeing that he really couldn’t convince himself, Ye Shuo closed his eyes, made up his mind, and decided to use the skill that made children famous – crying.
Ye Shuo was unreasonable and uncooperative, crying and making a fuss, and he refused to let his stepfather punish him.
There is no other way. I have said everything that needs to be said. This is the only trick left.
Although it’s a bit embarrassing, the effect is great.
You know what, this trick really works. Seeing that his youngest son was so determined and his high fever had just subsided, Emperor Jingwen was afraid that he would make a fuss and start having a fever again. He really thought about it seriously. Finally, considering his youngest son’s illness, he decided to reluctantly agree to his request this time.
“Get up, Wu Yi.”
Emperor Jingwen said indifferently: “Since the little prince pleads for you, I will forgive you this time.”
Wu Yi was stunned for a long time, then slowly stood up from the ground: “Thank you, Your Majesty, thank you, Your Highness.”
Ye Shuo silently covered his chest, and when he felt better, he lay down again.
Wu Yi quickly left. Just as he was about to close the door, the prince, who had been silent all this time, finally couldn’t help but ask a question he really wanted to know: “I see that you seem to treat Wu Yi very differently. Why?”
If it were him, if someone was watching him like this every day, the prince would think he was lucky enough not to be crazy, and would not be nice to that person.
Emperor Jingwen was also somewhat curious about this question, and as the prince finished speaking, he could not help but turn his head.
Ye Shuo thought for a moment and said sincerely: “Because I think Wu Yi is a good person.”
Isn’t it true? He gave away martial arts and hidden weapons, and the part-time storyteller and bodyguard didn’t complain at all. Such kind-hearted people are rare in this world. Ye Shuo wished that the other party would follow him like this forever.
Getting a master for free + someone who can answer all kinds of difficulties in learning martial arts at any time is really a huge profit. With Wu Yi, it doesn’t matter if I walk sideways in this palace, there will be no danger.
Ye Shuo didn’t hesitate and directly sent a good guy card.
Emotions surged up all at once, and then Ye Shuo’s expression became serious, and he spoke word by word: “In my heart, I regard Wu Yi as my teacher.”
When the prince heard this, he was shocked.
Emperor Jingwen, who was standing by, was also looking at his son in shock.
Facing the child’s serious and somewhat solemn expression, the two of them suddenly had the same thought in their minds: Oh no, could this child have a fever that damaged his brain? ?
At the same time, Wu Yi outside the door also widened his eyes, and his heart trembled unconsciously.
Because of his training, he already had excellent hearing and vision, so even if he was standing outside, he could hear everything going on in the room clearly.
When Su Yue came over with the cold water, what she saw was Wu Yi standing there like a wooden stake.
“This lord, this lord?”
He suddenly woke up unexpectedly, and before the palace maid in front of him could see his expression clearly, Wu Yi kicked his feet in panic, and the whole person instantly jumped two meters, jumped onto the tree next to him, and disappeared in the blink of an eye.
Su Yue: “?”
*
As if frightened by the expression of his younger son/younger brother that did not seem fake, Emperor Jingwen and the crown prince were silent for a long time. After looking at each other, the crown prince decided that he must ask the imperial physician later whether there was something wrong with the prescription he prescribed, or whether his younger brother really had a brain burnt out to say such a thing.
In order to dispel his idea, Emperor Jingwen explained to his youngest son: “Shuo’er, you must know that Wu Yi is a secret guard. I will never let him be your master.”
What are the secret guards? The secret guards are a group of people who are directly under the leadership of the emperor, who only obey the command of the emperor and are only responsible to the emperor.
The secret guards are the private property of the emperor and are the knife in the hands of the emperor. The most taboo thing is to be contaminated by the princes.
Once the secret guards are involved with the prince, it means being drawn into the vortex of the struggle for imperial power, which will pose a threat to the emperor’s life.
Therefore, Emperor Jingwen could never tolerate this.
“Can you understand what I’m saying?”
Ye Shuo nodded, “Son understands.”
“This son originally thought that he would learn martial arts from Wu Yi…”
The identity of a secret guard is very sensitive in itself, and the skills of a secret guard are even more sensitive.
If the prince learns it, how can the secret guards prevent it? If the prince has the intention to kill, won’t the emperor be in danger all the time?
But since they are just children, the idea of ​​martial arts is understandable.
Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but touch his youngest son’s head and said, “When you grow up and go to the upper study, there will naturally be a martial arts master to teach you.”
As the son of an emperor, it is not enough to just be literate. The minimum requirement is to be proficient in both civil and martial arts. The rest include riding, archery, driving, etc., not to mention the six arts of a gentleman.
Ye Shuo couldn’t help but smack his lips, as expected, the involution among the royal family members was so serious.
When Ye Shuo came into contact with the Sixth Prince, he did not see any internal strength in him, so he guessed that he had not formally started learning yet.
As for the Crown Prince, Ye Shuo didn’t know martial arts when he approached him before, and now that he knows martial arts, he still hasn’t found a chance to get close to him.
After experimenting with Wu Yi countless times, Ye Shuo discovered that internal force was not so easy to detect. He needed to directly touch the opponent’s dantian with his hands. The prince’s belly was not so easy to touch. Ye Shuo was even afraid that the servants around him would catch him and chop off his claws.
However, judging from the prince’s behavior, Ye Shuo estimated that his kung fu was not very good.
He is so busy every day that he wishes he could be split in half. It would be strange if he could be good at kung fu.
It seems that the quality of the martial arts master that my cheap dad mentioned is worrying.
Thinking of this, Ye Shuo asked straightforwardly, “How does Master in the upper study compare to Wu Yi?”
How can this be compared? Wu Yi is the best martial artist among the Dark Guards. He was carefully selected from the Dark Guards. Although there are also powerful martial artists among the martial arts masters, how can the masters selected from the people have the deep foundation of the royal family?
In fact, it was not because Emperor Jingwen was stingy and unwilling to give it, nor was it because the emperor was on guard against his son everywhere. It was mainly because martial arts were too difficult to practice. A person’s energy was always limited. There were so many people practicing martial arts in the world, and the total number was much larger than that of the royal family. How could we expect such a few people in the royal family to become the first? The probability was too low.
And even if you become the first, so what? You can’t rule the world by martial arts.
Emperor Jingwen did not give a direct answer, but said: “The martial arts is only a minor path after all, you and your brothers are not on this path.”
Ye Shuo understood it instantly, so the meaning was quite different.
It turned out that I was right to keep a trick in advance.
Ye Shuo also noticed that his adoptive father seemed to be particularly averse to the prince learning martial arts, especially the martial arts of the secret guards, so he secretly decided in his heart that he would never let him know that he had secretly learned Wu Yi’s martial arts.
Facing his youngest son’s disappointed expression, Emperor Jingwen changed from touching to patting and patted his head.
The imperial concubine in the main hall couldn’t sleep well because she was always thinking about her son. She woke up in less than half an hour.
Seeing that the little guy finally woke up, and the fever subsided, the imperial concubine couldn’t help but hugged him in her arms.
“There can’t be a next time, you really scared me to death!”
“Mother, it’s Shuo’er’s fault. Shuo’er will never dare to do it again…” Ye Shuo felt heartbroken when he noticed the faint blue color under his mother’s eyes.
When she thought about him standing in the limelight, the imperial concubine was so angry that she wanted to beat him up, but in the end, she couldn’t do it. She just said with red eyes: “It’s good that you’re okay, it’s good that you’re okay.”
Ye Shuo felt inexplicably sad.
It was really nice to be loved by his own mother. Apart from being held down and not allowed to get out of bed, he had no other problems. Even his mother fed him personally.
“Your Highness has really suffered a great crime this time.”
Ye Shuo would help Wu Yi explain almost everything to anyone who came. For example, the first thing Zhao Chongrong and the other two did when they entered the room was to glare at Wu Yi who was standing next to them, and they did so while comforting Ye Shuo.
Ye Shuo had no choice but to repeat what he said before: “It’s really not him, it’s me who insisted on standing in the wind.”
However, the more he explained, the lower Wu Yi buried his head.
However, this was not the most unbearable thing for Ye Shuo. What was most unbearable for Ye Shuo was that Wu Yi seemed to be particularly nice to him in recent days.
Although Wu Yi still looked cold and silent on the surface, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but fall into deep thought as he looked at the peeled fruit Wu Yi handed over to him.
Even though he said that it was prepared by Su Yue and the others, Ye Shuo had seen his knife skills, and the skin was peeled so thinly, it was definitely Wu Yi’s work.
After a long time, when Ye Shuo was able to get out of bed and move around freely, he couldn’t help but cautiously asked, “Can I not practice calligraphy today? I haven’t made clay figures for a long time.”
I thought Wu Yi would refuse, but –
“…Okay.” Wu Yi nodded after a moment’s silence: “That’s right, I know a good place in the palace.”
He he he agreed!!!
Ye Shuo felt a chill in his heart.
It’s over, Wu Yi finally broke down.

chapters.title: Chapter 36: Leaving
chapters.content:
This is a cold-blooded and ruthless secret guard!
But now it’s really not cold or cool at all.
When I think of how unkind he was at the beginning, I really miss him.
Ye Shuo whimpered and collapsed into the quilt.
Wu Yi, who was standing by, couldn’t help but get a little nervous when he saw this: “Are you okay, little prince?”
It seemed that he was frightened by the fact that just two gusts of wind could make the little prince seriously ill, so now whenever there was any sign of trouble, Wu Yi would ask carefully.
This is how people who have never raised a child are. Wu Yi has not yet evolved to the point where he has to check whether Ye Shuo’s breathing is normal when he is sleeping.
Ever since the high fever incident, Concubine Rong forced even the young eunuchs sleeping in the outer room to move in, for fear that such a situation would happen again.
This time, Wu Yi had sharp ears and discovered it in time. What about next time? If no one responded when he called out, he would have burned to death inside after a night.
So no, absolutely not, he must not be allowed to sleep alone!Ye Shuo had no way to resist and could only agree reluctantly.
After the little eunuch came, it seriously affected Ye Shuo’s practice at night. He had no choice but to ask Su Xin to help them make a blackout curtain. When he went to bed at night, he would draw the blackout curtain so that no one could see what the person inside was doing.
Although his mother teased him about this, saying that he was young but still shy and couldn’t stand others even looking at him, Ye Shuo was so thick-skinned that he didn’t feel embarrassed at all. He said openly in front of everyone: “No one can see my body except my future wife.”
At that time, Concubine Rong burst out laughing: “How old are you? You’re already thinking about getting married?”
Ye Shuo snorted: “Age is not important. It’s always right to prepare early.”
What if, what if his wife cares about this?
If you love her, you should naturally give her the best and not let her have any regrets.
But when he thought about it, he had never found a partner who loved him in his previous life, and he was still a bachelor until his death. This life would probably be tough too, and Ye Shuo immediately became depressed.
Alas, in life, why is it so difficult to find someone you love, and who loves you back?
No matter what the other person’s identity is, it can be a noble lady or a commoner, a chivalrous woman or an ordinary palace maid, Ye Shuo doesn’t care, the most important thing is that both parties love each other.
As a modern man, equality and freedom have long been engraved in Ye Shuo’s bones, and have never changed even now.
It’s just that he couldn’t change the situation alone, so he just went with the flow.
As for the fact that his status as a prince destined him to have no freedom in marriage in this life and that he could only be manipulated like a puppet, Ye Shuo said that this was not true. No matter what, his wife had to be the one he deeply loved.
When the time comes, his stepfather will be furious, the ministers will pressure him, and the royal family will be shocked, but Ye Shuo won’t care. After all, he was not born to please and obey these people, and his marriage will never be a bargaining chip.
He didn’t want to fight for that position anyway. As the saying goes, a man without desires is strong. His cheap father couldn’t threaten him.
If those people turned their spearheads against his beloved woman, Ye Shuo thought to himself that he was not so incapable of doing this.
Of course, he is not even three years old yet, so it is too early to talk about these things. Ye Shuo dare not say them out loud now. After all, they are too unorthodox and can really make his stepfather mad to death.
It’s better to wait a little longer and let my cheap dad live a few more years in peace.
Ye Shuo had already made plans in his mind in advance. Now everything was ready, except for a wife.
But thinking about his experiences in his previous life, Ye Shuo instantly felt hopeless.
Forget it, forget it. Don’t think about it anymore. If that person doesn’t show up, it will be useless even if I have thought of where my grandson will go to school.
Let’s take a look at Wu Yi who is so close to us.
Meeting Wu Yi’s slightly nervous gaze, Ye Shuo collapsed on the bed and replied weakly, “I’m fine.”
Wu Yi opened his mouth and said hesitantly: “The clay figurine…”
Ye Shuo waved his hand: “Forget it, forget it, I won’t go today.”
If it wasn’t for the crime going against the wind, it would feel too boring.
Since Wu Yi is already broken, it would be better to let him break more thoroughly.
My conscience aches, it can’t be in vain, right?
It’s going to hurt anyway, so why not just call it pain in a more literal sense, so it doesn’t seem so unfair.
So… Ye Shuo not only did not stop, but intensified it. He took advantage of the time when Wu Yi was surrounded by guilt and took out almost everything he could from Wu Yi’s body.
Ye Shuo learned all of Wu Yi’s skills, including the technique of launching hidden weapons, the skill of concealing breath, the skill of lightness, etc. Ye Shuo estimated that ordinary secret guards now knew less than he did.
Just like now, Ye Shuo didn’t need to go out of his way to investigate. As long as he was close, he could basically find out in time whether there were people on the surrounding trees and beams, and how many people there were.
As for the mud on the soles of Wu Yi’s boots, you have to know that the soil in the palace is not like this. The answer to where the scattered mud on Wu Yi’s boots came from is self-evident.
When Wu Yi habitually ran back and forth among the trees and grass, flower petals and grass debris were accidentally stuck in his hair and clothes. Ye Shuo once picked up half of a petal that fell from his body when he was not paying attention.
Maybe it was because the petals were very small, or maybe it was because the petals were very ordinary, so Wu Yi saw them but didn’t care at all.
Wu Yi ignored the fact that it was precisely because the petals were ordinary that he needed to be more careful.
There was not a single ordinary flower or grass in the palace, and basically all of them could be named. It happened that Ye Shuo had already visited the entire palace, so he could tell at a glance whether there was a particular species in the palace.
Wu Yi never thought that there was actually someone who could remember so many flowers and plants in his mind.
But Ye Shuo on the side understood it very well. When doing official work, in addition to guards and assassins like Wu Yi, there might be a special team in the secret guard team to help with the aftermath and create the scene. Otherwise, if there was no special team to deal with such things, the secret guards would have gone through countless setbacks over the years.
Just when Ye Shuo was about to get in touch with the core secrets of the secret guards, he thought about it and stopped at the door of the gate. In the end, he chose not to go in. At least he left Wu Yi with a pair of pants and did not let him run completely naked.
Fortunately, not long after, Wu Yi received a secret order from Emperor Jingwen, and then he packed up and prepared to leave.
If he didn’t leave, Ye Shuo estimated that he might not be able to resist touching those things.
Wu Yi had no idea that it was this sudden order that saved him from danger and enabled him to successfully save the last bit of his dignity.
Emperor Jingwen’s secret order came very urgently, and it was estimated that there was something important for Wu Yi to do.
Of course, he certainly couldn’t say that to the little prince Wu Yi. He certainly couldn’t say that the emperor asked him to do something, so he left. Emperor Jingwen asked him to make up a reason, so Wu Yi really made up a reason.
Looking at the secret guard who was talking nonsense in a serious manner and was about to be unable to justify himself, Ye Shuo could not help but fall into deep thought.
As expected, you can’t have your cake and eat it too. You can only choose one between intelligence and loyalty. If you choose one, it will be difficult to take into account the other.
It is difficult to guarantee the loyalty of smart people who know how to judge the situation, and the reason why loyal people are loyal is often because they are not smart enough.
Not smart enough, but in line with the superior’s wishes.
After Wu Yi finished speaking, Ye Shuo spoke for a long time before he spoke with difficulty: “You mean, your fellow villager’s father came to Beijing for medical treatment recently, and because he has no relatives, he came to you for help, and then you can’t stay here recently, right?”
Please, the secret guards are directly responsible for the emperor’s safety and cannot be involved with any forces. They are most likely orphans, so how could they have any relatives, fellow townsmen or friends?
Does Wu Yi think he is a three-year-old child?
Wait a minute, I seem to be just a three-year-old child.
Wu Yi, on the other hand, was still unaware of this and even nodded affirmatively: “Your Highness, yes.”
The corners of Ye Shuo’s mouth twitched involuntarily.
He really dares to admit it…
It was hard to express in words what was in his mind, and then Ye Shuo asked out of the blue: “How old is your fellow countryman’s father this year?”
“Your Highness, he is 25 years old.”
Ye Shuo asked again: “How old are you this year?”
“…”
Wu Yi was stunned for a moment. After a moment, he froze his expression and whispered, “Also, it’s also 25.”
Wow, what a coincidence.
Ye Shuo had a wooden face, it turned out that his fellow villager was Wu Yi himself.
For someone like Wu Yi who has to find materials from his surroundings and himself when making up stories, Ye Shuo sincerely advises him to stop lying from now on.
Just when Wu Yi was sweating profusely and wondering if he had been discovered, he saw the little prince flipping something out from the head of the bed and throwing it towards him.
Wu Yi subconsciously reached out to catch it, and after he caught it, he discovered that it was an amulet.
“Your Highness, this is…”
“After I fell ill, my mother asked my aunt outside the palace to pray at the temple.” There was no other way. He had taken too many advantages of Wu Yi, and it would be bad for him to leave empty-handed when the other party left, right?
I can only ask my mother for another one later.
Ye Shuo waved his hand weakly: “This amulet is for you… no, it’s for your fellow villager’s father. I hope that Buddha and Guanyin Bodhisattva can protect him and keep him safe and sound in the end.” Ye Shuo deliberately emphasized a few words in the middle.
But in fact, the story about the father from the same hometown was all made up by him.
This amulet can be given to no one except himself.
Wu Yi tightened his grip on the amulet. After a long moment, he lowered his eyes and said, “Thank you, Your Highness.” Without waiting for Ye Shuo’s reaction, he disappeared in a flash.
Wu Yi’s departure seemed to be an episode that could not be any smaller. His departure had no impact on Qiuwu Palace at all, and even Concubine Rong breathed a sigh of relief.
Although Wu Yi has been a little more lenient with his son in recent days due to the emperor’s order, with someone always there, Concubine Rong still worries that her son won’t be able to bear it.
Fortunately, Wu Yi is finally gone now.
Concubine Rong thought about it and finally did not force her son to study anymore. Ye Shuo was also happy and at ease, and had a great time for several months.
It wasn’t until the beginning of the following spring that new troubles came.
Because of this matter, Concubine Rong was so worried that she couldn’t sleep well for several days.
After the New Year, he grew one year older. He is already three years old this year. If we count his age in lunar calendar, he is already five years old. It is time for him to go to the study.

chapters.title: Chapter 37: Irritability
chapters.content:
Although it seems very common that the Sixth Prince did not go to the upper study until he was seven years old, in fact, the Sixth Prince’s case was truly special.
No one cared for the Sixth Prince in the past, and no one urged him to go to school. Later, he was taken in by Imperial Concubine Rong, who kept him for several months to make up for his basics. He was then sent to the Imperial Study, where he successfully studied with the other princes.
Although the official age stipulated by the Imperial Study Room was six years old for school entry, almost no princes could actually wait until they were six years old.
It was better in the past few years. When Emperor Jingwen was still the crown prince, everyone still followed the rules and did not push their son so hard.
Later, when Emperor Jingwen ascended the throne and became emperor, as the number of children in the harem gradually increased, the age at which the princes went to school became younger and younger.
Some even waited until the child could speak, walk steadily, and understand what others were saying, and they sent him in directly regardless of his age.
For example, the eighth prince born to Concubine De is three years older than Ye Shuo. He has been studying in the upper study room for almost three years. In other words, he was sent in when he was just over three years old.
Children of the royal family were born precocious, as if they were born to remember things earlier than children of ordinary families. They rarely made trouble, and Emperor Jingwen was happy to see his children become successful, so he never cared about them.
Under such vicious competition, everyone will naturally become more and more competitive.
And once you start, it’s hard to stop.That was why the Imperial Concubine was worried. She also didn’t want her son to lose at the starting line. When she thought of Concubine De, Concubine Xian, Concubine Shu, and the Fourth Prince, the Fifth Prince, the Seventh Prince, and the Eighth Prince, Imperial Concubine Rong felt chest tightness, shortness of breath, and very anxious.
If they weren’t there, the imperial concubine wouldn’t be so anxious.
If Ye Shuo were here, he would definitely be able to empathize with this feeling.
It’s just like taking an exam. She had just finished writing the multiple-choice questions and fill-in-the-blank questions, while the students around her had already finished the last two big questions. No one would be able to hold back if they were in her shoes.
However, her son’s health is also an important factor that the imperial concubine has to take into consideration.
After the previous high fever, the Imperial Concubine was really scared. If it was before, she would definitely do the same as the Virtuous Concubine and the others and just send it over without thinking too much about it.
But now, the imperial concubine couldn’t help but start thinking in her heart, Shuo’er is only three years old now, isn’t it too early to send him to the upper study room now?
Although he is five years old in terms of age, he is only three years old in actual age.
If it happened again like before, the imperial concubine couldn’t guarantee that her son would be so lucky.
Perhaps it was because Concubine Rong’s anxiety was too obvious, Ye Shuo noticed it the next day. He asked casually, and after finding out what happened, he was completely stunned.
Three years old! Here, children have to go to school at the age of three? ?
If it was a kindergarten, Ye Shuo could still understand it. A bunch of kids playing and fighting together would make a day pass by, which was equivalent to reducing the burden on busy working parents.
But! The upper study room here is obviously not that! !
Thinking of the “Encouragement to Study” that the Sixth Prince had recited before, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but be amazed.
This is totally not something a three-year-old should learn!
So Ye Shuo decisively pushed away the bowl in the nanny’s hand, and didn’t even bother to eat. He jumped off the chair, ran over, grabbed his mother’s sleeve, and looked at her eagerly: “Mom…”
The imperial concubine immediately softened her heart.
She thought to herself that Shuo’er was still young, so it wouldn’t matter if she delayed it for another year, so she said softly, “Okay, Shuo’er, don’t worry, we won’t go this year.”
Ye Shuo couldn’t help but breathe a sigh of relief.
“Mom, you are so good to Shuo’er. You are the best mother in the world.” Ye Shuo did not say this intentionally to flatter his mother, but he sincerely felt this way.
In such a feudal society, where imperial power was supreme, women in the harem gave birth to children mostly to consolidate their own status. For them, children were just a means to climb up or consolidate their favor.
It’s not that they don’t love them, but this love, as long as it doesn’t involve life, should take precedence over rights.
In simple terms, as long as you can’t die, fight to the death.
But there are very few people like his mother who voluntarily give up the competition simply because of his health.
His mother may not know that as long as he is careful, things like last time will basically not happen, but she dare not take the risk because of such a tiny probability, which shows how deeply his mother loves him.
“Mom, I want to be your son in my next life and the next life.”
Meeting the child’s serious and determined gaze, for some reason, Concubine Rong’s eyes suddenly turned red.
After she realized what was happening, she quickly slapped her son on the back of his hand: “Pah, pah, pah, what are you talking about?”
“What’s the next life, the next life? It’s so unlucky, just spit it out.”
Then the imperial concubine couldn’t help but tap his nose and said, “You are just a nice person. You always say nice things to fool your mother. If you really think your mother is good, you will make her less angry with you in the future. Your mother will be thankful.”
That wouldn’t work. What his mother hoped for, such as competing for the throne, was something he could never do.
In addition to the fact that he has no ambitions here, there is also the fact that if he really shows signs of this, he and his mother should be fine, but his grandfather’s family will definitely be doomed.
So forget it.
Ye Shuo came to his senses instantly, and his expression suddenly became embarrassed.
Well…I don’t know if it’s too late to take back what I just said.
No one knows a son better than his mother. Seeing him like this, the imperial concubine immediately understood what had happened. The feeling of being touched in her heart disappeared in an instant, and she was immediately filled with anger: “Well, you little bastard, you really lied to me!”
“Mom, I suddenly remembered that the prince still wants to talk to me about something. I’ll leave first. Bye!”
“Come back, come back to me!”
Looking at the two people playing and fighting early in the morning, the nanny next to them put the bowl in her hand back on the table and couldn’t help laughing.
But in fact, Ye Shuo was not lying. The prince did have an appointment with him, but it was not the prince who made an appointment with him, but he who made an appointment with the prince.
The one-year ban is finally over. How can I not visit the East Palace?
Although the prince didn’t know why his younger brother had such a good impression of him, he didn’t reject it.
As for the future, we’ll talk about it later.
Ye Shuo had picked a random time to go there, without thinking too much about it, but he didn’t expect that he would run into an unexpected person by coincidence.
Judging from the patterns on the other person’s red official robe, this person should be his brother’s teacher.
Prince’s tutor?
“Greetings to His Majesty.”
Just as Ye Shuo was stunned, the person opposite him spoke and slowly bowed to him.
Although there was nothing wrong with the other party’s behavior, Ye Shuo didn’t know why, but he always felt that something was strange.
Soon, he understood.
His brother’s teacher seemed particularly distant and cold towards him.
Isn’t it? Since the other party is the prince’s teacher, he is naturally the one who upholds orthodoxy. To a prince like himself who is of unorthodox origin, he would naturally be rude.
By the way, this was the first time in Ye Shuo’s life that he was disliked by a teacher. In his previous life, he was the teacher’s sweetheart wherever he went.
Such an experience is quite novel.
Ye Shuo was thinking at this time, and the tutor opposite him was also thinking.
He had not expected that he would run into the imperial concubine’s son so suddenly. He still remembered that the birth of the little prince almost made the prince’s situation even more difficult.
Therefore, the Grand Tutor naturally disliked this prince.
Today, the Grand Tutor saw that he was behaving so recklessly and was even more disgusted. He didn’t look like a prince at all. How could a prince run around and jump so disrespectfully? How could he be so disrespectful!
Of course, this was not what the Taifu was most concerned about. What was most concerning to the Taifu was the child in front of him, who almost led astray the student he had taught for so long.
When the child was just over one year old, he was already eating grapes and listening to music. What would happen if the prince also developed these bad habits?
The Grand Tutor has always been a man of integrity. He would never show intimacy to people he doesn’t like. It is already his limit if he can resist showing disgust.
So after Ye Shuo asked him to get up, the tutor left without wasting a moment.
The Grand Tutor didn’t know the Imperial Concubine’s plan at this time. He thought that the little prince would go to school this year. When he thought that his old rival was going to torture the little prince, the Grand Tutor suddenly didn’t feel bored anymore, and even vaguely revealed a sense of relief.
The prince did not expect that his teacher would be so hostile to his younger brother, and even unwilling to stay in the East Palace for long.
Then he thought about how the teacher hated lazy and extravagant young men the most, and he felt that the teacher’s behavior was very normal.
But he has to comfort my little brother.
After a brief thought, the prince ordered people to fetch the new tribute fruits from the south.
On the other side, in the Qinzheng Hall——
Emperor Jingwen soon learned the news that his youngest son would not be attending school this year. Hearing this, he just frowned slightly and did not take it to heart.
In his opinion, it is a good thing for his younger son to start school later.
It took him two full years to finally reach a delicate balance with the Duke of Zhen. Under the circumstances, Emperor Jingwen himself did not want this balance to be destroyed.
Also, my youngest son had already shown extraordinary intelligence when he was over two years old. Once he starts school, his development will surely be extremely rapid.
Emperor Jingwen was very conflicted. He hoped that his youngest son would be successful, but at the same time he was worried that he would be too successful.
In his opinion, it was inevitable that his youngest son was extremely gifted. Once he entered the upper study room, he would definitely learn everything. He never considered the second possibility at all.
So Emperor Jingwen decided to take the cold approach. He wanted to see how the Duke of Zhen and the Imperial Concubine would react.
Anyway, the Duke of Zhen and the Imperial Concubine will always take action.
He could also take this opportunity to test how patient the Duke of Zhen was and whether he would really behave himself this time.
If the Duke of Zhen is particularly anxious, then……
And so, Emperor Jingwen waited and waited.
When Ye Shuo was three years old, Emperor Jingwen was sitting firmly on the Diaoyutai.
(T/L: Sitting firmly on the Diaoyutai = Sitting at ease in a fishing boat despite storms (idiom); to stay calm during tense situation
a cool head in a crisis)
When Ye Shuo was four years old, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but sigh that the Duke of Zhen and the Imperial Concubine were really patient.
When Ye Shuo was five years old, Emperor Jingwen began to frown.
When Ye Shuo was six years old, and it was time for school to start in the spring, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but walk around the Qinzheng Hall twice.
When Ye Shuo was seven years old, Emperor Jingwen would look outside from time to time while reviewing memorials.
Even the young eunuch beside him could clearly feel the emperor’s anxiety, not to mention Wang Ziquan who had followed Emperor Jingwen for so many years.
Wang Ziquan served carefully and prayed desperately in his heart, hoping that God would bless him and that it would succeed this year!
Soon, a figure walked in quickly.
The moment he saw that person, Emperor Jingwen put down the imperial pen in his hand.
“Your Majesty, I pay my respects to you. Your Majesty, please…”
“Alright, stop wasting time. Just tell me the result. Just tell me, has the Ninth Prince enrolled this year?”
Caught off guard, the young eunuch who came hurriedly had a frozen expression on his face, and then he reported the result of his investigation in a trembling voice: “Your Majesty… No, no!” After saying that, he didn’t even dare to look up.
The moment he finished speaking, Emperor Jingwen lost control and almost broke the armrest of the chair.
The Ninth Prince is already nine years old this year, what on earth do they want to do!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 38: Waiting
chapters.content:
The emperor thought about it over and over again, and felt that this would not work.
The emperor had originally planned very well, to see how the Duke of Zhen would react and then make a choice, but now…
Even someone as thoughtful as Emperor Jingwen could no longer sit still.
He realized that if he didn’t stop her, the Imperial Concubine would really keep dragging her feet and not allow the Ninth Prince to enroll in school!
But if he just moves like this, he would always feel like he is inexplicably inferior to the Duke of Zhen.
Emperor Jingwen sat on the dragon throne with an uncertain expression.
Wang Ziquan on the side was thinking, even though the little prince has grown up, the situation has not improved, but has become more serious. At the beginning, the little prince was just simply naughty, but now… His Majesty must be worried to death.
In the end, Emperor Jingwen still felt that compared to losing to the Duke of Zhen, it was more intolerable for the royal family, especially his own son, to have an illiterate person who could not read a single word. The former only made him feel uncomfortable, but the latter was a real harm.
Emperors are generally pragmatic, so Emperor Jingwen closed his eyes, gritted his teeth, and became extremely annoyed, almost yelling out word by word: “Come, prepare the carriage to the Qiuwu Palace!”
No matter what, the Ninth Prince must enroll in school this year!!!At the same time, over in the East Palace, Ye Shuo seemed to sense something and couldn’t help sneezing.
“A-choo!”
The noise startled the child next to Ye Shuo. After realizing what was happening, the child looked over at him worriedly, “Ninth Uncle, are you okay?”
“It’s okay, it’s okay. The ninth uncle is in good health.” Ye Shuo waved his hands, not caring at all. Now that he has already mastered the internal strength, ordinary minor illnesses like colds and fevers can no longer affect him.
Seeing the child in front of him so cute, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but rub his head, which naturally resulted in the child’s protest.
“Ninth Uncle!!!”
Looking at the child who couldn’t help but jump, Ye Shuo smiled and dodged, while his thoughts gradually drifted away.
From three to seven years old, there are still many changes in four years.
For example, he has successfully been listed in the imperial edict and officially obtained his own ranking.
As he grew older, the Sixth Prince felt a growing sense of urgency, especially since he would gradually begin to get involved in government affairs in two years. He was studying very hard, and except for the New Year holidays, he hardly had any time to stop.
Even though Ye Shuo lived with him in Qiuwu Palace, he often didn’t see him.
And on the prince’s side, Ye Shuo had just celebrated his third birthday. In the same year, the prince, who had just turned eighteen, got married. The woman he married was none other than the daughter of his teacher, the Grand Tutor.
Zhen is very different from her old-fashioned father. Zhen is very well-behaved and has a gentle and generous personality. Even when facing a naughty boy like Ye Shuo, she can be very patient and almost never loses her temper. Ye Shuo often comes to the East Palace and makes trouble there, but she never gets angry.
Ye Shuo observed carefully and confirmed that she was really not angry, and she was not saying one thing in front of others and another behind their backs.
According to the Crown Princess, she had never seen such a lively child before, and just watching him playing around made her feel more relaxed.
This is true. Ye Shuo is the most comfortable person in the whole palace.
Perhaps because she was too harshly disciplined since childhood, the Crown Princess was particularly envious of free children. Due to the rules, she could not run, jump or laugh, so she particularly liked to watch others run, jump and laugh, which almost pissed off the Grand Tutor.
At first Ye Shuo was still thinking that he must not act the same way as before after the Crown Prince got married. After all, disturbing the young couple would be struck by lightning. But seeing the Crown Princess’s behavior, Ye Shuo no longer had any scruples.
Not long after the Crown Prince and the Crown Princess got married, the Crown Princess became pregnant and gave birth to a child the following year. Now, four years have passed, and the child is three years old.
Look, that’s the kid next to Ye Shuo.
The little kid in front of him is the legitimate son of the crown prince. There is no one more legitimate than him.
Perhaps it was for the sake of the Grand Tutor, or perhaps it was because the Crown Prince and the Crown Princess knew each other when they were young and had a very close friendship, so there was almost no one else in the Crown Prince’s room before he married the Crown Princess, and no one was brought in for two years after he married her. Last year, he took in two new concubines.
Although Ye Shuo himself could not understand it, the world was in such a state today that the prince could not be blamed.
Ye Shuo was an outsider, so naturally he had no right to interfere in the prince’s family affairs, so he stopped paying attention to it.
Ye Shuo just has a good relationship with the little kid.
Because her husband was the crown prince, her son was destined from birth to never be able to do whatever he wanted in his life like ordinary children. The crown princess knew this clearly, so she wanted him to be happier when he was young.
In this palace, is there anyone who is more comfortable than the little prince back then, and now the ninth prince? Of course not.
So after her son was over one year old and could walk steadily, the Crown Princess began to allow the two to interact.
This method seemed to be very useful. Her son had already begun to show signs of maturity when he was one year old. he probably learned it from his father. A good child would eat and sleep according to the rules. This reminded the Crown Princess of her own childhood.
But after the Crown Princess handed her son over to the Ninth Prince, things gradually became different.
At first, the little prince was a little reserved and at a loss, but as he came into contact with more new things with his uncle, he gradually relaxed.
The little grandson of the emperor, Ye Xun, never knew before that mud could be so much fun.
There are also kites that can fly into the sky, peaches in spring, crickets in summer…even growing garlic is so interesting.
Ye Shuo gave almost all the fruits of his labor in the past few years to his adopted nephew, without any reservation.
He felt that it was pitiful for the child who was so excited even to see the hydroponic garlic sprouting.
Speaking of which, he seemed quite pitiful. How old was he now? He was only seven years old, and he was forced to help his brother take care of his children.
During this year or so, the little grandson of the emperor almost went crazy playing with him. Whenever the Grand Tutor heard about these things, he became so angry that he almost vomited blood.
If it weren’t for his status as a prince, Ye Shuo always felt that the Grand Tutor would definitely kill him personally for leading his grandson astray.
Look, in the main hall, the Grand Tutor and the Crown Princess started arguing again, and the content of the argument was nothing more than the same few sentences, that is, what the Grand Tutor thought the little emperor’s grandson looked like, and the Crown Princess, having seen a child like Ye Shuo, also wanted to make her son’s life easier when he was young.
Ye Shuo still clearly remembered the look of disbelief on the Grand Tutor’s face when the Crown Princess argued with her father for the first time in her life.
At first, the Crown Princess was a little nervous and afraid. After all, talking back to her father was considered a heinous crime. But after doing it many times, she gradually got used to it.
Anyway, no matter what, the period before her son arrives at the study is the Crown Princess’ bottom line.
“Nonsense, absolutely nonsense! I think you have lost your mind!” The Grand Tutor really couldn’t understand what kind of magic potion the Ninth Prince had fed his daughter. It had only been a short time, and the once gentle and quiet daughter dared to argue with her father.
Also, why hasn’t that damn Ninth Prince gone to school yet?!
The Grand Tutor has been looking forward to this for four years, and has been disappointed every year. Now he has become numb.
The key point is that because of his daughter, the Taifu can often see the Ninth Prince in the East Palace. He can’t avoid him even if he wants to. Every time he sees him, the Taifu can’t help but feel hurt internally.
How can there be such a kid in the world? !
Anyone who becomes this child’s teacher will be in dire straits for the rest of his life.
If one day the Ninth Prince finally leaves the Eastern Palace and goes to school in the study, the Grand Tutor will certainly ask the servants to go to the market to buy a set of 2,000-bang firecrackers and set them off to celebrate.
“The Crown Princess, can you please sober up a little?” The Taifu tried hard to suppress his rage and spoke earnestly.
The Crown Princess didn’t buy it, and just said calmly: “Father, don’t worry. I know what to do.”
Bullshit sense of propriety!
If she really had some sense, would she let his grandson hang out with the Ninth Prince? !
The Taifu was so angry that his head hurt. Seeing that he could not persuade him, he left in anger countless times.
As a result… as soon as he went out, he ran into the Ninth Prince who was bringing his grandson.
There were traces of mud on the little prince’s body, and his hands were not clean either. It was easy to guess what the two had just done.
The Grand Tutor was already extremely angry, and his eyes went dark when he saw this scene.
Ye Shuo touched his nose, pretending nothing happened, and took the initiative to greet him: “Hello, Master.”
“Ninth Prince, you must not do this. I am unworthy of this honor.” The Grand Tutor was so angry that he couldn’t vent his anger, and his tone was so depressed.
Ye Shuo was not angry, for fear of upsetting his cheap brother’s teacher, so he hurriedly pulled his cheap nephew away.
“Taifu, you are busy. I have something else to do, so I will leave first. Goodbye!”
The little grandson was still waiting to show his mother the fruits of his work this afternoon. Besides, he was always afraid of his grandfather, so he hurriedly left after saying “Hello, Grandpa. I’m going to see my mother first” and ran away quickly.
The figure of the Taifu was left behind, so desolate and miserable.
Because he heard the words “study in the upper study” from the quarrel between the Crown Princess and the Grand Tutor, Ye Xun’s mood inexplicably became low on the way, “Ninth Uncle, I heard from my mother that Xun’er will go to the upper study this year, and will not be able to play with you in the future.”
Ye Xun thought that the Ninth Uncle was really interesting, and he couldn’t bear to part with him.
“Don’t be sentimental yet. We don’t know how things will turn out. Maybe the Ninth Uncle will have to accompany you to the study this year.” Ye Shuo had a clear mind. He had been in this business for so many years. No matter what happened this year, he would not be able to get away with it.
“Ah? Really?” Ye Xun was stunned.
Ye Shuo was distracted: “Nine out of ten.”
It is not difficult to guess what my cheap dad is thinking. It is probably something like “I bet you will make a move, and when you make a move, I will be able to catch you.”
He has remained silent in the past few years, probably waiting for news from his grandfather.
It was because of this that Ye Shuo was able to waste four whole years.
After all, if his stepfather didn’t interfere, his mother’s side would be easy to deal with. Every time he went to school, Ye Shuo would be extremely anxious and unable to sleep all night long. He would lose a lot of weight in just a few days, and soon his mother would not be able to bear it anymore.
In this way, Ye Shuo relied on this method to drag it on year after year.
And now, four years have passed, and the stepfather must have figured out what’s going on. As an emperor who values ​​his reputation so much, how could he allow his son to be uneducated?
School would start in a few days. By then, his cheap father might already be waiting for him in Qiuwu Palace.
But…so what?
As long as no one was sent to urge him, he would pretend not to know.
Thinking of this, Ye Shuo felt relieved. With the idea of ​​being happy every day, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but pat his nephew on the head and said, “Let’s go. I’ll take you to see something good this afternoon.”
When Ye Xun heard this, his eyes suddenly lit up.
On the other hand, upon learning that his son had gone to the Eastern Palace to play again today, Emperor Jingwen just said “hmm” lightly and had no other expression.
It doesn’t matter, he has nothing to do today, just sit here and wait.
He wanted to see how crazy that little bastard could get and when he would come back!
Thus, the whole afternoon passed like this, and then it was dark, and finally Emperor Jingwen had finished his dinner and had almost digested it.
This wait lasted nearly four hours.
Emperor Jingwen: “…………”

chapters.title: Chapter 39: Reading
chapters.content:
When Emperor Jingwen came, he was already holding back a lot of anger. The reason why he didn’t send anyone to call the Ninth Prince over was to wait for him to come back and then give him a scare.
Emperor Jingwen had even imagined the scene of his son being terrified when he saw him.
At that time, if you ask him why he doesn’t go to school, the effect will definitely be doubled.
As a result…he never came back.
Then Emperor Jingwen became even angrier.
But it was his dark face that frightened the Sixth Prince who had just returned from the upper study.
Think about it, the Sixth Prince had been tired from studying all day, and he finally came back to relax for a while. However, when he looked up after entering the room, he was caught off guard by the majestic face of Emperor Jingwen, and all his sleepiness and fatigue were scared away.
“Greetings to the Emperor, may your Majesty be well.” The Sixth Prince knelt down hurriedly.
After seeing this scene, Emperor Jingwen felt relieved. In his opinion, this was normal.
This is exactly the effect that Emperor Jingwen wanted. Except for the wrong ‘object’, everything else was perfect.So Emperor Jingwen’s expression finally improved: “Get up, pack up, and prepare for dinner.”
“…yes.”
The Sixth Prince looked at the Imperial Concubine next to him. Judging from the Imperial Concubine’s expression and various signs, his father must have come to look for his Ninth Prince.
Although such scenes do not happen often, they do happen from time to time.
What the Sixth Prince didn’t understand was why his father would always be so angry at his little brother’s unintentional actions, and why he never got tired of it.
In this way, the silent atmosphere continued until the end of dinner.
It was already dark outside, but the Ninth Prince still hadn’t returned.
Noticing his father’s increasingly ugly expression, the Sixth Prince complained inwardly.
Damn it! Father looks very angry.
Just as the Sixth Prince began to pray for his brother, Emperor Jingwen finally couldn’t hold it anymore, and with a sullen face, he said to Wang Ziquan beside him: “Please, go and bring the Ninth Prince back to me.”
In the end, Emperor Jingwen compromised.
He finally realized that his son might not be able to come back today. If he didn’t see him, then his trip today would be in vain.
Hiss–
The emperor even used the word “please”, it seems that he is really angry.
Wang Ziquan did not dare to delay and hurriedly took the order to “capture” the ninth prince from the East Palace.
