She didn’t even know she was in school, she just thought she was getting revenge for her brother.
This has always been the method for educating children.
“This is the Three Character Classic. Come here, little princess, and follow me to read it. Man is born good…”
The little princess was ignorant: “When people are born, their nature is good…”
Taifu: “Nature is similar, but habits are different.”
Jianjian: “We are similar in nature, but different in habits.”
…
Both of them were reciting, and I guess there was nothing left for me to do.
Ye Shuo yawned, closed his eyes, lay on the table and started practising.
The same thought flashed through the minds of the Crown Prince and the Grand Tutor at the same time –
The ninth prince said he was looking for a teacher for the little princess. Was his purpose to divert attention?
I knew he was not so kind.
After counting the time, which was almost enough for a class, Ye Shuo woke up on time.
At that time, Jianjian was in high spirits and had already learned that “there are insects, fish, birds and beasts, and this animal can fly away.”
At first, the Grand Tutor was quite dissatisfied, but he found that teaching the little princess was much easier than teaching the ninth prince, even though she was only three years old.
But children also have their advantages. One of them is that they are very obedient, especially when facing teachers, they naturally have a sense of awe.
The most important thing is that the little princess is smart and able to learn, which makes the tutor, who has not taught students for a long time and only taught Ye Shuo, suddenly feel astonished.
The prince was also a little surprised. He vaguely remembered that his own son was just like this when he was just starting out.
Ye Shuo was even more generous, and he clapped non-stop beside him, with a look of amazement on his face: “Jian Jian is great! Jian Jian is amazing!”
The Grand Tutor couldn’t help but praise him as well: “She is much better than you.”
The little princess had never experienced the dangers of the world, and she soon lost herself in the praises, and her little face turned rosy.
Then…Ye Shuo immediately carried her out.
“Brother…?” Jianjian was puzzled. Didn’t he tell her to study?
“You have to study and play.” If a child is so young, she will get sick if she sits for a long time.
However, Ye Shuo’s action made the Taifu very angry.
He said he would teach, and he said he would play. This is simply too much!
“Even if you, the ninth prince, don’t learn, the little princess still has to learn!”
Hearing this, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but frown and looked down: “Jianjian, do you still want to continue learning?”
Jianjian didn’t know actually, she just simply felt happy when others praised her, so she nodded in confusion: “Yes, Jianjian wants to learn.”
“Then let’s do this.” Ye Shuo looked embarrassed: “How about we have a discussion?”
“As long as you can play for a quarter of an hour, I’ll let you go to school for half an hour. How about that?”
In Ye Shuo’s words, playing has become a burden, while studying has become a reward.
But it was true that because of what he had done before, in Jianjian’s eyes, wasn’t studying much easier than playing with him?
At least she didn’t have to run around with him, and she didn’t have to worry about him getting lost.
Jianjian nodded without hesitation: “Okay!”
Oh, children are so easy to deceive.
In this way, Ye Shuo forced Jian Jian to play hide-and-seek with him for half a day. Every time Jian Jian acted like a ghost, Ye Shuo would find her accurately, but when it was Ye Shuo’s turn to act like a ghost, Jian Jian just couldn’t find him no matter what.
This one-sided massacre is really not fun at all.
So as soon as Ye Shuo announced that the time was up, Jian Jian immediately ran back to the house without looking back.
Ye Shuo couldn’t help laughing, holding his stomach and bending over with laughter in the yard.
The other side.
The empress was also worried about her son’s studies, because the prince had a teacher specially appointed by Emperor Jingwen, and since they were both legitimate sons, they were naturally treated differently from his illegitimate brothers. Therefore, the empress was unwilling to accept this and also wanted to find a teacher to teach him individually.
As a result, before she found a solution, she heard that the Ninth Prince had brought the little princess directly to the Grand Tutor.

chapters.title: Chapter 123: Departure
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
In the past, the queen never took the little princess seriously.
In her opinion, how could a mere princess be as noble as a prince?
But the fact is that the little princess is treated much better than her little prince in every aspect.
This fact was hard for the queen to accept from the bottom of her heart.
What’s even more hateful is that this matter was instigated by the Ninth Prince.
He brought the little princess directly to the Grand Tutor and begged him to teach her to read. Most people would never do such a thing. Only the Ninth Prince, who was so thick-skinned, could do it.
But it was because of the Ninth Prince’s shamelessness that this thing actually happened. There is nothing more absurd and bizarre in the world than this.
After hearing this, how could the queen not feel upset?
But no matter how upset she was, she couldn’t use the same method to force the tutor to agree.Not to mention that the queen didn’t want to be associated with the prince’s teacher at all, it was not certain whether the other party could teach her son wholeheartedly. Even if the other party was willing to teach wholeheartedly, the queen couldn’t bring herself to ask him for help.
There are some things that are okay for children to do, but it would be inappropriate for adults to do them.
There was no other way, the Queen could only ask Emperor Jingwen to appoint a private tutor and ask her brother to report the Ninth Prince’s deed. As expected, the former was immediately rejected.
Emperor Jingwen really couldn’t understand. The little grandsons and the princes were all in the Shangshufang now. Look at it, except Xiaojiu, which prince didn’t come out of the Shangshufang? Lord Cen was not much worse than the Taifu. Why did the Queen have to be so eccentric?
It’s right for a mother to want the best for her child, but the more this is the case, the less likely it is that Emperor Jingwen will agree.
Emperor Jingwen didn’t want to give the Queen any hope. He didn’t understand why the Queen just couldn’t understand.
As for the latter, the King’s uncle reported Xiaojiu to the emperor, saying that the Ninth Prince acted absurdly and disregarded palace rules. Emperor Jingwen was so angry that he laughed.
The queen couldn’t even accommodate a princess, which made her seem even more stingy.
Being against the rules is one thing, and the queen’s insistence on holding on to it is another. The former is that Xiaojiu is being absurd, but it is not the first time that Xiaojiu has acted absurdly, and she is just a princess. Even Emperor Jingwen is willing to take good care of her before she gets married.
The latter is that the queen has lost her tolerance for others and has really gone backwards as she grows older.
Therefore, Emperor Jingwen first fined Xiaojiu half a year’s salary, and then scolded his uncle in the court.
The other ministers did not say anything either. They also felt that the princess was of no importance at all. Moreover, the emperor was particularly fond of the little princess. Minister He and others were too lazy to make the emperor unhappy because of this matter.
The civil officials did not say a word, not to mention the military generals. The Duke of Zhen took the lead and scolded the king’s uncle harshly. Naturally, the matter ended up in nothing.
After hearing this, the queen was so angry that her hands shook for a long time.
But there is no way, my son’s education is already imminent.
The little prince was weak, and he was already three and a half years old before he could finally talk and walk. This delay lasted a full six months. The queen saw it and was very worried.
If the emperor did not come forward, the teacher she or her uncle’s family could find would be worse than Lord Cen in the Upper Study.
In the end, the queen had no choice but to send her son to the study.
Sometimes the more people lack something, the more they want to show it. Now that the Empress is in decline and afraid of being laughed at, she pays more attention to pomp and circumstance.
On the day when the little prince was sent to the upper study, the queen arranged for four or five maids, eunuchs and tutors. The group was so grand that when the ceremonial procession passed by, all the palace servants gave way and saluted.
To show her importance, the Queen came personally to see him off, so there were even more personal palace maids around.
After all, it was the first day in the study, so the queen did not get up so early. When she appeared with the little prince, it was already bright.
The queen held her son’s hand and walked slowly along the path in the palace. She had a smile on her face and would lean over to give him a few words of advice from time to time. She looked like a real loving mother.
But the little prince was not moved at all, and even seemed to want to break free.
But how could the Queen, an adult, do as he wished? She immediately held her hand tighter.
The little prince’s expression was excited for a moment, but when he met the queen’s gaze, he shuddered suddenly and then immediately lowered his head.
The queen was satisfied, and her voice became softer: “When the time comes, my son will go to the upper study room, he must study hard and not disappoint his mother’s expectations.”
So far, the only thing that comforts the queen is that her son has a good brain. Although he is not talkative, he is very smart.
“You are the only hope for your mother in this life. You must perform well and strive to surpass everyone else. You are not in good health. Only if you study hard, your brothers won’t look down on you.”
The queen kept on giving instructions and didn’t notice the change in her son’s expression at all.
Just at this time, Ye Shuo also came to send his sister to school.
He said he was sending his sister away, but in fact it was Jianjian who was dragging him away.
Ye Shuo’s old habit of sleeping in the morning came back again, but this time it was not Emperor Jingwen or the guards who called him, but the little Princess Jianjian.
After all, the master said yesterday that we must arrive before the hour of Chen. In Jianjian’s opinion, since the master has already set the time, how can she be late?
“Jianjian, why don’t you go first and let your brother sleep a little longer.” Ye Shuo yawned and begged.
“No, Jianjian…supervise…my brother…” Jianjian was particularly stubborn about this matter.
Ye Shuo wanted to cry but had no tears, having completely forgotten that she was now at the age where she should take her teacher’s words as imperial decrees, and that the words of the Grand Tutor were even more effective than those of her stepfather.
The Grand Tutor casually asked her to supervise herself, and Jianjian really carried out her orders meticulously.
Ye Shuo was annoyed. What a mistake. What a mistake.
Just as the brother and sister were trying their best to pull and drag the baby, they happened to run into the Queen’s procession.
Ye Shuo was stunned at first, then he put away the playful smile on his face, and then pulled Jian Jian to salute: “Greetings to the Queen.”
What the queen was most impatient about now was seeing him, and the little princess secondly, so she didn’t stay for long at all. She coldly told the two of them to get up and leave with her people.
The Queen’s procession almost passed by Ye Shuo.
Ye Shuo once again saw the little prince whom he seldom met.
If he remembered correctly, the little prince should be three months older than Jianjian, but now, the little prince is more than half a head shorter than Jianjian.
Other aspects are even more incomparable.
Jianjian is white and plump, like a lucky doll, but the little prince is very thin, and his expression is dull, and he does not have the liveliness and cuteness of a child at all.
The little prince was surrounded by maids and eunuchs. The maids and eunuchs formed a wall and imprisoned the little prince firmly inside.
For some reason, this thought suddenly flashed through Ye Shuo’s mind.
Not sure if the little prince noticed Ye Shuo’s gaze or if the queen said something to him, but he turned his head for no reason.
Just as Ye Shuo was about to smile, Jian Jian had already subconsciously waved at him.
How could a child understand the complicated thoughts of adults? Jianjian was an extrovert by nature. Wouldn’t he be more enthusiastic when he saw his peers?
The little prince seemed to be startled and wanted to respond, but the queen pulled his arm hard. The little prince staggered and immediately couldn’t take care of this side.
“That’s the Ninth Prince and the Seventh Princess. Especially the Ninth Prince, Mother warns you that no matter what, you must not become a person like him in the future. Remember?”
“I remember.”
These two siblings, one is uneducated and the other breaks the rules. In short, neither of them is good. The imperial concubine is vulgar and unlettered, so she raised such children.
The queen was worried and couldn’t help but remind him again: “You are not allowed to get close to them or play with them in the future. Do you hear me?”
The little prince hesitated and did not dare to resist at all.
The other side.
Ye Shuo had long known that the King’s uncle had reported him, and he had roughly guessed who came up with the idea.
But what’s the use of this?
He is now just an oligarch prince. His cheap father can’t take away his prince status because of this matter, right?
Ye Shuo plans to participate in politics in the future. Whether he participates or not has no effect on him at all. As for the salary, to be honest, his mother gives him more pocket money every month.
Therefore, the King’s Uncle and the people behind him were completely wasting their time.
As for the reason why the other party did this, Ye Shuo almost knew it.
All I can say is that Ye Shuo would never stop sending Jianjian to school because of something like this, and it is even more impossible for him to give up his own life because of considering other people’s feelings.
People who are malicious towards him will be malicious towards him no matter what he does. The feelings of others are not within Ye Shuo’s consideration.
Soon, Ye Shuo and Jian Jian came to the East Palace together.
Having spent a long time in contact with the little princess recently, the Grand Tutor’s mood has become increasingly complicated. He has sighed in his heart for who knows how many times, wishing that the Ninth Prince could be swapped with the little princess. If only the Ninth Prince could be as smart and studious as the little princess.
Although the Grand Tutor did not say it directly, the look he gave the two of them was full of regret.
A princess will eventually get married, so no one would say anything even if she is not very well educated. It is such a waste of intelligence on a princess.
If it were an ordinary child, he would not take this matter to heart at all, but Jianjian was brought up by Ye Shuo himself after all, so she inexplicably began to feel unhappy about the attitude of the tutor.
Ye Shuo felt somewhat relieved when he saw this.
In Ye Shuo’s opinion, what others think of her is not important. What is important is Jianjian herself and how she sees herself.
Taifu had never read books like “Instructions for Women” and did not know how to teach girls. He taught Jianjian the same way the Taifu taught boys.
Women are no different from men if they learn the same things as men. Just wait and see the day when the cloth that is now covering women’s eyes in this world will no longer be able to hide their sharp eyes.
The so-called choice is not to go with the flow and finally get married when you are old enough. It is a choice to understand all the things and the truth and then decide to get married. It is completely different in nature.
So, we still have to find a way to make her study hard.
Ye Shuo touched his chin and came to this conclusion.
For some reason, the little princess with pointy hair, who was only three years old, suddenly felt a chill on her back.
Just when Ye Shuo was hesitating whether to teach Jian Jian martial arts, the Sixth Prince quietly celebrated his fifteenth birthday.
The Sixth Prince had finally reached the age to leave the Shangshufang, participate in state affairs, and build his own residence outside the palace.
And then there is…
The eldest prince is coming back.

chapters.title: Chapter 124: Gratitude
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
Because of the relationship with the Imperial Concubine, the Ministry of Internal Affairs had already started preparations for the Sixth Prince’s residence two years ago, and it has just been completed now.
Ten years have passed since the Sixth Prince was five years old. Even though the Imperial Concubine only treated him as a playmate for her son at the beginning and only wanted to raise him to be a helper for her son’s future, it was inevitable that she would develop feelings for him over time.
This is true even for kittens and puppies, let alone such a big person.
Although the Sixth Prince’s importance in the Imperial Concubine’s heart is far less than that of the brother and sister, Ye Shuo and Ye Zhenxi, he is not as insignificant as he was at the beginning.
Seeing her son like this now, the imperial concubine had no idea at all. It was obvious that her son was not that kind of material. It made no difference whether the Sixth Prince, the trained helper, was there or not.
Today was probably the Sixth Prince’s last day to spend the night in the palace. Even the Imperial Concubine couldn’t help feeling sad, so she asked the small kitchen to prepare a large table of dishes. The scene and scale were even grander than those of Ye Shuo and Jian Jian’s birthdays.
Emperor Jingwen originally had no plan to come. After all, in his view, it was not a big deal for his son to leave the palace and build a mansion. Every prince had gone through this. It proved that the prince had grown up. It was a happy event and a good thing.
Besides, even if he moved out of the palace and built his own residence, he still had to attend court every day. He could still be seen every day, so Emperor Jingwen felt that it had no impact at all.
But the imperial concubine didn’t think so. The child had grown up and was different after all, so she sent someone to invite him early in the morning.For the sake of the Imperial Concubine, Emperor Jingwen did not refuse and came over in the evening. During dinner, he drank two cups of wine with the Sixth Prince, which made the Sixth Prince so excited that he felt like he had picked up money.
No one can be a better father than this one.
After dinner, while Emperor Jingwen and his two children were outside digesting their food, the imperial concubine couldn’t help but wave to the Sixth Prince and called him to her side.
The Sixth Prince was only slightly tipsy to begin with. It was the first time that Emperor Jingwen drank with him. The Sixth Prince was so excited that it showed on his face, showing a bit of drunkenness. The Imperial Concubine called him over, and he sobered up immediately.
The Sixth Prince originally thought that the Imperial Concubine was instructing him to build up his own power in the court, and then fully support his Ninth Brother after he was able to attend court.
The Sixth Prince was not stupid, how could he not know why the Imperial Concubine picked him up? If it wasn’t for Xiao Jiu, why would the Imperial Concubine bother to raise someone else’s child?
From the very beginning it was nothing more than an exchange of interests, so the Sixth Prince was just a little sad, but not very heartbroken.
To be honest, the ten years he spent in Qiuwu Palace were the happiest and most comfortable ten years since the Sixth Prince was born. Just based on this, if the Imperial Concubine asked, the Sixth Prince would not refuse now.
What the Sixth Prince did not expect was that the Imperial Concubine did not give him instructions as he had expected, but instead asked Su Yue, who was beside her, to push a box in front of him.
Then, the imperial concubine spoke slowly: “Your mother has been gone since you were born. I have raised you in the palace since you were five years old. Now you have grown up. I know that your family is poor, unlike your other brothers who have their own mother to support them. Although I have some money, you are not my biological child after all. Most of my money will be spent on Shuo’er and Jianjian. Now I can only give you this much.”
The Imperial Concubine says whatever she wants. If he is not her biological son, then he is not her biological son. The Imperial Concubine will never be able to treat the Sixth Prince as her own son.
If he can accept it, then accept it; if he can’t, then just let it go.
“If you are interested in the future, please come to Qiuwu Palace to have a look. If you are not willing, I will not force you.”
“I can’t help you with anything else. Your future will depend on your own luck.”
The Sixth Prince was startled and looked up subconsciously. Then he saw that the box was filled with large-denomination silver notes such as one thousand taels and five hundred taels. There were at least a dozen or twenty of them, which was about twenty thousand taels.
The Sixth Prince had spent less than 200,000 taels of silver to build his mansion outside the palace. These 20,000 taels would be enough for him to spend for three to five years based on his current spending. After three to five years, the Sixth Prince would have established a firm foothold in the court, which would be just the right time for him to take over, and would be enough for him not to worry about money matters.
In order to pay less, the imperial concubine had someone specially calculate it.
“When the time comes, you can find a better housekeeper and ask him to set up a few shops for you in Shangjing City. Who knows, you can make money from this money. Anyway, you just need to be careful.” The imperial concubine gave a few casual instructions and didn’t seem to take it seriously.
The Sixth Prince knew the Imperial Concubine’s temperament. He knew that she was straightforward and would not think too much. Adding the slight insignificant feeling of alcohol, the Sixth Prince blurted out, “Concubine Rong!”
“Hmm?” The imperial concubine couldn’t help but look over.
The Sixth Prince hesitated for a moment, but finally he gritted his teeth and asked, “Madam Rong, there are still five years before Xiao Jiu goes to court. If you need anything, I can -“
“Forget it, just forget it.” I knew what he wanted to say, but I felt bad when he mentioned this.
There is hardly a parent in the world who does not hope that their children will become successful. The imperial concubine also wants her son and daughter to be successful, but the key is that she really does not have the ability to do so.
People only accept their fate when they feel there is really no hope. As long as there is even a little hope, they will never accept their fate.
Isn’t it just irrelevant for the Sixth Prince to bring up things that are not relevant?
When she thought of this, the imperial concubine’s mood became particularly bad, and her tone became not so good: “You should take care of yourself first!”
After she finished speaking, the imperial concubine did not notice the change in the Sixth Prince’s eyes.
The haze in his heart gradually dissipated, and finally, the Sixth Prince knelt down and kowtowed three times to the imperial concubine.
“Thank you, Madam Rong.”
On the other side, in the yard——
When Emperor Jingwen heard that his son wanted to teach his daughter martial arts, his first reaction was to oppose.
“I won’t allow it!”
Emperor Jingwen knew his son’s unique skills. When he thought about his son teaching his daughter such despicable tricks, he couldn’t help but raise his voice.
Due to physiological limitations, women are inherently weaker than men. Unless they are gifted, women will always be at a disadvantage in a fist-to-palm fight.
Therefore, practising more dirty tricks is the best choice. Ye Shuo really couldn’t understand why his cheap father was so strongly opposed.
Nonsense, all his tricks are aimed at hurting people. How can a girl do this? My daughter is a precious little princess. It is really inappropriate to let a princess do such a thing.
Besides, the princess is always surrounded by people when she travels, so he wouldn’t have to worry about Jianjian being bullied, and his little hands would become rough from practice.
Seeing that Xiaojiu was still eager to try, Emperor Jingwen took his ignorant daughter away without saying anything, and kept warning her: “I don’t care what happens to you, but you can’t lead Jianjian astray.”
“If you really want Jianjian to learn martial arts, I will find a martial arts master to teach her someday.”
Xiaojiu wanted to do it himself? Emperor Jingwen sneered, no way!
When it comes to this matter, Emperor Jingwen can be said to be endless, and he talks much more than before.
“And look at you, you’ve made Jianjian suffer so much.” She’s learning calligraphy and now martial arts, and her schedule is even busier than that of a prince, so why doesn’t he stop doing this to her?
“Jianjian is just a princess. She will have me and her brothers to protect her in the future.”
Well, this is another person who thinks it’s useless for the princess to study and practise martial arts.
Everyone here thinks so. Influenced by everything, the princess naturally cannot escape from such an environment. When she wakes up one day, it is already too late.
Before Ye Shuo could open his mouth to refute, Jian Jian started shaking her head.
“No, no, I don’t mind the trouble. I want to learn…”
“Practising martial arts… looks great!”
Jianjian witnessed with her own eyes the scene of two guards fighting in the palace’s martial arts field. Each of them held a long sword and stood facing each other. The atmosphere was murderous and in an instant, sand and rocks flew everywhere, making the onlookers dizzy.
Even though Jianjian was still young, she couldn’t help but feel her blood boiling when she saw that scene.
The fight between the two guards happened ten days ago. Perhaps the impression was too deep that Jianjian has been thinking about it until now. The look of longing on her face was beyond words.
Jianjian couldn’t help but demonstrate it to Emperor Jingwen in his arms.
However, what Jianjian didn’t know was that Ye Shuo deliberately let her see that scene, and the two guards were also specially arranged by Ye Shuo.
It doesn’t matter whether the weapon has high lethality or not. What matters is that it must be cool enough, handsome enough, and able to scare the little girl.
Jianjian is naive and could be deceived by him, but Emperor Jingwen is an adult and the emperor. How could he not know the tricks here?
He uses the same trick every time. He is really good at deceiving his own sister.
However, Ye Shuo not only did not feel ashamed, but instead looked righteous.
When Emperor Jingwen saw this, the veins on his forehead twitched. Just when Emperor Jingwen was about to curse, the Sixth Prince finally walked out of the room.
Although the Sixth Prince had never been listed in the Imperial Concubine’s imperial edict, after all, the Imperial Concubine had raised him for so many years. Before the Sixth Prince left the palace, the Imperial Concubine naturally had something to tell him, but Emperor Jingwen did not ask in detail.
As for Ye Shuo, a little kid who depended on his mother for support and cheated his sister for her New Year’s money, he couldn’t afford to give a very expensive gift, so he could only start with the gift of thought.
“This is the most complete version of the Five Animals Exercises that I specifically requested from the old doctor. You must remember to practise it more often in the future.”
“There are also these medicinal pillows and waist pillows. They are filled with medicinal herbs such as Ziziphus jujuba seeds, Salvia miltiorrhiza, and Astragalus. They are very helpful for your sleep. Remember to use them when you sleep.”
The Sixth Prince had not read many medical books, but he knew that Chinese jujube seeds and other foods were used to treat blood deficiency.
That is to say, even at this time, Xiaojiu was still saying that he was weak.
But despite this, the Sixth Prince couldn’t help but feel a little moved: “This pillow… did you sew it yourself?”
“Yes.” Ye Shuo nodded without hesitation.
“I personally gave the order to have Su Yue and the others sew it.”
The Sixth Prince: “…”
After all the talk, he just opened his mouth.
The Sixth Prince sighed and told himself to be content and not to demand too much from Xiaojiu.
To be honest, this pillow is really good. The faint medicinal fragrance does make it easier for him to fall asleep than before.
However, the Sixth Prince’s emotion did not last long. The next morning, when he was about to leave, Ye Shuo came out wrapped in a cloak.
“Why are you wrapped up so tightly in the hot summer?”
Taking a closer look, the Sixth Prince discovered that he was only wearing an undergarment underneath, and without the cloak, everything was exposed.
Underwear is equivalent to modern pajamas. Ye Shuo was too lazy to change clothes. He was still waiting to send the Sixth Prince away and then go back to take a nap.
When their eyes met, Ye Shuo’s expression looked extremely innocent.
“Why……”
The Sixth Prince only felt a sense of reality now. After he left, there was no one he could trust in the entire Qiuwu Palace.
The most reliable one left was Jianjian, who was only three years old.
The Sixth Prince sighed, patted his brother’s shoulder, squatted down, and said to the little princess with a look of pity: “When Sixth Brother is gone, the Qiuwu Palace will all depend on you.”
“If there is anything, remember to ask someone to tell Sixth Brother.”
Jian Jian couldn’t help it and immediately straightened her chest: “Sixth brother…don’t worry!”
Don’t worry, don’t worry.
Looking at Ye Shuo who was standing aside, still yawning and careless, when he looked over, he still looked puzzled and confused, and grinned at him. Finally, the Sixth Prince dragged his steps that suddenly became heavy, and slowly left the Qiuwu Palace where he had lived for ten years.
Ye Shuo was still holding his cloak and waving: “Goodbye, Xiao Ming. When you have time in the future, remember to come home often~”

chapters.title: Chapter 125: Welcoming
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
The Sixth Prince thought that he would be much more comfortable after he established his own residence outside the palace, but in fact it seemed that he did not feel that way.
On the contrary, because he has not yet been engaged, there are very few people in the prince’s mansion, so he seems even more lonely and deserted.
The Sixth Prince used to think that his Ninth Brother was noisy and never had a moment of rest. He was always causing trouble or something else, and the entire Qiuwu Palace was always in a state of chaos.
The Sixth Prince used to be impatient, always thinking that everything would be fine once he got out, and that he wouldn’t have to endure all this once he got out.
Now that he had really come out, the Sixth Prince felt deserted instead.
Think about it, I really am…
The Sixth Prince couldn’t help but laugh.
But the Sixth Prince was the Sixth Prince after all, and he did not allow this weak mood to last long. Or rather, he just took a nap, and by the time he went to court on the first day, he had returned to normal.
Everyone else has a mother, but he doesn’t, so there will always be no one behind him.There may be people like Xiaojiu and Guifei appearing in the middle, but in the end, it will not last long.
The imperial concubine has Xiaojiu as her son, and no matter what, I will never become her son.
Xiaojiu, the little princess, and the imperial concubine, the three of them are a family. The Sixth Prince felt that he must be strong so that he could walk the next path without fear.
And now that he has finally come into contact with court affairs, a new journey has slowly come into view.
Although Emperor Jingwen had a mediocre feeling towards this son, he also knew that the Sixth Prince was outstanding, so Emperor Jingwen did not treat him unfairly in this regard. As soon as he entered the court, Emperor Jingwen directly let him take the assignment of the Ministry of Personnel.
The Ministry of Personnel was in charge of the appointment, dismissal, imperial examinations, promotion, demotion, transfer, honors, etc. of all civil officials in the Zhou Dynasty, and its responsibilities were quite heavy.
Although Emperor Jingwen only asked him to participate instead of being in charge, it was also a sign of his great importance.
As the saying goes, hard work pays off. Emperor Jingwen naturally noticed the efforts of the Sixth Prince.
The Sixth Prince was extremely ambitious, but he also knew that this matter could not be rushed, so after entering the Ministry of Personnel, he did not rush to show his abilities. Instead, after he had figured out the operating rules of the Ministry of Personnel, he gradually began to relax.
Emperor Jingwen saw all of this and felt very satisfied.
It can be said that over the years, the imperial concubine only provided the Sixth Prince with basic things such as food and drink, and the rest depended entirely on the Sixth Prince’s own efforts.
Not long after, Ye Shuo received the news that the Sixth Prince was doing very well in the Ministry of Personnel following the Fourth Prince.
As expected, this guy has been dishonest since he was a child, and he is indeed suitable for a place like officialdom.
Look, it hasn’t been long since then and he’s already been able to get the hang of it smoothly. It’s hard to deny his talent.
Ye Shuo sighed in his heart, but soon he got back into the game with Jian Jian.
Of course, this time it was not hide-and-seek. Jianjian would never play hide-and-seek with him. This time it was shuttlecock kicking, to see who could kick the most.
The shuttlecock is made of copper coins and chicken feathers, especially the tail feathers from the back of a rooster. It is so beautiful.
But the ending was not unexpected and was no better than hide-and-seek.
How could Jianjian, a kid, have the speed to react to Ye Shuo’s?
After a while, she was so angry that she started to howl.
Looking from the house into the yard, the prince couldn’t help but laugh: “After so many years, Xiaojiu still has the mentality of a child.”
In the past, he bullied his son, but now that Xiaojiu has a younger sister, he has started bullying his own sister.
It cannot be said that it has grown, it can only be said that it has become worse and more excessive.
“Who said it wasn’t?” The Taifu was also convinced. He had seen naughty children, but this was the only one who was naughty and made no progress.
It seems like the Ninth Prince’s character is ingrained in his bones, and he probably won’t be able to change it in this lifetime.
Now, the Grand Tutor depends on the steady little princess to keep him alive. The existence of the little princess makes the Grand Tutor no longer doubt whether his level is enough to become a teacher.
At first, the Grand Tutor was not very willing to teach the little princess, but now that the Ninth Prince is here to take care of the little princess, the Grand Tutor feels at ease.
At least there is someone who is willing to learn, proving that I am not talking to a cow.
Seeing that the Grand Tutor had endless things to say when he mentioned Xiaojiu, the Prince hesitated to speak. In fact, this was not what he wanted to say.
The Grand Tutor then realised that now was not the time to talk about this.
The Master even recovered from his complaining state.
“Your Highness, I heard that the eldest prince will be back soon?”
“Yes.” The prince’s information is more accurate than that of the tutor.
“It will arrive in ten days at the latest.”
The eldest prince informed his father of the news two months ago, and his father agreed.
Of course, the prince was not concerned about these things. Instead, the reason why the eldest prince came back was because he won the battle with Beiting…
Not only did they win, but they won a complete victory. There has been very little record of this since the founding of the Great Zhou Dynasty. Even when the Duke of Zhen led the troops, there were only one or two such times.
The people of Beiting have always been tough, so winning is extremely difficult. When the previous emperor was in power, the Great Zhou even lost seven cities in a row and finally took them back with great difficulty.
The eldest prince’s move really dealt a heavy blow to Beiting’s fighting spirit and suppressed its arrogance.
From the perspective of the country, the prince is naturally happy, but from a personal perspective, it is naturally very bad.
As the eldest prince, he was not very convinced of his own status as the crown prince. Back then, his mother was just an insignificant concubine, while his mother was the crown princess. Naturally, the eldest prince did not dare to say what was in his mind directly at that time.
But now, his mother has passed away for many years, and the eldest prince’s biological mother is already Concubine De, one of the three concubines. The eldest prince is also the eldest, so how can the prince not worry?
What’s more, the eldest prince returned with military merits this time. With his achievements, even his father would have to praise him highly.
As the saying goes, the west wind prevails over the east wind. If the eldest prince gains power, his brilliance as the crown prince will inevitably be overshadowed. There is nothing that can be done about it.
“Now I am just worried whether these days will ever end.” The prince smiled bitterly.
I have lived peacefully in Shangjing City for so many years, and now it is finally time to repay my debts.
“At this point, this is all we can do.” The Grand Tutor couldn’t help but sigh, “With the defeat of Beiting, the rise of the eldest prince is unstoppable. Your Highness, please be patient for a while.”
If the prince steps out at this time, it will only do harm and no good.
“Your Highness, please relax. As long as the emperor does not change his mind, your position will not be shaken by anyone.”
The issue of the crown prince is related to the foundation of the country. The crown prince has long passed the most difficult period and has now established a firm foothold. This cannot be easily changed, so the current tutor is not actually that worried.
After all, no matter how great the achievements are, they are not as important as the emperor’s intentions.
The prince was silent for a moment, then slowly said, “I hope so.”
I just don’t know how long the happy days in the East Palace can last.
Listening to the sounds of Xiaojiu and the little princess playing and fighting in the yard outside, the prince couldn’t help but show envy in his eyes, and then sighed: “It’s better to be a child…” But at this time, he would never let anything go.
The Grand Tutor remained silent.
Ten days passed in a flash, and early in the morning Ye Shuo was woken up by Xiao Luzi and Xing Yucheng.
“Oh, Your Highness, why are you still sleeping? The eldest prince is about to take his men back to the capital!” After three days of rest, the army led by the eldest prince has reached the time to enter the city.
No matter what, the Ninth Prince must not be late this time.
Ye Shuo was still very sensible about this matter. This time, Ye Shuo did not let Xiao Luzi and Xing Yucheng wait too long and quickly got out of bed.
Xiao Luzi was stunned for a moment, wondering why the Ninth Prince got up so early today.
If Ye Shuo knew what Xiao Luzi was thinking, he would definitely say something. Of course, because of this matter, he went to bed much earlier than usual last night.
After washing up, Ye Shuo changed his clothes and opened the door.
It was only at this time that Ye Shuo noticed that today’s weather didn’t seem to be particularly good.
It was indeed inconvenient in ancient times because there was no weather forecast. For such a big event, it was necessary to choose a sunny day. But unfortunately, the matter had already been decided and could not be easily changed.
As long as it doesn’t rain, it doesn’t matter if the sky is a little cloudy.
Ye Shuo was eating breakfast when he noticed that Xiao Jianjian came running over to him without him noticing.
Ye Shuo originally wanted to go find her specifically, but now it seems that there is no need.
Without waiting for Jian Jian’s response, Ye Shuo quickly said, “Eat quickly. I’ll take you to see the big scene later.”
After saying that, Ye Shuo stuffed the bean bun into the little princess’s hand without saying anything.
The imperial concubine who followed closely behind could not help but be stunned when she heard this: “Why did you take Jianjian to do something like this?”
Ye Shuo didn’t even think twice: “The army is entering the city. It’s a rare sight. It would be a pity not to bring Jian Jian to see it.”
Imperial Concubine: “…”
There would be people everywhere, so what was so interesting about it? Was he just taking it as a normal trip?
But Jianjian didn’t care about that. When she heard about going outside the palace, it was quite attractive for a child, so she subconsciously started to eat the bean bun in her hand.
By the time Ye Shuo finished eating, Jian Jian was almost done.
He wiped her paws with a handkerchief, and then Ye Shuo threw Jian Jian onto his back. Before Jian Jian could even react, he said, “It’s too late. Hold on tight. I won’t be responsible if you fall.”
Jianjian subconsciously hugged his neck.
The child was too honest, and Ye Shuo almost rolled his eyes.
Just like that, the imperial concubine had no time to stop it at all. She could only watch her son running away with her daughter on his back, and soon they disappeared.
Looking at Xiao Luzi and Xing Yucheng who were desperately chasing after them, the imperial concubine couldn’t come back to her senses for a long time.
At the same time, on the other side——
The fact that the eldest prince had defeated Beiting made Emperor Jingwen very happy. Even though he had known about it several months ago, he was still very happy that the eldest prince had returned to the court.
To show his importance, he notified all the princes and Prime Minister He and others, and prepared to go to the city wall of Shangjing City to welcome him in person.
As for the infighting among the princes, it has now spread to the smallest details.
Ye Shuo thought that he was already very early as he arrived a quarter of an hour early, but in fact the Second Prince and his companions had already arrived half an hour ago, so compared to them, Ye Shuo was once again very gloriously… late.
Just when Emperor Jingwen thought that the little bastard would not be able to get out of bed today, and just when Emperor Jingwen could not help frowning, he saw something in the distance running towards him at an extremely fast speed and in an unruly manner.
This figure…
Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help it and the corners of his mouth twitched slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 126: Human Nature
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
‘What is that?’
The Second Prince stared blankly, trying hard to identify it.
Looking at the Fifth Prince and the Sixth Prince next to them, they already looked like they were in a state of great headache but were not surprised at all.
Being brothers with this guy is really embarrassing… The Fifth Prince gritted his teeth secretly.
Emperor Jingwen was in a very complicated mood at this time, feeling both relieved and angry.
The good news is that he didn’t go too far and stayed in bed until his elder brother came back. The bad news is that even though he came, he still caused a lot of trouble.
After Ye Shuo ran all the way, Jian Jian on his back almost vomited. Now her eyes were full of tears and she looked like she wanted to vomit but couldn’t. She looked so miserable.
The moment he saw Jianjian, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but take a deep breath: “Why did you bring Jianjian here?”
“Your Majesty, we’re here to welcome my eldest brother back to the palace.” Ye Shuo said as if it was a matter of course.So…did he think that this family was going to go out for fun? ? ?
Emperor Jingwen originally wanted to scold him, but after Wang Ziquan reminded him that there was not much time left before departure, Emperor Jingwen reluctantly endured it.
Forget it, forget it, he has already brought her here, and it’s too late to send the little princess back now.
“…Hurry up and join the team!”
As expected of the Ninth Prince, he is still being scolded at this time.
Upon seeing this, all the ministers could not help but shake their heads.
Ye Shuo didn’t feel ashamed at all. He brought Jian Jian to the side of the Sixth Prince. On the way, he asked about the Sixth Prince’s recent situation: “How do you feel after building your own palace?”
At this hour, Xiaojiu is still chatting…
The Sixth Prince curled his lips and said, “It’s OK.”
Seeing that he was about to speak again, the Sixth Prince quickly said, “Don’t talk anymore. Get ready to get on the carriage. We are about to leave the city.”
Seeing the carriage coming in front of him, Ye Shuo had to shut his mouth.
The Sixth Prince breathed a sigh of relief.
In this way, the group of people arrived at the gate of Shangjing City in a mighty manner.
Probably because they had also received the news of the Great Zhou’s victory, the people around were jubilant and the entire Shangjing City was filled with joy and peace.
Ye Shuo couldn’t help but sneak a peek at the prince next to his adoptive father, only to find that the prince had a smile on his lips, looking as if he was also happy about this.
From time to time, he would even praise his adoptive father, showing the wise and generous image of the crown prince.
Ye Shuo was stunned for a moment, then sighed.
“Brother…?” Including the Sixth Prince, everyone’s attention was not here at this moment. Only the little Princess Jianjian noticed that something was wrong with her brother.
Seeing Jianjian looking up at him, Ye Shuo shook his head gently: “Nothing.”
“I just feel that… the wind is getting stronger right now. I wonder if it will rain later.”
For some reason, Jianjian suddenly felt that her brother standing on the city wall at this moment was particularly gloomy, with a solemn look between his brows, totally different from his usual smiling face.
However, it was only a brief moment, and when Jianjian blinked, she looked carefully and found that her brother was still the same brother, except that the words “not doing his job properly” were almost written on his face.
The pointed and tender little face suddenly fell.
Since they were welcoming the victorious soldiers back, the Queen, as the mother of the country, was naturally there as well. Not only was the Queen there, she even brought the little prince with her.
The queen held the little prince’s hand and never let go for a moment.
“You must take a good look at what the eldest prince looks like today.” Pretending to straighten the little prince’s clothes, the queen said softly.
She wanted to let her son see how high-spirited and energetic his elder brother is now.
Almost as soon as the words fell, the little prince suddenly became nervous.
Not to mention the Queen, even the Second Prince and the others couldn’t help but feel nervous.
On the city wall, the people looked all different, and Ye Shuo felt tired just by looking at them.
Just when Ye Shuo was feeling bored, he suddenly felt the city wall under his feet shaking slightly. Listening carefully, he could hear the sound of galloping horses in the distance, like fine drum beats, becoming closer and clearer.
Ye Shuo was startled, then suddenly looked up.
I saw the small black dots that were the size of ants just now gradually enlarged, and one by one, their figures gradually appeared.
When they were about two or three miles away from Shangjing City, the eldest prince made a gesture and all the soldiers stopped.
Looking at the towering Shangjing City in the distance, a complex look flashed across the eldest prince’s eyes.
After ten years of hardships at the border, I finally returned here alive.
I just wonder if my brothers are living a comfortable life in the capital?
“Go!” Quickly restraining the various emotions in his eyes, the eldest prince gently patted his beloved warhorse.
The warhorse had followed the eldest prince for several years and was naturally familiar with every command of the eldest prince. It quickly changed from its previous wild galloping state to slowly walking forward.
The road of more than two miles was neither long nor short. It took no more than a quarter of an hour for the large army to appear in front of them.
Ye Shuo had excellent eyesight and immediately saw the man at the front of the team.
The man was tall and strong, with deep facial features. Perhaps due to years of fighting, he exuded a murderous aura that was intimidating without even getting angry. Compared to him, the other princes, including the crown prince, were like flowers in a greenhouse.
The prince’s hands tightened for a moment, but soon relaxed again before anyone else noticed.
Ye Shuo was ready to watch it a few more times. It was a live version of the ancient military parade. The scene was indeed spectacular enough and rare to see in many years. But after a while, he saw Jianjian below desperately pulling at his sleeves.
“Brother, brother…I want to see…I want to see…”
It turned out that Jianjian was young and short, and couldn’t see what was happening below at all.
Ye Shuo didn’t think much about it. He just picked up Jian Jian and put her on the top of the city wall.
Jianjian still didn’t know what fear was. She was so brave that even Ye Shuo had to admit defeat. So she was not afraid and looked over with curiosity in her eyes.
Wherever the main force below went, the two scorching gazes followed.
The eldest prince, who was leading the group, raised his head sharply, and then he saw two figures moving along with his movements. They were completely fake and completely different from the others. The amazement in his eyes was almost overflowing.
They are exactly the same as the common people they met along the way.
When he reached the bottom of the city wall, the two children bent their bodies lower and lower, and finally they were lying on the wall to watch.
Ye Shuo couldn’t help but touch his chin: “So impressive…”
Jianjian nodded repeatedly: “That’s right!”
The eldest prince: “…”
Looking at their ages, the eldest prince almost instantly figured out the identities of the two people, the adult and the child.
Everyone in the palace said that the Ninth Prince acted arbitrarily, and it turned out to be true.
Not long after, the eldest prince came before Emperor Jingwen.
The first moment he saw Emperor Jingwen, the eldest prince knelt down and said, “Your Highness, I pay my respects to you, father. Long live your Highness.”
He was only seventeen years old when he left the palace. Now, ten years have passed and he is already twenty-seven years old. Thinking of this, even the eldest prince couldn’t help but feel excited.
Therefore, when he met Emperor Jingwen, he inevitably leaked some information.
“Father, I have accomplished my mission and brought back the head of General Beiting Lanruo to present to you.”
As soon as he finished speaking, the person behind the eldest prince walked out in time, holding a wooden box in his hand.
Almost at the moment he saw the wooden box, Ye Shuo covered Jianjian’s eyes in time and refused to let go no matter how Jianjian struggled.
It is right to exercise children, but this does not include letting them look at human heads. If this is not done properly, it may leave a lifelong psychological trauma on them.
Even if there is blood involved, we have to wait until the child grows up a little.
But Ye Shuo’s behaviour doesn’t necessarily mean the Queen will be the same.
The empress was standing next to Emperor Jingwen and was quite close to him. The moment the little prince saw the box, he instinctively wanted to close his eyes. However, the empress pinched his palm hard, and the little prince couldn’t help but scream in pain.
Almost at the same time, the wooden box opened, and the man’s head inside was wide-eyed and full of murderous intent.
Caught off guard, the little prince screamed subconsciously.
The so-called legitimate son of the Empress Central Palace is just like this, not even half as good as the son of the previous Empress.
The eldest prince glanced at the younger prince, and seeing his reaction, he didn’t take him seriously at all, and quickly looked at the crown prince.
Seeing that the prince’s expression did not change, he was actually a little surprised. He clapped his hands and praised: “It really is General Lanruo’s head. Big brother is really brave!”
The prince was as flawless as ever.
This guy has been acting like this since he was a child. He is so boring.
The eldest prince’s interest suddenly dropped by half, but looking at the reactions of his other brothers, especially the second prince who was only good at literature and not martial arts, his face turned slightly pale, and the fourth prince and others were not much better. As for the rumoured ninth prince, he looked up at the sky and the earth, and refused to look at the wooden box no matter what.
The eldest prince couldn’t help but sneer in his heart when he saw this.
What a bunch of wimps!
Although the eldest prince’s ridicule was not only directed at the younger prince, but more at his other grown-up brothers, the queen didn’t think so in her heart.
Catching a glimpse of the contempt in the eldest prince’s eyes, the queen couldn’t help feeling humiliated.
Especially her own son’s scream made the queen even more embarrassed.
The little prince seemed to sense something vaguely, and couldn’t help but tremble even more violently.
Emperor Jingwen, on the other hand, was surprised at first, but after he recognized the face, he was overjoyed.
Lanruo….Lanruo, this name sounds gentle and amiable, but in fact, who in the Three Kingdoms does not know this General Lanruo?
How could Emperor Jingwen not be happy when such a powerful general of Beiting was killed by his own son?
“Good! Good! Good!” Emperor Jingwen said three good words in a row, which made everyone present excited.
The eldest prince felt relieved upon seeing this, and he obviously realised that the hardships he had endured for the past ten years were not in vain.
Ye Shuo stood at almost the farthest position, watching everything from afar. He knew in his heart that at this point, the conflict between the eldest prince and the crown prince was inevitable.
The previous emperor was incompetent and wars were frequent during his reign, so in the end there were no more titles to be given and he allowed my grandfather’s family to become more powerful.
When my cheap dad ascended the throne, over 70% of the military generals were direct descendants of my grandfather. My grandfather’s power was deeply rooted and intertwined. My cheap dad felt that his throne was unstable, but he was unable to interfere in military affairs for a while.
It is difficult to convince ordinary people to be in this position. Without a foundation and achievements, how can the generals in the army recognize them? In the end, no matter how hard they try, they are just a decoration and will never have access to real power.
Therefore, the person chosen by the cheap father must be important enough.
And in this world, is there anyone more important than the Dragon Prince? The generals may not listen to ordinary people, but they must listen to the prince, right?
At that time, all the princes were still young, the position of the crown prince could not be moved, and the second prince was weak, so Emperor Jingwen could only let the eldest prince, who was only seventeen years old, take on all the responsibility.
The eldest prince takes the lead, and the people arranged by Emperor Jingwen can gradually grow under the wings of the eldest prince.
Now, ten years have passed, and the family of the Duke of Zhen is finally no longer a major concern for Emperor Jingwen.
All the chaos had been sown as early as the time of the previous emperor, but it is only now gradually emerging.
Ye Shuo asked himself, if he were the eldest prince, would he be willing to accept this?
He worked so hard to support the country, but his younger brothers were eating, drinking, and having fun under his wings, enjoying all the wealth and luxury in the world. No one would be willing to do this.
And what about the crown prince? His position as the heir to the throne was decided when he was ten years old, and there was no turning back for him.
As for the Second Prince, the Fourth Prince, the Fifth Prince, and the Sixth Prince… perhaps they do not have that thought at the moment, but as the fight between the Crown Prince and the Eldest Prince intensifies, they will gradually develop that thought.
Although everyone was so happy at the moment, in Ye Shuo’s eyes, it seemed like a storm was about to come.
Human nature is like this, and it is beyond human power. As long as human nature is not destroyed, disputes will not end.
This is what is called the pain of wakefulness.

chapters.title: Chapter 127: Big Events
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
Although he knew when he came to this world that this day would come sooner or later, when this day really came, Ye Shuo still found it difficult to accept it.
In fact, Ye Shuo has tried his best to avoid dealing with his brothers over the years. He has also reminded himself not to invest too much emotion in them.
It’s just that emotions are something that cannot be controlled by humans. Over time, they will appear more or less.
Ye Shuo is a human, not a god. He simply cannot regard these living people as NPCs in the game. NPCs can come back to life after death, but they are just a piece of data. If they die, they are really dead and will never come back.
Especially the prince, who once saved Ye Shuo’s life by accident. If the prince’s attendant had not happened to come by, causing the midwife’s hand to tremble, he would have been dead by now.
Of all people, what Ye Shuo least wanted to see was something happening to the Crown Prince.
But now that the eldest prince is back, the possibility of nothing happening to the crown prince is extremely low.
Ye Shuo knew very well that once a person reached that point, he would feel helpless. Even if the prince did not want to fight, reality would force him to do so.
The eldest prince has made great contributions and is very popular for a while. If you want to compete with him, you will definitely need more followers.How can the party develop? Don’t even think about it if there is no sufficient benefit.
If the prince’s position is stable, he will naturally attract a large number of followers, but if his position is unstable, what can he rely on?
At this point, Ye Shuo’s only hope is that the prince must not go astray.
My stepfather is no pushover, and neither are my group of fierce and ferocious brothers.
If the prince showed any weakness, he would be attacked and eaten by everyone.
The so-called crooked path is bound to be a dead end.
As for asking the eldest prince to give up voluntarily? If you put yourself in his shoes, it’s impossible.
Otherwise, why would the eldest prince risk his life and stay at the border for ten years?
Sometimes people just can’t see things too clearly. If they see too clearly but are powerless to do anything about it, all that will result is endless torture.
Ye Shuo subconsciously closed his eyes. He had never hated his own intelligence so much. It made him unable to harbour any hope of luck.
“elder brother……”
I don’t know if it was telepathy, but when Jianjian looked up, she was immediately frightened by her brother’s pale face.
“Brother, what’s wrong with you?”
Although Jianjian usually disliked him, she was still very nervous when she saw him like this, and even spoke in a much softer voice.
Seeing that he seemed to have frightened her, Ye Shuo was startled, then shook his head: “Nothing, I was just frightened by General Lan Ruo’s head just now.”
“Is it really scary?” Jianjian was originally unhappy that he suddenly blindfolded her, causing her to not see anything. Now seeing his performance, she suddenly felt sympathetic.
Ye Shuo nodded without hesitation: “Of course, it’s particularly scary.”
The princes, who rarely saw such a bloody scene, were also frightened at first, but they all tried their best to cover it up. He was the only one who said it so bluntly.
Even the eldest prince couldn’t help but look at his younger brother a little more.
This younger brother is a bit bad, but at least he is honest.
After all the soldiers entered Shangjing City, Ye Shuo went back with them in a carriage.
The great victory of the eldest prince made the people vent their anger. Flowers and purses were thrown at the eldest prince and his men along the way without any cost. After a while, the eldest prince and the generals were covered with the fragrance of flowers, which contrasted with their armor that had been washed but still had dried blood in the cracks, and their cheeks that were slightly glowing red. In the bloody scene, it became beautiful.
Lifting the curtain, looking at the flower petals all over the sky, and then looking at the little princess next to him who was having a lot of fun with a look of surprise on her face, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but smile.
After the eldest prince and the generals returned to the Xuanzheng Hall, his stepfather would naturally reward them lavishly.
Of course, this is not something Ye Shuo should worry about.
Emperor Jingwen was sitting on the dragon throne, still thinking about how to start the conversation. Unexpectedly, before Emperor Jingwen could say anything, the eldest prince had already stepped forward and offered the tiger talisman representing military power with both hands.
“Ten years ago, my father gave this tiger talisman to me. Ten years later, I have fulfilled my mission. Now the tiger talisman has returned intact to Zhao. I hope you can take it back.”
The moment the words fell, the expressions of the Crown Prince and the Grand Tutor changed almost at the same time.
The more the eldest prince acted like this, the more difficult it became for the two of them.
They originally thought that if he refused to hand over his military power, they would still have room to talk later, but now the eldest prince was so obedient that the two of them could not do anything.
Emperor Jingwen became even happier upon seeing this.
Looking at his eldest son’s now mature face, Emperor Jingwen was silent for a moment, then said casually: “You have suffered a lot in the past ten years.”
This sentence is not from an emperor to his subjects, but from a father to his son.
Emperor Jingwen knew that he owed a lot to his eldest son, so he couldn’t help but soften his heart now.
The eldest prince left home at the age of seventeen and returned at the age of twenty-seven. Although he had other thoughts, he also wanted to prove one thing –
He, Ye Liancheng, is no worse than Ye Chengzuo.
Ten years ago, the eldest prince was just a young man who was holding a grudge in his heart and wanted to win his father’s favour.
So what if he was the crown prince? He was just born into the womb of the late queen, but his mother arrived at the crown prince’s residence two years earlier than the late queen!
And today, wasn’t he standing with the crown prince by virtue of his own efforts?
The eldest prince had been waiting for Emperor Jingwen to say this for ten years.
Just one simple word, “It’s hard work,” made the eldest prince’s eyes suddenly red even though he had never cried out in pain when a poison arrow pierced his shoulder.
“Replying to Father, it’s not hard. It’s what a son should do.”
Emperor Jingwen could not help but step forward and help him up personally.
When the prince saw this scene, he could only smile bitterly in his heart.
After all, one of them was the emperor and the other was the prince, so they quickly calmed down their emotions.
Then, the eldest prince brought an unexpected news –
Beiting is preparing to send an envoy to discuss the relations between the two countries.
Now that the war has come to an end, there should be an explanation between both sides, right?
What’s more, the eldest prince killed their General Lanruo and seized their three cities. Beiting cannot sit still this time.
General Lanruo’s head has been cut off and he cannot be resurrected. The other party’s only purpose in coming here is to take the three cities occupied by the Great Zhou.
Although the eldest prince won, the price he paid was not small. Therefore, the Great Zhou naturally had to be extremely cautious when dealing with the envoys from Beiting.
Emperor Jingwen’s heart trembled: “I understand. Let’s hand it over to the Ministry of Rites now.”
There is a lot of exchanges between the three countries, so the Ministry of Rites is familiar with such matters.
After a brief discussion with the ministers, Emperor Jingwen showed sympathy for the eldest prince and asked him how he had been doing over the years.
The ministers did not want to interfere in the affairs between the father and son, and soon they all left.
But when they were leaving, no matter whether it was the prime minister or the minister of the Chancellery, their eyes had changed to varying degrees.
Before the eldest prince returned, the prince’s position was naturally stable. But now that the eldest prince has returned, and has returned victoriously, the situation has suddenly become delicate.
He Xiang and Shang Shuling, who were not members of the Crown Prince’s party, had to take the eldest prince into their consideration.
The princes are trying to win over these old ministers, and these old ministers are naturally also considering these princes.
No one uttered a word, and soon they all dispersed.
The other side.
The queen had just returned to her palace and hadn’t even had time to sit down when she saw her son’s timid look and she became furious.
Especially when compared with the heroic and extraordinary eldest prince, his own son seemed even more stingy and cowardly.
What the queen wanted was a prince like the eldest prince who could bring honour to her, not a child like her own son.
“Cry, cry, cry, you just know how to cry. You really brought shame to me today!”
“It’s just a human head, but you are so scared. Look at yourself, do you look like a prince at all?”
What’s the point of giving birth to such a useless prince? Not only will he be burdened with illnesses.
The more she thought about it, the angrier she became. However, the queen also knew that with her son’s innate conditions, it would be difficult for him to become like the eldest prince in his lifetime. Although she was unwilling, the queen could do nothing about it.
Changing the subject, the queen quickly asked about the little prince’s recent studies.
In fact, the little prince knew the answers to all the questions she asked, but because the queen’s expression was so terrifying, the little prince was so nervous that he couldn’t answer them.
The more anxious he became, the less he could speak, and soon the little prince’s breathing became rapid and he looked like he was out of breath.
Instead of showing any sympathy, the queen became even more angry.
However, she had just cursed him twice. The little prince had been staying up late to study and had to get up early, and he had been frightened before. After coming back, he had to endure the verbal humiliation from his own biological mother. He couldn’t even catch his breath and fainted.
I touched my forehead again and it was burning hot.
Soon, the Queen’s Palace was in chaos.
And this summer rain finally fell.
*
Ye Shuo soon heard about the envoy’s arrival, and also heard the news that the little prince fell ill due to the previous rainstorm.
As to whether he really got sick because of the rain, Ye Shuo had an idea in his mind.
How could such a young child, less than four years old, not be frightened when he first saw such a scene?
The Queen has been trying to force the growth of seedlings, but she forgets that if she pulls too hard, the seedlings will rot.
The entire harem was very lively for a while because of the eldest prince’s return to the palace, but it quieted down after about half a month.
The days in the palace seemed to be unchanged, but the rain seemed to have turned on a switch, and it kept raining on and off, and it had been raining for half a month and it hadn’t cleared up yet.
Not to mention Emperor Jingwen and the Crown Prince, even Ye Shuo felt something was wrong.
You have to know that summer is the flood season. Given the drainage level in ancient times, too much precipitation would cause big problems.
As expected, three days later, news came from the south that the Yuan River, the mother river of the Great Zhou, had burst its banks.
After listening to Xiao Luzi’s words, Ye Shuo’s hand holding the charcoal pencil suddenly paused.

chapters.title: Chapter 128: Help
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
Envoy… The river burst its banks…
These two things together are not a good thing.
Although the eldest prince and his stepfather announced to the outside world that they had won a great victory, the price they paid behind the scenes must have been heavy.
Two countries that were originally evenly matched, suddenly one of them becomes increasingly powerful, and then defeats the other as if opening up its Ren and Du meridians. It is easy to imagine that this kind of thing is unlikely to happen.
The bursting of the Yuan River’s dike is a matter of great importance and will certainly consume a great deal of manpower and material resources. If the envoys discover any signs of weakness in the Great Zhou during their visit, they may come back again after returning. By then, the Great Zhou will be in danger due to internal and external troubles.
This can be seen from the sudden change in the atmosphere in the palace.
Ever since Ye Shuo was born, the palace has never been so tense.
The palace servants, who had originally seemed relatively relaxed, were now in a hurry. Apart from their master’s orders, they refused to say a single word, fearing that saying the wrong thing would bring disaster upon themselves.
Especially the eunuch Wang Ziquan of the Qinzheng Palace. Even eunuch Wang doesn’t seem to smile now, let alone others.Ever since the news of the Yuan River bursting its banks, my stepfather has never set foot in the harem again and has simply slept in the Qinzheng Hall at night.
The same goes for the prince, who is almost nowhere to be seen nowadays.
Prime Minister He and the Grand Tutor came and went, with a hint of worry on their faces. It was obvious that they also found the situation difficult.
Under such circumstances, the Grand Tutor didn’t even have time to take care of the Ninth Prince and the little princess, and directly gave them both a holiday.
Under normal circumstances, Ye Shuo would have been extremely happy, but now, he really couldn’t laugh.
Since he has become a prince of the Zhou Dynasty in this life, he will never be able to get rid of this identity for the rest of his life.
Now in the Great Zhou Dynasty, he has his mother, his grandfather’s family, and many other people he cares about, so Ye Shuo naturally cannot leave them.
Only when the Great Zhou is doing well can Ye Shuo live a good life.
In this situation, Ye Shuo couldn’t just sit there and do nothing, right?
Thinking about it, Ye Shuo sighed, then somersaulted and sat up from the gorgeous carved wooden bed.
Then Ye Shuo sent Xiao Luzi to deliver the several books that had been sorted out two days ago, as well as a letter, to his eldest cousin in the name of purchasing.
It is written very clearly in the letter, and my cousin will naturally understand it after reading it.
Because the envoy was about to arrive, everyone in the palace was not paying attention here, so no one noticed that Xiao Luzi, who was beside the Ninth Prince, had been away for almost an hour.
The other side.
Although the officials below had notified the people downstream before the water level surged, many people were still killed because the dam of the source river burst too suddenly. In some places, there was even an entire village with no one left.
Large areas of villages are now submerged by floods.
In order to prevent the concealment of the news, Emperor Jingwen promptly sent imperial envoys out of the capital. Now, news came one after another from various places downstream, the scope of the impact was getting wider and wider, the number of casualties was increasing, and Emperor Jingwen’s face was getting uglier and uglier.
From a few hundred at the beginning, it grew to a few thousand, and now it has reached tens of thousands.
Water sources are an indispensable part of people’s lives. In the absence of modern facilities, most people like to live near water. While this facilitates farmland irrigation, they also have to bear the risk of floods.
The casualties were increasing, and more and more people were being displaced. Emperor Jingwen did everything he could, and his eyes were red from staying up late. However, in the face of natural disasters, human power is always so powerless.
If this continues, the situation will be bad.
The most important thing at the moment is to curb the spread of the flood, as well as the resettlement of the victims, the reconstruction of villages and the repair of dams.
Each and every one of them requires a lot of effort and money.
Leaving aside the mind and money, the issues of containment, reconstruction and renovation alone are already quite tricky.
There are too few talented people in this area in the court.
Because of the geographical location of Da Zhou in the lower reaches of the source river, Da Zhou suffered far more flood disasters than the other two countries.
However, people who know how to manage water are always extremely scarce.
Just when Emperor Jingwen was suffering from a splitting headache, he suddenly thought of a person, and that person happened to be within the territory of the Great Zhou.
Emperor Jingwen made a prompt decision and “invited” Mr. Zeng Mohuai over.
Things are different now. Emperor Jingwen no longer cares about using any conciliatory tactics. At such a critical moment, he will tie Zeng Mohuai up even if he has to.
In addition to improving various tools and designing mechanisms, this man is also very capable in controlling floods and building dams, otherwise he would not be so respected.
Zeng Mohuai had served as an official in the Great Zhou for half a year. Although Emperor Jingwen knew his character and was even more aware that he was stubborn and never considered himself a subject of any of the Three Kingdoms, people like him would be less willing to work the more they were forced to do so.
Emperor Jingwen was even prepared to massacre all the disciples around Zeng Mohuai in order to force him to submit. However, as soon as he made the decision and before he could tell the secret guards to do it immediately, Zeng Mohuai took the initiative to send a message saying that he was willing to come forward and do his best.
People with ill intentions would rather watch the joke of Da Zhou, so it is unlikely that someone with bad intentions would take action at this time.
Zeng Mohuai had three thousand disciples, and the breach of the Yuan River caused such a big commotion, so it was not difficult to understand that he knew about it so quickly.
Therefore, when Emperor Jingwen learned the news, he was not surprised, but happy.
Several years ago, the Yuanqing Canal, which Zeng Mohuai participated in building when he was young, is still standing today. After more than 20 years of wind and rain, the surrounding embankments have collapsed countless times, but the Yuanqing Canal is still strong. Zeng Mohuai’s ability is evident.
However, while he was happy, Emperor Jingwen was also a little puzzled. Normally, he wouldn’t worry about such things. Why did he suddenly become so kind-hearted this time?
However, being puzzled does not mean that Emperor Jingwen doubted him. After all, Zeng Mohuai was used to doing whatever he wanted. He had never had any rules in doing things, so it was not strange for him to act on impulse occasionally.
When Zeng Mohuai arrived at the lower reaches of Yuan River in a carriage, Emperor Jingwen sent secret guards to investigate. They found out that it was not for any other reason, but that Zeng Mohuai had accepted a large number of new disciples in recent years. Zeng Mohuai felt that it was not a good idea to let them study all the time, so he brought them out this time to practise.
Of course, Zeng Mohuai has high standards and he doesn’t want everyone. This time, he only picked out seven or eight students from thousands of them.
Although the number of people is small, they are the most outstanding among my teaching achievements in the past three years and can be called masterpieces.
Zeng Mohuai is worthy of being Zeng Mohuai. He has always been so rebellious. The disciples he brought out this time include both male and female disciples. Most of them are teenagers. What’s more, there are even children who are twelve or thirteen years old.
Emperor Jingwen felt overwhelmed at the thought of asking these young boys and girls, especially the girls, to participate in the flood control.
The flood is a serious matter, and it can cost the lives of countless people. Zeng Mohuai’s actions are somewhat disregarding human life.
If Zeng Mohuai was just leading them, it would be fine and Emperor Jingwen would have tolerated it reluctantly. However, two days later, news came from the imperial envoy that Zeng Mohuai actually planned to let these children do it himself, and Emperor Jingwen could no longer sit still.
Is he crazy?
But there was nothing that could be done about it. It was not that Zeng Mohuai did not take his fate seriously, but after he arrived he found that the flood had affected too wide a range, and that even with himself and his eldest disciple, they were far from enough.
No matter how capable Zeng Mohuai is, he is just one person. He can only take care of the areas most affected by the disaster, and other places are out of his reach.
Although this group of young boys and girls are still young, they have learned it after all, and they are the best ones. They are better than those who know nothing about water control.
And these good things are equivalent to many lives.
