While the eldest prince was stunned, Emperor Jingwen said, “In fact, today I am really worried that Xiaojiu will take action directly.”
The eldest prince originally thought that Emperor Jingwen was worried that his ninth brother would suffer a loss if they really fought, but Emperor Jingwen immediately said, “It would be bad if Little Nine hit hard and hurt the grandson of the emperor.”
It would be fine if it comes to studying, as there are no good teachers at the border, so Yan’er and the others are naturally worse at studying than the prince’s sons. But when it comes to martial arts, the eldest prince is confident that no one of his peers can be a match for his son.
“Your Majesty, you underestimate Yan’er and the others.” Even if the Ninth Prince was taught by the Duke of Zhen, it would not be like this. The First Prince was confident that he was no worse than the Duke of Zhen.
Therefore, the eldest prince couldn’t help but defend his sons.
Upon hearing this, Ye Yan and the others immediately straightened their chests.
“Oh? Are your sons confident that they can withstand these moves?” Suddenly remembering the incident of his ear being bitten, Emperor Jingwen’s expression froze at first, and then quickly returned to normal.
In this way, the eldest prince soon learned about his younger brother’s famous skills, except for the ear-biting thing.
These are all tricks that the eldest prince would never use even if he were beaten to death.
Since the eldest prince doesn’t use it, his sons naturally won’t use it either.
For some reason, Ye Yan and the others suddenly felt a chill between their legs.
I didn’t expect the Ninth Prince to be like this…
The eldest prince was now completely speechless, and even felt a little regretful for provoking such a scoundrel.
As the sun sets, the eldest prince leaves the palace with his absent-minded sons.
Looking at the backs of several people from afar, Wang Ziquan didn’t know why, but he always felt that the emperor said those words on purpose.
After a while, Wang Ziquan vaguely heard Emperor Jingwen sigh softly.
Emperor Jingwen didn’t want to say so much. After all, he had never worried so much when he was the crown prince.
But Xiaojiu is different after all. As the crown prince, if he is protected too tightly without any leaks, it may be detrimental to the Great Zhou. As for Xiaojiu, he has no ability and is easy to offend people, so he can only rely on himself.
If he really offends his eldest son to death, he will suffer in the future.
Xiaojiu couldn’t think so much, so I could only take the trouble to help him clean up the mess.
Soon, Emperor Jingwen waved to Wang Ziquan.
“Let’s go, we’re going back too.”
The other side.
Ye Shuo had a good sleep. The next morning, he packed up and took Jian Jian to the study.
The four brothers Ye Yan no longer had the arrogance they had yesterday. Time was too tight, and they didn’t even have time to find a study partner. They just came to the upper study room like they had lost their parents.
Although Ye Yan and others were already prepared, they were still very panicked when they saw the Ninth Prince walking towards them after the second class.
“It’s almost time for the horseback archery class, all of you follow me.”
Ye Yan subconsciously wanted to resist, but Ye Shuo seemed to see through his intention and immediately turned his gaze to the Eighth Prince standing beside him.
The Eighth Prince felt that he had offended someone and secretly made up his mind that when Master Wu arrived, he would learn well this time!
Forced by Ye Shuo’s tyranny, Ye Yan could only follow Ye Shuo out reluctantly. However, what they were thinking in their hearts was that Eighth Uncle would leave the palace and build his own house in less than a year. By that time, Eighth Uncle would not be in the study, so who could Ninth Uncle threaten?
Thinking of this, they suddenly had hope, and Ye Yan and the other three felt much more relieved.
As the saying goes, it is never too late for a gentleman to take revenge. Ye Yan made a decisive decision and endured it!
Satisfied to see that they were obedient, Ye Shuo threw Jian Jian to a few people and told her to go for it as her nephews were so strong that she would definitely not be able to hurt them with her current strength.
Just like this, Ye Yan and others, who were still children themselves, were forced to take care of children.
Looking at Ye Shuo on the side, after doing horse stance and two sets of boxing, he flipped over the hammock, closed his eyes and took a good rest.
It was unexpected that he wanted to let his nephew teach his aunt martial arts.
However, Emperor Jingwen was no longer surprised. He didn’t even blink when he heard the news and continued to discuss the follow-up issues of the flood with Prime Minister He and others.
On the other side, after hearing the news, the Grand Tutor couldn’t help but frown, and seemed a little angry.
“How could His Highness do this! How could His Highness hang out with the eldest prince’s sons!”
The Grand Tutor, who had already included the Ninth Prince in his own camp, obviously found it difficult to accept this matter. He even thought that Ye Shuo’s move was an attempt to please both sides.
To put it bluntly, the Grand Tutor thought Ye Shuo was one of his own, which is why he feels betrayed now.
As for the prince standing aside, he was stunned for a while, then said in a deep voice: “Master!”
The Grand Tutor subconsciously turned his head and heard the Crown Prince slowly speak: “This matter has nothing to do with Xiaojiu. Xiaojiu is free by nature. He can be with whoever he wants.”
“Don’t involve him in the affairs of the court. Those things have nothing to do with him.”
Let a child like that do whatever he wants…
Upon hearing this, the Grand Tutor fell silent.
If this is true, then wouldn’t the previous closeness be in vain? Although the Ninth Prince is useless, the emperor’s favor is quite helpful.
Although thinking this in his heart, the Grand Tutor opened his mouth and finally said: “…In that case, I will follow your Highness’s wishes.”
For a long time afterwards, the two of them looked at the yard in front of them without saying a word.
The days passed one by one, and just when the foundation laying of Jianjian was in full swing, the eight people from Zouwu and the envoys from Beiting arrived almost at the same time.

chapters.title: Chapter 135: Misunderstanding
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
Another month has passed. Although the flood is gradually receding, the follow-up matters have not decreased at all.
Fortunately, during the years when Emperor Jingwen was in power, the Great Zhou had developed well and the treasury was full, so it still had enough strength to deal with this sudden crisis. However, if Beiting took the opportunity to join in, it would be hard to say what would happen.
Fortunately, compared with the victims who died in the disaster, more people were saved. I think with the addition of these people, they will be able to restore their previous order soon.
When Emperor Jingwen received the report about the disaster area from the imperial envoy, he was not optimistic at first. It has been so many years since he became the crown prince, and the Yuan River has been flooding all year round. After each flood, typhoid fever and malaria would be rampant.
This time the collapse of the Yuanhe dam was so massive that it would be even more so.
Emperor Jingwen had already prepared for a drastic population decline. However, when he opened the memorial, he found that although the flood was severe, the subsequent casualties were even less than before. Epidemics broke out in several places, but they were quickly brought under control. The methods used were ones that Emperor Jingwen had never heard of before.
For example, feces must be centrally processed and filth must be cleaned up in a timely manner. The various sundries produced by the victims’ daily lives cannot be thrown away at random, but must be collected by special people and handled in a unified manner. Other things include not drinking raw water, even well water that looks clean must be boiled before it can be drunk, food must be thoroughly cooked, the meat of dead animals must not be eaten, but must be buried in a deep pit, and clothes cannot be washed in the river. The places where the victims live must be fumigated with large amounts of wormwood every day, etc.
At first, the imperial envoy thought it was troublesome. After all, everyone felt extremely tired after the disaster. Who could care so much?
But there was no way. The eight people forced him to do it.Those people are now heroes who played a big role when the flood occurred. They are also the ones specifically requested by the emperor. Even the imperial envoy has to take their feelings into consideration.
After much deliberation, the imperial envoy finally did as he was told.
The people’s daily lives are not very particular, so it is quite difficult to get them to behave themselves all of a sudden.
But it didn’t matter, the imperial envoy had soldiers at his disposal. Emperor Jingwen temporarily gave him the power to dispatch the nearest troop. Under the concerted efforts and strict supervision of everyone, the epidemic that had raged in the past was miraculously reduced a lot. It was truly a miracle.
If this method had been known before, the Great Zhou would have suffered fewer casualties during the flood.
Shocked, the imperial envoy hurriedly reported the matter to Emperor Jingwen.
Although they did not know the reason behind it, the doctors around them, including the imperial physician sent by Emperor Jingwen, recorded the above methods in a book to pass on to future generations.
After reading this thick book of memorials, Emperor Jingwen regarded those eight people even more highly.
With such talented people, why should the Great Zhou Dynasty worry about its prosperity?
It so happened that the envoys from Beiting were about to arrive, and the significance of the eight representatives was even more different.
The other side.
After setting foot in Shangjing City, Zou Wu and the others were very excited. Some of this excitement was due to the prosperity of Shangjing, but more of it was the anticipation for the teacher whom they had never met.
Master Zeng said that their other teacher was a member of the royal family. If they were lucky enough to meet him, he would wear a jade pendant shaped like a lily flower around his waist, and they could recognize him by the pendant.
However, the lily of the valley is always small and more suitable for women, so the eight people couldn’t help but wonder whether their other teacher would be a woman.
Thinking of this, Zou Wu and the other two, who were also women, couldn’t help but feel excited.
The other five people felt a little embarrassed.
Although there were many women among the people who studied with him, they were still influenced by the current secular world. They still felt naturally embarrassed when facing women, and their faces turned red in a short while.
Obviously, they have already imagined the image of a noble and elegant female teacher in their minds.
But at the same time, the five of them were a little worried. If this was the case, wouldn’t it be inconvenient for the other party to teach them again?
Rather than the so-called gender distinction, they care more about whether they can learn something.
In order to leave a good impression on the mysterious teacher, Zou Wu and her companions, who originally did not care much about their appearance, ordered hot water and dressed up properly the day before they were summoned to the palace.
Now, they are still young and energetic, so even though they have been busy in the disaster area for such a long time, they can have a good sleep after cleaning up, and when they wake up, they have regained the vitality that young people should have, which makes the young eunuchs on the side envious.
Although the group of people in front of them looked rustic and were far less graceful than the nobles in the palace, at this critical juncture, the significance represented by these eight people was extraordinary.
Even though they are still commoners now, if they perform well when the envoys come, they will surely be able to rise to prominence.
Thinking of this, the young eunuchs became even more respectful.
Seeing that the time was almost up, one of the eunuchs stepped forward and reminded, “It is almost the morning hour, everyone please follow me into the palace.”
Zou Wu and her companions felt a tightness in their hearts at first, and they breathed in and out for a long time. After they calmed down, they quickly boarded the carriage to the palace.
About half an hour later, looking at the white marble stone steps in front of them, the majestic white jade dragon head on it looked down from above, with solemn and dignified eyes, which made people feel intimidated. Even Zou Wu and the others wanted to retreat for a moment.
This is the imperial palace, where the most honourable emperor of the Great Zhou Dynasty lives. It is a place that ordinary people would never be able to set foot in their entire lives, but now it is right before their eyes.
If it weren’t for the two teachers and General Wei who had always supported them, they would definitely not be where they are today.
The more this happened, the more they could not embarrass the two teachers.
After all, he was the person Zeng Mohuai liked. He hesitated for only a moment, and soon Zou Wu and the others took the first step without fear.
At the 15th hour in the morning, inside the Xuanzheng Hall, Emperor Jingwen and the ministers stopped at the same time as if they had sensed something.
Not long after, eight people appeared outside the Xuanzheng Hall.
Now is the time when the morning sun is just rising. The morning sun symbolises flourishing hope. Besides, Zou Wu and the others are so young, the eight of them seem to be stepping on the morning sun. Even He Xiang and the others are moved for a moment.
As expected of Zeng Mohuai’s students, he is indeed different from others.
Zou Wu and the others had no idea what the other ministers were thinking. After they entered the palace, they seemed to be intimidated by the emperor’s holy face on the dragon throne. They all lowered their heads and said in a loud voice, “We greet the emperor. Long live the emperor.”
Although these eight people were a little nervous, they were not timid. The saying “a newborn calf is not afraid of a tiger” was almost fully reflected in them.
When Emperor Jingwen saw this scene, a thought subconsciously crossed his mind –
It would be great if his son could be like this. Without saying too much, Emperor Jingwen would be satisfied if he could have half of what they have.
As for who this son is talking about, you don’t have to think about it to know.
Thinking this in his heart, Emperor Jingwen said, “Well, everyone get up.”
Zou Wu and the others did as they were told. When they stood up, their eyes simultaneously glanced at the waists of several people wearing python robes next to them.
No, no, no, no this either.
Since it was an early morning court session, basically all the princes and nobles who had reached the age were here. If nothing had been discovered, then the possibility that the teacher was a woman increased a little.
Just as the eight people were thinking about it, Emperor Jingwen asked a few more questions. Seeing that most of them answered fluently, he was satisfied. At the same time, he was certain in his heart and asked, “The envoy is coming. If I want you to show the power of my Great Zhou in front of the envoy, can you do it?”
Master Zeng had already explained this matter to them when they arrived, so the eight people were not particularly surprised.
“I will do my best to obey the orders of His Majesty.”
They didn’t know what would happen at that time, so they didn’t say anything definite.
Upon hearing this, Emperor Jingwen was not dissatisfied at all. Instead, he nodded in praise.
Of course, along with the arrival of the eight people, there was also news that the eldest prince was promoted to prince*.
[1] The eldest prince was promoted as prince with title, like king of jin, the title of his uncle
Ten years ago, when the eldest prince went to war, he was conferred the title of a prince in order to elevate his status. Now that he has returned victorious, he deserves a reward.
This decree, which had been delayed for two full months, finally came down.
At the very end, when seeing the thirteen-year-old Lu Mu, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but say, “You are indeed a disciple of Master Zeng. You are truly a young man to be feared. If my ninth son could be like you, I wouldn’t have to worry every day now.”
Upon hearing this, Prime Minister He and the Grand Tutor could not help but nod in agreement.
The Ninth Prince?
This name flashed through their minds. They had just noticed that the one standing in the front was the Crown Prince, and the remaining princes were only the Seventh Prince. The Seventh Prince was only fifteen years old this year, so the Ninth Prince must be even younger.
Therefore, Zou Wu and others didn’t take Emperor Jingwen’s casual words to heart at all.
However, they lived in the imperial city for the next few days, so they naturally heard some things about the Ninth Prince.
It’s not that they intended to spy, nor is it that the people around them were not tight-lipped. The main reason was that the Ninth Prince was too famous. Just like the previous incident with the Cao family, where the Crown Prince’s tutor and the Prince of Jin personally caught the adulterer, it would be hard for the people in the capital to not know about it.
As for the culprit of this incident, it was the Ninth Prince.
Zou Wu couldn’t help but laughed and teased: “This Ninth Prince is even more mischievous than you.”
Lu Mu is young, so it’s normal for him to be not so steady sometimes.
Hearing this, Lu Mu couldn’t help but chuckle, feeling quite embarrassed.
At the same time, Ye Shuo, who was doing horse stance, felt his nose itchy and couldn’t help sneezing.
Time passed quietly in such an atmosphere. Three days passed in a flash, and the envoys from Beiting finally arrived in Shangjing City.
The arrival of envoys from foreign countries is always a big event, and the capital city also becomes lively.
Ye Shuo, who had been doing nothing, jumped up upon hearing the news and prepared to leave the palace with Xiao Luzi.
References
↑1The eldest prince was promoted as prince with title, like king of jin, the title of his uncle

chapters.title: Chapter 136: Wandering
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
The time Ye Shuo chooses is always so coincidental.
Now that the envoys were about to arrive, no one cared about him at all. Ye Shuo easily left the gate of the imperial city. By the time Emperor Jingwen received the news, it was too late. He could only quickly send two guards to follow him to prevent Xiao Jiu from causing any more trouble.
Jianjian woke up happily and went to look for her brother, but she found him in vain. She heard from the imperial concubine that her brother had gone out to play and had left long ago. Jianjian couldn’t help crying.
She didn’t even mind her brother being stupid, but he went out to play without her. What a bad brother!
Without her brother, Jianjian was like a bird without wings. Suddenly, she couldn’t feel happy anymore!
The imperial concubine’s scalp was numb when she saw this. After a lot of coaxing, she gradually diverted the little princess’ attention.
On the other hand, Ye Shuo felt no guilt at all for leaving his sister behind, and swaggered to the streets of Shangjing City.
Now the envoys are about to arrive, and the capital city is a mixed crowd. Jianjian is still too young. Ye Shuo cannot guarantee that he can keep an eye on her 100% for a little child. If she falls into the hands of bad people, she will have no place to cry. So it is better to just keep her in the palace.
Ye Shuo originally wanted to bring Ye Xun with him, but he heard that Ye Xun was helping the prince deal with the reception of envoys and was really busy, so he asked the eunuch who delivered the message to apologize to him.A child of only seven years old is now handling the diplomatic relations between the two countries. This is unimaginable.
Since Ye Xun had important things to do, Ye Shuo certainly couldn’t delay him, so Ye Shuo turned around and invited a few other nephews who were unemployed at home and had nothing to do to come and play with him.
Ye Yan and the others thought that their days of suffering were finally over, but it turned out that the Ninth Prince was not willing to let them go at all.
At that time, Ye Yan and his brothers were resting at home, enjoying the long-lost leisure time. The four brothers all burst into tears.
God knows how hard their days have been recently as they have to study while practising martial arts with their little aunt. The little aunt is young and delicate. If they don’t use enough strength and there is no effect, the Ninth Prince will be unhappy. If they use too much strength, they will hurt the little aunt and the Ninth Prince will still be angry. With this kind of dilemma, one day of practice is more tiring than three days of normal practice, not to mention how painful it is.
Now when Ye Yan and others see Ye Shuo, they want to stay as far away from him as possible.
However, the eldest prince, now Prince Ding, heard something different.
“You have been following the Ninth Prince for so long, haven’t you noticed anything different?”
“No.” Ye Yan and the other three shook their heads in unison. “Ninth Prince sleeps until noon every day, often skips school, and always makes Lord Cen very angry. It seems that the Grand Tutor can’t do anything about him. In the morning, he usually reads some miscellaneous books and then goes to the various palace ladies for lunch. In the afternoon, he just does some horse stance and a few sets of boxing, and then starts to bask in the sun, and doesn’t go back until almost dusk…”
Perhaps it was because Ye Shuo was too familiar with this process, and Lord Cen and the others seemed to be accustomed to it, it was difficult for Ye Yan and the others not to wonder whether the Ninth Prince had always done this.
“This…is impossible?” There is actually such an unmotivated person among his younger brothers?
The eldest prince had only seen such leisurely state in some old princes of the royal family, but the key point was that all of these old princes were old men with one foot in the coffin.
“Are you sure he’s not pretending?”
As soon as the eldest prince asked this question, news came from the gatehouse that the ninth prince had just left the palace, and asked several of the emperor’s grandsons to hurry over.
The eldest prince: “…”
Ye Yan and the other three: “…”
No way, again?
The eldest prince suddenly realized that he might not know that he had been promoted to prince.
The four little ones looked at their father eagerly.
Ye Yan and the others had originally planned to let the eldest prince make the decision for them, but who would have thought that after hesitating for a while, the eldest prince actually waved his hand at them.
“Forget it, since he asked you to go, then go.”
It seems that what the emperor said before was true. The ninth prince is indeed a fool.
The eldest prince felt that he was even more stupid for arguing with a fool.
The eldest prince suddenly became too lazy to argue with his younger brother.
Just like that, Ye Yan and his brothers failed to take charge and were instead kicked out of the house by their father.
The four little ones had no choice but to follow Xiao Luzi dejectedly to Ye Shuo’s side.
Then Ye Shuo learned that the eldest prince had just been conferred the title of prince. As for the title of his cheap elder brother, it was even more interesting——
King Ding.
The word “ding” has the meaning of stabilizing the country, but it also has the meaning of fixed or established.
I just don’t know whether my cheap dad is thinking the former, the latter, or both. If that’s really what he thinks…
It is a decision that should not be regretted. The stepfather must have already thought about the position of his son when he sent the eldest prince to the military camp.
The emperor’s heart is as deep as an abyss, and his will is the truth, which cannot be resisted in the slightest.
What is fate? What my cheap dad arranged is fate.
If this is true, the crown prince can be saved, but the eldest prince will be in danger.
What would he do with those who were beyond his control?
While Ye Shuo was stunned, Ye Yan and the others couldn’t help but straighten their chests.
So, is the Ninth Prince scared?
Now his father is a prince, and his status is much higher than his, the oligarch prince.
Their status also rose with the tide. Now they were the sons of a prince. Who had ever seen a prince’s son being a playmate?
However, the next moment, their fantasies were shattered.
“Your father is a prince, and my father is the emperor. Stop showing off and go to the front to lead the way.” Seeing their smug looks, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but patted each of them on the head.
How could he not be afraid!
Ye Yan turned his head with an expression of disbelief. Ye Shuo glanced over and the chests of Ye Yan and the others rose and fell violently. Thinking of their father’s instructions before returning to the capital, the four brothers of Ye Yan finally gritted their teeth and went to the front to clear the way.
The kids were as strong as calves and had great strength. Soon, a large open space appeared around Ye Shuo.
Ye Shuo had brought enough money with him on this trip. When he passed by the candied haws stand, he casually asked, “Do you want to eat candied haws?”
As an uncle, it’s normal to buy snacks for your children.
But Ye Yan and the others were the grandchildren of the emperor, so how could they not look down upon the food of ordinary people? So they all shook their heads.
“What about pea yellow? Lotus crisps? Donkey meat hotpot?”
Ye Shuo mentioned several snacks in a row, but Ye Yan and others still refused.
“Okay then, if you don’t want to eat it, I’ll eat it myself.” Ye Shuo didn’t force him.
Soon the small path beside him and the hands of the two guards were occupied, while Ye Shuo took a bite of the donkey meat hotpot and drank a sip of the ancient handmade lotus root powder.
Ye Yan and his brothers were children after all. They get hungry quickly if they exercise a lot. It didn’t take long for them to digest their breakfast. Then, surrounded by the aroma of meat and the sweet smell of snacks, they suddenly felt tormented.
Seeing how happily the Ninth Prince was eating, the youngest one couldn’t help but looked back again and again.
Ye Shuo pretended not to see it and took another big bite of the fire in his hand.
As the saying goes, there is dragon meat in the sky and donkey meat on the ground. Donkey meat itself is particularly fresh and fragrant. Coupled with the good skills of the stall owner, the braised donkey meat is even more tender and juicy.
The emperor’s grandson watched helplessly as a trickle of oil slid down from the fire and seeped into the oil paper bag.
“Gudong,” the child swallowed hard.
“Ninth Uncle…”
“Why, you want to eat?”
The child hesitated for a moment, and finally nodded vigorously.
Ye Shuo raised his eyebrows, then motioned Xiao Luzi to come over and opened the oil paper bag in Xiao Luzi’s hand. Ye Shuo deliberately picked out a piece of fattier donkey meat and stuffed it into his little nephew’s mouth.
The little grandson of the emperor suddenly discovered that folk snacks seemed to be quite good, and had a different flavor than those cooked by the imperial chefs.
Once there was one, there were two. Soon the remaining few also fell. Ye Yan, the eldest brother, tried to struggle, but he couldn’t resist the temptation of food at all.
Just when the group was enjoying their meal, the envoy from Beiting finally arrived and revealed his true appearance.
That was an extremely powerful team. Beiting was located in the north of Da Zhou. The subjects of Beiting had been eating cattle and sheep all year round, and they were all fat and strong. Ye Shuo estimated that one of them was almost as powerful as two people in Beijing.
If all the soldiers in Beiting were like this, it’s no wonder that my cheap father would regard them as a thorn in his side and treat them so cautiously.
Not to mention the people, even the horses they ride are larger than those of the Great Zhou. The horses have strong limbs, so they should have better endurance.
The dozens of people walking in front should be guards. As for the real envoy, he should be the one sitting in the carriage at the back.
Ye Shuo noticed that these people all looked extremely arrogant. No matter if it was real arrogance or fake arrogance, just by looking at the disdain and arrogance flashing in their eyes when they looked at the people of the Great Zhou, Ye Shuo knew that this group of people probably had bad intentions.
That’s right. After all, there had just been a flood in the Great Zhou. Even if the Great Zhou had won the previous battle, it could just start over now.
When the Minister of Rites also came on horseback to greet them, he passed by the surrounding shops. Originally, his attention was all on the envoys’ team, but he accidentally saw a few very familiar figures.
Who else could it be but the Ninth Prince and his nephews?
And now the Ninth Prince and the emperor’s grandchildren were squatting under the eaves of the shop, each holding an oil-paper bag, eating food like donkey meat and hot bread without any image.
Seeing that the other party seemed to have recognized his identity, Ye Shuo not only had no sense of shame, but waved to the other party happily.
Minister of Rites: “…”
Oh my God, we must not let the people of Beiting know that these are their prince and grandson!
Otherwise, Da Zhou would lose all face.
The Minister of Rites had prepared a lot of things to say, but now he couldn’t say them.
He turned his eyes away silently, pretending nothing had happened, and the Minister of Rites said succinctly: “Everyone is tired from the journey, please follow me.”
When the previous emperor of the Great Zhou was in power, he was extremely polite to the Beiting people. Even amidst his politeness, there was a hint of fear. But the officials under the current emperor are quite arrogant.
The Beiting envoy in the carriage frowned, and after a moment, he signaled everyone to follow the Minister of Rites.
At the same time, in the Qinzheng Hall, upon learning of the arrival of the envoy, Emperor Jingwen remained calm and continued to handle the memorials at hand as usual.
Even though the Great Zhou had just experienced a flood, Beiting was defeated and since it was defeated, it should be treated as a defeated country.
Emperor Jingwen didn’t even let the crown prince go to receive him, he only sent the Minister of Rites.
“Your servant pays respects to His Majesty.”
Just when there was silence in the Qinzheng Hall, a figure suddenly appeared.
Familiar voice, familiar actions, who else could the person coming be but Wu Yi?

chapters.title: Chapter 137: Late
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
After many years, Wu Yi has become more mature.
When Emperor Jingwen saw him, he didn’t say anything but asked, “How is Beiting doing recently?”
It turns out that Wu Yi’s mission back then was to lead a group of people to collect intelligence about Beiting, and now the time has finally come when it can be put to use.
After receiving the order, Wu Yi rushed back without stopping and finally arrived just before the envoy arrived.
Wu Yi briefly reported the recent situation in Beiting to Emperor Jingwen.
As expected by others, the envoys from Beiting came with ill intentions. It has rarely rained in Beiting since spring this year, and there was no rain at all throughout the summer. The grain planted by the people of Beiting this year was almost a failure.
That would be fine, as even without food there were still cattle and sheep, but the problem was that there was no rainfall, the grassland was so dry that a large number of cattle and sheep also starved to death.
Beiting is now facing a famine. According to Beiting’s brutal nature, once it reaches the end of its rope, it will inevitably march its troops southward, start slaughtering the people of other countries, and occupy other countries’ lands in order to survive.
The question now is whether the enemy’s target is the Great Zhou or the Chen State in the west.Although Chen was the weakest of the three countries, it was easy to defend but difficult to attack due to its complex terrain and many mountains and rivers. In addition, Da Zhou had just experienced a flood, so Emperor Jingwen was almost certain that the enemy was most likely targeting Da Zhou.
Fortunately, Zeng Mohuai led his disciples to take action in time, otherwise if the flood was allowed to rage, Beiting would probably have taken action by now, and would not even have gone through this.
Especially this time, the envoy sent by the other party was Huyan Jue.
Huyan is the surname of the Beiting royal family, and Huyan Jue is the uncle of the current Beiting Wolf King. Such an important identity is naturally extraordinary.
The other party is probably trying to determine whether the Great Zhou still has the strength to fight against them.
If there is another war, the current treasury can still support it, but the key is that in order to survive, Beiting will certainly do its best. This time the outcome is unpredictable. Even if it wins by chance again, Da Zhou will inevitably suffer heavy losses, and the neighboring Chen State will inevitably take the opportunity to cause chaos.
The best outcome would be to let Beiting confront the State of Chen, while the Great Zhou would sit on the mountain and watch the fight between the two tigers, and reap the benefits.
But how to make Beiting give up this idea is a problem.
The envoys from Beiting will stay in Shangjing for about seven days. A solution must be found within these seven days.
The most important thing today is tonight’s banquet.
“I understand. You go down first.” After pondering for a long time, Emperor Jingwen waved at Wu Yi.
Wu Yi bowed his head and said, “I will take my leave.”
Soon, the Qinzheng Hall returned to peace.
The other side.
Ye Shuo pondered for a long time and finally decided to join in the fun.
It was so hard to have an outsider come, and he was very curious.
“Let’s go and take a look.” Ye Shuo wrapped the food in oil paper and handed it to Xiao Luzi beside him. He wiped his mouth and stood up.
Ye Yan and the other three were stunned for a moment, then quickly stuffed the remaining steamed bread into their mouths and followed.
After spending a few days with the Ninth Prince, Ye Yan and his companions clearly discovered that the Ninth Prince seemed to particularly love joining in the fun; wherever there was fun, he would be there.
Led by the Minister of Rites, the envoys’ team soon arrived at the post station.
Beiting is Beiting after all. Even if it was defeated in the war, its treatment was different from that of other small countries. The Ministry of Rites entertained Beiting envoys according to almost the highest standards. A few days before the Beiting envoys arrived, the Ministry of Rites had ordered people to vacate the entire post station.
People from other small countries have now temporarily moved elsewhere.
The Great Zhou was still the same Great Zhou, seemingly no different from many years ago.
When Huyan Jue got off the car, he gave a subtle wink to the servants around him.
The servant understood, and after entering the room, he started making a fuss in a short while.
According to the servants, the beds in the rooms that were nicely arranged by the Ministry of Rites have now become garbage. Either the quilts are not soft enough, or the wooden beds are unstable, or the surrounding furnishings are not of high enough quality.
That look was as if Huyan Jue had lived in a fairy palace before.
If the Minister of Rites had not known that the people in Beiting, from the common people to the royal family, were all barbarians who ate raw meat and drank blood, he would have been deceived by them.
In the past, people in Beiting were not so particular. I guess they must have lost the war and were looking for trouble on purpose.
When Ye Shuo arrived at the inn, he heard the quarrel inside.
Originally, Ye Shuo wanted to go in and find out what was going on, but now, there was no need to go in. The other party was making so much noise that he could hear it even from outside.
Looking at Ye Yan and the others standing aside, I don’t know when their facial features were wrinkled.
“This envoy from Beiting is so rude!”
“Yes, yes.” Ye Shuo nodded repeatedly.
Although the people of Beiting look tall and powerful, they are not real fools. They probably do this not just to vent their dissatisfaction.
Going to the capital nowadays is probably to welcome bad guests.
Since they are bad guests, there is no need to be polite to them. Ye Shuo was very interested in this group of so-called envoys at first, but now, he suddenly finds them boring.
It would be better to go to other places in the capital to have some fun.
Look at the poor Minister of Rites, who is now haggling with the other party all the time, not knowing that even if he says something beautiful, the other party will still find fault with it.
“Forget it, forget it, let’s go.” Ye Shuo didn’t know the other party’s purpose, and he didn’t know whether his cheap father had other plans. Anyway, his cheap father would take care of it in the end, so he didn’t worry about it.
However, Ye Yan and his group, who were from Beiting and had seen a lot of such things at the border, were immediately angered by the other party’s behavior.
But when they thought about not causing trouble for their father, they became discouraged again.
“Okay, okay, don’t be unhappy. The ninth uncle will take you to some fun places.”
Ye Yan and the others finally followed Ye Shuo reluctantly.
Time passed by, and in the blink of an eye it was already late in the evening. After a morning and an afternoon of adjustment, the people of Beiting, who were already full of energy, had already recovered their spirits.
Seeing that the night banquet was about to begin, Huyan Jue boarded the carriage almost on time.
About half an hour later, when the carriage arrived at the gate of the imperial city, the guard almost subconsciously stretched out his hand to stop it: “Stop.”
Noticing that the eight people, including Hu Yanjue, all had scimitars on their waists, the guards could not help but say, “This is a restricted area of ​​the imperial city, and weapons are not allowed. Please take off your swords before entering.”
As if he had heard a joke, Hu Yanjue laughed loudly and patted the scimitar on his waist. Then his face changed and said, “It is a rule set by the Great Zhou Dynasty in the early years that our envoys are allowed to carry weapons. Who do you think you are? How dare you stop me?”
Hu Yanjue’s eyes were as sharp as knives.
The guards had never heard of such a rule, and they naturally did not dare to take the initiative because of the other party’s noble status. Finally, a captain surnamed Li, who was a seventh-rank officer, came over and ordered people to intercept the envoys outside. The guards quickly restored order. “I’m really sorry, I have never heard of such a rule in our Great Zhou. I will send someone to ask the emperor. Please wait here.” The captain surnamed Li was neither humble nor arrogant. He was polite, but his actions showed no intention of letting them in.
Huyan Jue wanted to get angry, but when he saw his move, the other party seemed to want to unsheathe his sword. Huyan Jue paused, narrowed his eyes, and smiled: “Little guard, you are so brave.”
The captain surnamed Li remained unmoved.
Hu Yanjue finally gave up. He crossed his arms and said, “Okay, I will wait here. I want to see if what the Great Zhou Emperor said before still counts.”
Emperor Jingwen soon learned about this matter, and he naturally also knew who made this rule.
No doubt it must be the late emperor.
The late emperor granted permission for envoys from Beiting to carry swords when entering the country in order to maintain diplomatic relations between the two countries.
Even Emperor Jingwen couldn’t openly disobey the late emperor so blatantly. His face was as gloomy as water and he nodded to the guard who came to report.
The guard then went back to report.
The captain surnamed Li received the order and then let them go.
“Pretending.” After taking a deep look at the other person, Huyan Jue sneered, and finally, under the watchful eyes of a group of guards, he swaggered into the imperial city with a sword in his hand.
Huyan Jue deliberately arrived a little late, and combined with the time he spent at the palace gate, by the time he arrived, the banquet was almost full, with only the eight of them waiting. This showed how much importance he attached to the event.
Although the Great Zhou won the battle, it was still so weak.
Huyan Jue bowed slightly towards Emperor Jingwen who was sitting at the top of the table as a greeting. Without even waiting for Emperor Jingwen to call him, he found his own seat and sat down.
Emperor Jingwen’s face darkened slightly, and the eldest prince and the crown prince were even more furious.
As for other ministers, most of them knew that Beiting was not easy to mess with, so no one said anything.
Just when Emperor Jingwen was about to express his dissatisfaction, he inadvertently saw that there seemed to be a few empty seats not far away.
Emperor Jingwen knew who was sitting in the empty seat without even having to think about it.
Emperor Jingwen was startled for a moment, then he felt relieved.
As for Hu Yanjue, not long after he sat down, he seemed to have just noticed his impoliteness. He said perfunctorily, “I am really sorry. I didn’t follow so many rules when I faced the Wolf King in Beiting. When I came here, I forgot about it for a moment. I hope that Emperor Zhou will forgive me.”
He kept asking for forgiveness, but his expression did not show much fear, as if he had already known in advance that Emperor Jingwen would not do anything to him.
However, just as he finished speaking, there was a sudden noise outside the Luanqing Palace.
Ye Shuo never thought that he had just been playing around, and had done nothing except drinking tea, eating, listening to operas, music, storytelling, shopping, etc., how could it be dark in the blink of an eye?
Seeing that the time for the night banquet was about to end, Ye Shuo was startled and ran to the palace in a hurry.
When he arrived, he was covered in sweat from running.
But thinking that those envoys didn’t look like guests at all, Ye Shuo didn’t care much. He was afraid that his cheap father would be angry, so after Ye Shuo rushed in, he hurriedly apologized to the envoys and then shifted all his attention to his cheap father.
“I’m sorry, I’m sorry. I’m late, but considering my young age, I think you won’t mind, right?”
Why does this sound so familiar?
It seems like I have heard it somewhere before.
Everyone’s attention inevitably shifted to Huyan Jue and his companions.
In an instant, Huyan Jue’s expression became extremely ugly.
Zou Wu and the others who had already taken their seats did not take this scene to heart. They were not interested in such things, and it was not their job, so Zou Wu and the others just watched at first.
Until they noticed the jade pendant hanging around the visitor’s waist.
The jade pendant is densely carved with various flowers, which are so eye-catching.
It was the first time they had seen such a fancy jade pendant, but that was fine. The key point was that surrounded by thousands of flowers, right in the center of the jade pendant, was a jade hairpin.
The one wearing the jade pendant with a jade hairpin flower around his waist is the mysterious master they have been thinking about all the time.
Zou Wu and the other eight young men were all stunned.
Having no time to pay attention to them, Ye Shuo only noticed that the moment he walked in, two pairs of eyes full of resentment suddenly fell on him.
One of the pairs was, as expected, the little princess’s. As for the other pair…
Looking at the four people following Ye Shuo, Ye Xun gritted his teeth.

chapters.title: Chapter 138: Ignore
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
It must be fake…
This thought flashed through the minds of Zou Wu and the other eight people at the same time.
However, before Ye Shuo came in, Zou Wu and her companions had already observed all the princes and nobles in the Luanqing Palace, even the concubines and princesses were not spared.
However, because valley patterns, snake patterns, coiled dragon patterns, etc. were popular in the Great Zhou Dynasty, flowers and plants did not seem so solemn, so few people chose them. Even if they did choose flowers and plants, they were mostly golden lotus, peony, and peony. The existence of Lilly valley flowers was pitifully rare.
Zou Wu and her friends searched around but couldn’t find him. At first, they wondered if their teacher hadn’t come at all.
Until the Ninth Prince appeared, the string of jade hairpins on the jade pendant on his waist was so eye-catching that it was difficult for Zou Wu and the other eight to ignore it.
No wonder Master Zeng was so confident before, saying that they could recognize people by their jade pendants.
Zou Wu and the others were still thinking that the jade pendant itself was not a very eye-catching thing, and the lily of the valley flower was even more ordinary. Even if there were eight of them, it might not be easy to identify them. What if they missed it?
As a result…it turned out that it was not a lily of the valley flower, but a bunch of lily of the valley flowers.With other gorgeous flowers guarding it, it is so eye-catching that you can see it almost at a glance.
The eyes of Zou Wu and the other eight people were wide open.
As if he had guessed what they were thinking, Ye Shuo looked down at the jade pendant on his waist and couldn’t help but have the urge to tease them. Then he took it off openly in front of everyone in Luanqing Palace, held the jade pendant in his hand and walked closer, shaking it in front of the eight people.
“These flowers were drawn by me personally, and I specially asked the people in the Ministry of Internal Affairs to spend half a year to carve them. Aren’t they particularly beautiful?”
The Ninth Prince must have piled up all the most beautiful flowers of all varieties in the Imperial Garden. Fortunately, the jade craftsmen employed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs have good skills, otherwise what a mess it would have been.
The jade pendant is hollow, with densely packed flowers on all sides, each more eye-catching than the other.
Not to mention Zou Wu and the other young men, even He Xiang and the others nearby were attracted by this thing when they looked over after hearing the Ninth Prince’s voice.
But the amazing thing is that such a fancy thing does not look out of place at all when worn by the Ninth Prince. The Ninth Prince’s face, which inherited all the good qualities of the Emperor and the Imperial Concubine and is now becoming more and more handsome, plays a significant role in this.
When ordinary people wear this thing, it is like matching cow dung with flowers, but when the Ninth Prince wears it, he is more beautiful than any other flower.
What a waste of such a good-looking face, how could you have such a temper?
They soon came to their senses and couldn’t help cursing in their hearts. The Grand Tutor and Lord Cen felt ashamed to face people and to admit that the Ninth Prince was their student.
Seeing that his son scared eight young men who had just arrived in Shangjing and made them change their faces in one breath, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but feel a headache.
Now, the four brothers Ye Yan are almost crying.
How could this Ninth Prince be so troublesome? On such an important day, he even dared to be late.
Being stared at by so many people in the hall, Ye Yan and his three companions, who usually prided themselves on being generous and unselfish, felt extremely uncomfortable.
Looking at Ye Shuo again, he seemed fine, still with his usual cheerful look.
Seeing Huyan Jue and the others’ increasingly ugly faces, Emperor Jingwen finally felt relieved.
After waiting for his son to show off enough, Emperor Jingwen slowly rebuked his son: “How can you behave in this hall? Go back to your seat!”
My cheap dad is really good at pretending. He didn’t say a word when he came in.
Ye Shuo thought so in his heart, but his expression immediately changed to one of submissive submission. He did not dare to refute at all. He put away the jade pendant and returned to his seat in dejection.
At this point, the ministers had a deeper understanding of how favoured the Ninth Prince was.
He was late for the state banquet and was let off with just a few words of reprimand without even a decent punishment. This was an honour that even the crown prince had never had, and only the ninth prince in the world had it.
Beside Emperor Jingwen, the Queen’s eyes changed.
However, even though it has come to this, there are still some people who are blind.
For example, when the uncle saw that his sister looked unhappy, he immediately said, “If I remember correctly, the Ninth Prince is already eleven years old. How come he is still so ignorant?”
“Since the Ninth Prince knew that the envoys would be coming today, he should have made preparations in advance. It would have been fine if it was a normal day, but how could he be late on such an important day? It is really wrong.”
The king’s uncle is the queen’s younger brother, and the queen is like a mother of all the princes and nation. Now the king’s uncle is acting like an elder.
If this happened before, there was nothing wrong with the old Duke Zhen when he was not favoured by Emperor Jingwen. Emperor Jingwen at that time would like to find faults even if there were none, and the actions of the uncle just suited his wishes.
But things are different now. Emperor Jingwen no longer has as much objection to the Duke of Zhen as he did before. Moreover, it would be strange for Emperor Jingwen to be happy when his uncle-in-law blames his son so easily.
As the saying goes, family disgrace should not be made public. Even if the Ninth Prince was wrong, he should not be spoken out on such an occasion. The King’s uncle has really brought shame upon himself.
He Xiang and other discerning people couldn’t help but shake their heads in their hearts.
However, before Emperor Jingwen could speak, the eldest prince spoke first: “Then according to your uncle’s opinion, what should we do if we are late?”
The uncle didn’t think too much about it and answered casually: “At the very least, they should reflect on their mistakes behind closed doors to correct the atmosphere.”
With a “dong” sound, the eldest prince put the wine glass on the table.
“In that case, according to what the uncle said, Yan’er and the others will also come along?”
The king’s uncle was stunned, and then he realised that the eldest prince’s group of sons seemed to be with the ninth prince, but the ninth prince was too ostentatious, causing others to ignore the grandchildren behind him.
“…That’s not what I meant.”
“My uncle, you may have drunk too much. If that’s the case, then just say less and don’t make a fool of yourself.” Others care about the queen, but the eldest prince doesn’t. The queen’s legitimate son is only a little old. It will never be his turn to take the position.
If the queen was safe and sound, the eldest prince might have given her some face, but the queen was obviously not safe and sound, so the eldest prince naturally would not take her seriously.
The series of scoldings from the eldest prince made the uncle’s face turn red. Seeing that he wanted to say something else, Emperor Jingwen’s patience was completely exhausted. Then he gave him a look and the uncle stopped talking on the spot.
After Ye Shuo sat down, looking at his expression that he had no idea he was doing anything wrong, Princess Jian Jian couldn’t help but put her hands on her hips and cursed, “Bad brother!”
Sure enough, what is meant to come will come.
It would have been fine if it was just Jianjian, but when Ye Shuo saw Ye Xun next door staring at him with a resentful look on his face, he felt even more uncomfortable.
Before Ye Xun could speak, Ye Shuo quickly said, “I called you first, but you didn’t want to go. You can’t blame me for this.”
After hearing this, Ye Xun didn’t feel comforted, but even more unhappy: “So I rejected you once, and you went to find them, right?”
What’s more, the other party was the eldest uncle’s son. Ye Xun suddenly felt particularly wronged.
“Before they came back, you only looked for me!”
hiss…
Why does this conversation sound weird?
Ye Shuo’s face was serious: “What else? You are so busy, I just want to find someone to accompany me, is there anything wrong with that? I don’t have any other thoughts, can you not be so petty?”
“I, I…” Is he really so petty?
As if he didn’t notice Ye Xun’s confusion, Ye Shuo continued, and he spoke more and more fluently: “Before, you insisted on playing with me, and when I really played with you, you said you didn’t have time. Don’t you think you are being too much and overbearing?”
No matter how smart Ye Xun was, he was only a seven-year-old kid. How could he withstand such rhetoric? He couldn’t stand it after a while.
Thinking about it, it was indeed he who broke the appointment first, Ye Xun was soon surrounded by guilt.
“I’m sorry, Uncle Nine, I shouldn’t have lost my temper with you just now…”
Ye Shuo nodded: “Well, it’s good that you know.”
“Although I am very angry, you are my closest nephew after all. For this reason, I will forgive you no matter what you do. Don’t act so unreasonably in the future, otherwise I will be sad.”
Ye Xun was so moved when he heard these words that he almost cried: “Ninth Uncle…”
“Cough, cough, cough!” The Crown Princess next to him couldn’t stand it anymore. She covered her lips with a handkerchief and coughed violently, then glared at her brother-in-law angrily.
What the hell is going on? Ye Xun can’t hear anything wrong, but how can the Crown Princess not hear it?
“You just bully him.”
Seeing that he was exposed by the Crown Princess at a glance, Ye Shuo blinked, quickly closed his mouth, and looked embarrassed.
As for what happened next, Ye Yan and the others had already pricked up their ears when Ye Xun opened his mouth.
Since the fathers of both sides don’t get along, it’s natural for the sons to follow suit.
Just like the eldest prince regards the crown prince as his biggest enemy, Ye Yan and the others can’t help but compare themselves with Ye Xun in everything.
Seeing that Ye Xun cared so much about the Ninth Uncle and even made a fuss if the Ninth Uncle didn’t take him out, Ye Yan and the other three immediately became excited.
Doesn’t this mean that if the four of them snatch the Ninth Prince away, then they would have won against Ye Xun in disguise?
But the Ninth Prince’s words “closest” are really an eyesore.
But it doesn’t matter, as long as they stay with the Ninth Prince, they will be the ones to be called the closest sooner or later.
Ye Yan and others, who were reluctant and felt extremely painful at first, suddenly changed their mindset.
Huyan Jue watched helplessly as the attention that was originally focused on him quickly dispersed after the Ninth Prince appeared. He waited for a long time but received no further news, and his face turned ashen.
Emperor Jingwen, who was sitting at the top of the table, seemed to have just noticed it and said, “My son is young and naughty. I’m sorry to have made you laugh.”
Even now that the seventeenth prince has been born, His Majesty still thinks that the ninth prince is the youngest son, as if the tenth to seventeenth princes did not exist.
The Queen could barely keep her expression.
Hu Yanjue snorted coldly: “It’s okay for the Ninth Prince, he is a prince, but the guards in this palace are really ignorant. If it were in our Beiting, a small guard would offend the royal family and his tendons would be cut off and dragged out to feed the wolves!”
Emperor Jingwen frowned, then looked at the commander-in-chief below him and asked, “Who is on duty at the gate of the imperial city today?”
The commander-in-chief called out the man’s name very fluently.
Ye Shuo’s ears twitched.
Hu Yanjue was certain of this, but before he could smile, he heard Emperor Jingwen speak, “Come here, give him a reward!”
Huyan Jue’s expression changed immediately.

chapters.title: Chapter 139: Dispute
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
“Emperor Zhou, may I ask what you mean? If I am not mistaken, Emperor Zhou is provoking my Beiting?”
He said he wanted to punish, but Emperor Jingwen insisted on rewarding him. What else could this be but a provocation?
Hu Yanjue showed his anger at the right moment.
“How could that be? Your Highness must have misunderstood Father. The guard followed the rules and should be rewarded.”
“What is your Majesty thinking about?”
It would be too cheap for Emperor Jingwen to personally engage in a witticism, so without waiting for Emperor Jingwen to speak, the crown prince next to him looked embarrassed and spoke first: “I have heard that people in Beiting are generous and open-minded, but after meeting the prince today, I feel that the rumours are really not to be believed.”
It’s different from Beiting’s usual style to care about such a small matter.
Although Emperor Jingwen could not openly ignore the words of the late emperor, it was not difficult for him to show his true intentions.
With just one word of reward, Hu Yanjue’s face was immediately humiliated.Then the prince continued, “It is true that most people in Beiting are not so particular, but the prince is too impatient now. Also, the prince has been dissatisfied with every aspect of our Great Zhou since he set foot in Shangjing City. If we talk about provocation, the prince is more appropriate. It makes people wonder whether the purpose of the prince’s trip is really to seek peace.”
The prince paused and said, “Or was it the Wolf King who told the prince to act this way?”
[1] Calling huyan jue as prince is just for ‘respect’ as he is the uncle of the emperor there, so calling him as prince or his highness or something…
Da Zhou is afraid of Bei Ting, so how could Bei Ting not be afraid of Da Zhou?
Especially since Beiting has been without water and food for several months, it is already at the end of its strength. If this weakness is discovered, Da Zhou will definitely join forces with Chen State, and Beiting will be in danger then.
As the prince’s words became more and more profound, Huyan Jue became more and more alert.
However, just before the window paper was about to be broken, the prince stopped at the right time, and changed the subject, saying: “Of course, it is also possible that the prince himself has such an impulsive and irritable personality. If so, it is understandable.”
The prince’s meaning was very clear. Either there was something wrong with Beiting itself, or there was something wrong with Huyan Jue himself. In any case, just choose one.
Hu Yanjue definitely can’t choose the one in front, so…
Ye Shuo had never known before that his third brother was so eloquent. Look how angry he made the messenger, his face turned green.
“…The people of the Great Zhou are indeed sharp-tongued.”
Huyan Jue was naturally no match for his verbal rival. From his peripheral vision he noticed the eldest prince not far away, and in a flash, Huyan Jue came up with a vicious plan.
Hu Yanjue’s tense brows suddenly relaxed.
Seeing the other party’s behavior, Ye Shuo instinctively felt bad. Sure enough, the next moment Hu Yanjue said, “It’s just that I don’t want to deal with a weak prince like you. My Beiting has always valued the strong. Your highness, the eldest prince, defeated us and took the head of General Lanruo, the most powerful general in Beiting. Among all the princes, I only respect the eldest prince. What’s the point of you saying more?”
The envoy from Beiting did not even know who the Crown Prince of Da Zhou was. Huyan Jue pretended to be serious and deliberately blurred the Crown Prince’s name with that of an imperial prince, pretending as if he could not recognize the Crown Prince. He really deserves death!
Anyone who hears this will feel hurt, even if they know the other person did it on purpose.
Even though the prince was very well-mannered, his expression froze for a moment when he heard that.
Since the eldest prince came back, the court affairs have been tense. Ye Shuo has always been worried that the crown prince and the eldest prince will fight one day. Although he knows that day will come sooner or later, Ye Shuo still hopes to delay it for a day.
Now Hu Yanjue had come up with this move out of the blue, which had hit upon what Ye Shuo was most worried about. How could Ye Shuo not be annoyed?
… Damn it!
Ye Shuo failed to control his strength and the teacup in his hand was crushed to pieces. With a “bang”, Ye Shuo slammed the cup heavily on the table in front of him.
He moved so quickly that no one noticed that the cup broke before it touched the table. Even the pointy little princess who was closest to it only saw a daze before she saw the cup being smashed to pieces by her brother.
Ye Shuo’s sudden outburst stunned everyone in Luanqing Palace.
The anger in his eyes faded away like the tide in an instant, and Ye Shuo leaned back to conceal his anger. In the eyes of everyone, he showed the familiar cynical look.
Although he was furious, Ye Shuo still had a playful smile on his face: “This prince doesn’t even know the Crown Prince of my Great Zhou, and he can be an envoy. This really opens my eyes.”
“If he can do it, then I can do it too. After all, we are all related and got promoted through connections, so there is no difference.”
“Since Prince Huyan doesn’t even have this basic quality, I think, Father, we should talk to the Wolf King and see if we can send a different envoy. Anyway, there’s nothing much to talk about with this one, so there’s no point wasting time.”
The moment the words fell, the entire Luanqing Palace was in an uproar.
The Ninth Prince has such a vicious mouth that he could even say such words.
These two people are indeed in the same group. The other party just said that, and the Ninth Prince became anxious. The eldest prince couldn’t help but snort in his heart, but he was not surprised.
However, the Sixth Prince couldn’t help but look at Ye Shuo again and again.
As expected, Xiao Jiu was still closer to the Crown Prince. The Sixth Prince lowered his eyes.
Wow, the Ninth Prince is so awesome! The Ninth Prince is indeed on their side! Ye Xun’s face turned red with joy.
Xiaojiu…
The prince was stunned, feeling somewhat complicated.
Being scolded by a child like this, Hu Yanjue felt embarrassed and angry: “At a banquet between two countries, how can a child like you speak so freely? Is this the way of hospitality in the Great Zhou Dynasty?”
Ye Shuo sneered: “Your Highness, you may have forgotten that this is the Luanqing Palace of my Great Zhou. The person sitting on it is my biological father, and you are standing on the land of my Great Zhou. As a prince, I am naturally more qualified than you.”
In terms of momentum, Ye Shuo will not lose to anyone.
He is not even afraid of Emperor Jingwen, so how could he be afraid of a mere prince from another country?
He Xiang and others watched helplessly as the Ninth Prince, who was only eleven years old, and Hu Yanjue, who was almost fifty years old, argued with each other until they were red in the face.
Even though Huyan Jue’s eyes were almost popping out, the child in front of him did not calm down. In the end, Huyan Jue was so angry that he almost drew his sword.
Emperor Jingwen had seen the little bastard act like a rogue before, so even if the palace servants around him made a mistake, as long as it was not a big deal, he would basically just laugh it off.
This is the first time I’ve had such a big argument with someone.
Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but feel emotional, he really had deep feelings for the prince.
Emperor Jingwen was of course happy that his most valued son and his most beloved son had such a good relationship, but he could not allow them to continue like this.
If we keep arguing like this, there will be no end even if we continue arguing until tomorrow.
Not to mention Emperor Jingwen, even Zou Wu and others who were sitting opposite were caught off guard by such a scene.
The Ninth Prince doesn’t look like their teacher at all. In their eyes, anyone who can write something that would amaze even the gods must be strong, mature, and steady.
Let’s look at the Ninth Prince again. How does he relate to the above description?
He’s clearly just a little kid caught up in a fight.
However, the jade pendant with lily flowers on the waist of this little kid was so dazzling that it hurt people’s eyes.
After hesitating for a long time, when the two sides paused, Zou Wu took this opportunity to make a quick decision and immediately walked out of the team.
“Your Majesty, we, the common people, have a treasure to present to you.”
Since the emperor had specifically asked them to bring honour to the Zhou Dynasty, they couldn’t just sit there and act as mascots, right?
They had to come up with something.
After much deliberation, the eight people finally made something during the seven or eight days when the envoy was here.
The teacher had explained the drawings of this thing to them before, and they understood it at that time. Now they just had to restore it.
Emperor Jingwen was just worrying about how to start the conversation, but when he saw Zou Wu standing up, he just went with the flow and nodded.
He wanted to see what tricks the Great Zhou was planning.
Huyan Jue thought this in his heart while sitting there panting.
Soon, an object covered with red cloth was pushed up.
This shape…
Ye Shuo was stunned for a moment, and had a vague premonition in his heart.
After a moment, Zou Wu personally lifted the red cloth.
If the so-called treasure is not the Divine Arm Crossbow, one of the top cold weapons, then what is it?
These people actually got this thing out.

chapters.title: Chapter 140: Wandering
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {240+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
The Shenbi Crossbow, also known as the Shenbi Bow, was invented by Li Hong during the reign of Emperor Shenzong of the Northern Song Dynasty. The bow is three feet and three inches long, with a string two feet and five inches long. Its maximum range is over four hundred metres. It is equipped with a mechanism, so even though the Shenbi Bow is heavy, it can be fired by one person. Its power can even penetrate heavy armour, which made the Jin army at that time terrified.
According to historical records, the Shenbi bow could still shoot half an arrow into an elm tree at a distance of more than 240 steps, or more than 300 metres. This shows its lethality.
However, in modern times, the production method and design drawings of the Shenbi crossbow have long been lost. Although the one restored by some cold weapon enthusiasts later is also called the Shenbi bow, only Li Hong himself knows whether it is the same as the one in the Song Dynasty.
However, this power is not far from the historical records, so whether it is true or false is not important.
After everyone in the hall had seen it clearly, Zou Wu clasped his fists and said, “This place is too small to use this bow. Your Majesty, please come to the front of the hall and take a look.”
This little girl is quite courageous. The Luanqing Palace is a state banquet venue that is only used for major events. It is quite grand and huge, but in her mouth it becomes small.
What’s more, she actually spoke up and asked Emperor Jingwen to move the imperial carriage, which was extremely rude.
“Bold!”
At the night banquet, someone immediately shouted it out.On the other hand, He Xiang and the others remained silent, and no one knew what they were thinking about.
The young girl had good intentions, but they had never mentioned this matter before. Also, because they were young and they had polished and assembled the wood themselves, Emperor Jingwen did not expect that they would be able to make a crossbow in just a few days.
It would be fine if this thing was useful, but if it is useless, it will backfire.
The decision soon fell into the hands of Emperor Jingwen. Without much hesitation, he immediately said, “Come here, prepare the carriage.”
Emperor Jingwen decided to do as they said and go outside the palace to take a look.
Huyan Jue narrowed his eyes and began to speculate in his heart, wondering what kind of medicine the Great Zhou was trying to sell.
Soon, as Emperor Jingwen walked down from the chair above, the other Prime Ministers He and others followed him.
Now everyone’s attention is on Zou Wu. The youngest one, Lu Mu, pretended to be nervous and deliberately slowed down by two steps.
Then, he happened to meet Ye Shuo who was also walking out at the palace gate.
Lu Mu opened his mouth: “Your Highness the Ninth Prince…”
It’s over, it’s over, it’s over. What should I say now?
How can I know if he is the teacher I think of?
Just when Lu Mu was struggling, Ye Shuo over there seemed to see what he was thinking at the moment. Ye Shuo looked straight ahead and said something that could be considered a wise saying, but no one in the modern world could understand it.
“Odds change but evens don’t; the sign depends on the quadrant.”
Ye Shuo had wanted to try this kind of excitement of secret codes for a long time, and it was not until today that his dream came true.
However, compared to Ye Shuo, Lu Mu’s mood was much more complicated.
He had his head down, and because of his young age and short stature, no one even noticed that he had made a sound. After hearing these words, Lu Mu lowered his body even more, and no one noticed the turbulent emotions in his heart at this moment.
Naturally, no one knew that after hearing the Ninth Prince say such a thing, Lu Mu almost went crazy.
It was actually him! !
Lu Mu dared to guarantee that, apart from their own people, no one else in the Great Zhou Dynasty would know this sentence, “Odds change but evens do not change, and the sign depends on the quadrant.”
Add to that the jade pendant with lily of the valley, and the answer becomes very clear.
The person who could invent such concise and clear Arabic numerals, who was familiar with so many principles and formulas, such a unique person in the history, was actually… still a child! !
His fantasy was shattered, and Lu Mu’s face facing the ground suddenly became distorted.
However, Ye Shuo acted as if nothing had happened. After saying those words, he walked away as if nothing had happened, without caring at all about the huge waves rising in other people’s hearts.
In the blink of an eye, the two passed each other.
After everyone was outside the hall, Lu Mu followed behind and caught up with the main group in a daze.
‘how?’
When Zou Wu saw him coming, she subconsciously looked at him inquiringly.
Lu Mu took a deep breath, then nodded calmly.
Now it was already dark outside, and other people couldn’t see it, but how could Zou Wu and the others, who were closest to Lu Mu, not see it? Under that seemingly calm appearance, there was a look that seemed to be about to break in the next moment.
Zou Wu couldn’t help but feel dizzy.
At this time, Emperor Jingwen finally spoke: “Now that everyone is here, when will it start?”
Zou Wu quickly came back to his senses, and then said, “Please allow Your Majesty to send someone to take out the box from the drawer on the right hand side of my room.”
No weapons were allowed into the palace, so arrows were naturally included in that category.
Fortunately, Zou Wu and her family now live at the foot of the imperial city, so it doesn’t take much time to go back and forth.
Emperor Jingwen could not help but look at the commander-in-chief beside him. The commander-in-chief understood what he meant and called on a few guards to act according to his instructions.
In addition, Zou Wu also needs a target.
It was definitely too late to build a wall now, so Zou Wu pointed to the screen wall in the distance and said with a slightly embarrassed look, “Your Majesty, this crossbow is very powerful. I’m afraid it will destroy the screen wall later. I hope Your Majesty will not blame me.”
If the wall could really be destroyed, Emperor Jingwen would be so happy that he would not blame anyone.
So Emperor Jingwen said: “Just do what you want.”
Haha, it’s just a mystery.
In terms of horse riding and archery, Beiting was the strongest among the three countries, and the other two countries combined were no match for Beiting. Hu Yanjue, who was standing aside, wanted to see what the emperor of the Great Zhou was up to.
Soon the guards brought the box over. When the box was opened, as expected, there were five or six arrows inside.
The arrows were just ordinary arrows, and there didn’t seem to be anything special about them.
Only the crossbow arrow held by Zou Wu had a peculiar shape. I guess the novelty lies entirely in this crossbow arrow.
And although it is called a crossbow, it is actually more like a bow, and the opening and closing movements are also the same as a bow.
As the arrows arrived, several targets were also in place.
Among the children who grew up at the border, the weak ones had died long ago, and those who stayed behind, even the girls, were stronger than ordinary people.
In full view of everyone, Zou Wu pulled the bowstring open, and when the bowstring was pulled to a perfect length, Zou Wu aimed at the bull’s eye not far away, and then quickly let go.
With a “whoosh” sound, a sound of breaking through the air was heard. Everyone felt a flash before their eyes, and then a black dot appeared on the target.
It was dark now, and visibility was poor, even with lanterns lit, no one paid any attention to it at first. Hu Yanjue and the other eight people thought that this so-called treasure was just so-so.
It was not until the guards came forward to check that everyone discovered the clue.
It turned out that the arrow did not hit the target, but passed through the target and was nailed firmly on the screen wall!
The guards searched for a while but couldn’t find the arrow. Later, with the reminder of the young eunuch next to them, they saw the arrow nailed to the screen wall.
The arrow had now been mostly sunken, with only a section of the tail feathers sticking out, so the guards did not discover it in time.
Seeing this scene, a chill finally passed through everyone’s hearts.
It is recorded in the History of Song Dynasty: Biography of Xia State (Volume 1) that Tuoba Sizhong once shot an arrow at an iron crane, destroying its feathers.
Compared to such records, the power of the thing Zou Wu is holding in his hand now is still a little lacking.
But it’s eye-catching enough.
Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but clap his hands and blurted out: “Good!”
Ever since he learned about these eight people, Emperor Jingwen’s impression of them has changed again and again.
If Emperor Jingwen viewed them as talented young men before, now he sees them as people who can be used.
However, this was not the end. Zou Wu continued, “This arrow is made of ordinary iron. If it is replaced with fine steel, its power will increase by another three points.”
It could actually rise further? Emperor Jingwen was shocked.
only……
“What is this fine steel?” asked Emperor Jingwen.
Zou Wu gave a rough explanation, and the more Emperor Jingwen listened, the brighter his eyes became. Finally, he even asked anxiously, “Is it possible to forge it now?”
If you touch things like ironware and iron ore in private, you will lose your head, even if you are as special as Zeng Mohuai.
Therefore, Zou Wu only learned some methods, and the specific implementation still needs further research.
But now that there is another teacher here, it shouldn’t be a problem.
Zou Wu’s eyes could not help but slide across the Ninth Prince’s face. Seeing that he seemed to be smiling, the familiar feeling gave Zou Wu a sudden boost of confidence. His mind got heated, so he spoke decisively: “Of course.”
“Not only that, this crossbow can also be made into a crossbow cart and used for attacking cities and conquering land.”
Ye Shuo’s expression suddenly became stiff.
Hey, hey, hey, don’t take on such a job. It’s not that easy to make steel and convert a crossbow into a ballista.
They make it sound too easy.
However, Zou Wu and others were thinking that it would not be difficult for the teacher anyway. If he really was that person, then this little thing would definitely not be a problem.
Moreover, if the teacher is really a prince, the current situation will naturally be as beneficial to Da Zhou as possible.
After thinking about it, Zou Wu couldn’t help but said loudly: “This crossbow is called the Divine Arm Crossbow. The eight of us specially present this crossbow to His Majesty. Long live the emperor.”
The teacher’s father was their master’s master. Thinking of this relationship, Zou Wu respectfully presented the bow and crossbow in his hands with both hands.
Divine Arm Crossbow? What a good name.
He Xiang and his men followed closely behind: “Long live the emperor!”
Only envoys such as Huyan Jue were left standing there with sullen faces.
As Zou Wu spoke more and more, Hu Yanjue’s expression next to her became more and more unsightly.
Bows and crossbows are the most effective against cavalry, and weapons with long range and high lethality are even more effective. The Great Zhou suddenly has such a treasure. If it is used in the army, Beiting will definitely be in trouble.
They were the ones who solved the flood before, and they were the ones who presented the treasures afterwards. Zeng Mohuai was so hateful. If Zeng Mohuai came to Beiting next time, Hu Yanjue would definitely make this old man die on the spot!
After the treasure presentation, Emperor Jingwen was obviously in a much better mood, and the songs and dances that had been prepared before were quickly arranged.
There were all beauties, not even one ugly musician. However, how could Hu Yanjue be in the mood to enjoy the singing and dancing at this moment? He was so worried that he was dying.
However, the mountains and miasma of Chen State were not easy to deal with. Hu Yanjue still found it difficult to make a decision, so he could only pretend to be relaxed and said, “It’s just a show.”
From what he saw and heard along the way after he came to Da Zhou, it can be seen that most people in Da Zhou are still afraid of Beiting.
The source of the fear was the fact that Beiting had captured seven cities of the Great Zhou and massacred people in those seven cities.
