The eldest prince stared at them intently, noticing the respect and obedience in their eyes, and suddenly an incredible thought popped up in his mind –
Maybe it wasn’t a betrayal, but rather that they had been the emperor’s people from the very beginning.
Emperor Jingwen would not make the same mistake as the Duke of Zhen a second time, and would not allow others to threaten him again, even if that person was his own son. Therefore, anyone who holds a large number of troops would never be able to sit in that position.
However, when Emperor Jingwen first ascended the throne, there was no one else to choose from. Since one of them was destined to be sacrificed, he had no choice but to give up with great reluctance.
Emperor Jingwen had already made a choice between his two sons, the eldest prince and the crown prince, and even paved the way for the crown prince.
It’s a pity that the crown prince didn’t persist to this point and collapsed halfway.
It turned out that everything the eldest prince had was nothing but a castle in the air. The seemingly magnificent building actually collapsed in a matter of a moment.
From beginning to end, the eldest prince was just a tool used by Emperor Jingwen to fight for military power.

chapters.title: Chapter 209: Distortion
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {330+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
What on earth am I?
A chess piece to be played by others, or a stepping stone for the crown prince?
The eldest prince suddenly felt that everything before his eyes was ridiculous.
But in fact, Emperor Jingwen was not completely without love for the eldest prince. After the assassination and the death of the crown prince, Emperor Jingwen’s health became worse and worse, and his heart was not as cold and hard as before.
Perhaps because of his age, Emperor Jingwen has begun to cherish feelings and feels that he is not as ruthless as he was when he was young.
Otherwise, based on what the eldest prince had done during the month when he was missing, Emperor Jingwen would not have stayed until now, and would not have given the eldest prince two full chances through this assassination.
But unfortunately, the eldest prince disappointed him in the end.
If the eldest prince had made the right choice once, Emperor Jingwen would have turned a blind eye to it because he had fought on the battlefield for the Great Zhou for ten years, and the matter would have been over.
Emperor Jingwen allowed his son to have ambitions, but he did not allow such ambitions to be mixed with rebellious intentions.It is naturally impossible for tiger cubs to be vegetarians, but they also cannot compete for food in the tiger’s mouth. They must wait until the tiger is full before they can take their turn.
General Xu and General Fang have been with the eldest prince for more than ten years. The eldest prince trusts them very much, so he is not on guard. If they are not trustworthy, then the eldest prince will really have no one he can trust.
So when Emperor Jingwen asked the eldest prince to serve as the escort for this trip, the eldest prince did not think that this was a trap.
Even though the crown prince was dead, Emperor Jingwen never relaxed his vigilance for a moment. He was heartbroken, but he kept silent.
Being stared at like this by the eldest prince, General Xu and General Fang could not even raise their heads.
They felt somewhat guilty towards the eldest prince. After all, they had been at the border for ten years, and their friendship was not fake.
But as subjects, they are only loyal to His Majesty. If the eldest prince is against someone else, they will definitely help him. But if the eldest prince is against His Majesty… they have no choice.
Their power is granted by the emperor, so they are loyal to him.
Emperor Jingwen finally gave the eldest prince a last bit of face and did not let his embarrassing side show in front of others. After Emperor Jingwen ordered the secret guards to capture the thirteenth prince, the queen, and the people around the queen, he quickly drove everyone out, including Ye Shuo.
The handkerchief in Concubine De’s hand was about to be twisted into pieces, but she dared not make a sound. Although she didn’t know what had happened, looking at the expression of the emperor, she was sure that the eldest brother must have committed a serious crime.
Concubine De was an old lady who had served Emperor Jingwen. She understood the emperor’s temper and knew that if she gave him random advice without knowing the situation clearly, it would not only fail to work, but might even add fuel to the fire.
No matter how worried she was, she was forced to leave.
The Eighth Prince, who had just been protected by the First Prince, was still confused. Naturally, he didn’t know that the First Prince had deliberately let the assassins in twice.
“Father…” The Eighth Prince was about to speak when he saw the First Prince gently shaking his head at him.
The Eighth Prince reacted instantly. He hesitated for a while, but in the end he dared not say another word.
In a moment, Emperor Jingwen and the eldest prince were the only two people left in the dining hall.
Now the eldest prince was doomed and had no strength to struggle. He stood there and struggled violently for a long time. Before Emperor Jingwen looked over, he fell heavily to his knees with a plop.
Emperor Jingwen also clenched his hands holding the Buddhist beads.
After all, the eldest prince was his first grown-up son, so how could Emperor Jingwen have no fatherly feelings for him?
The eldest prince also knew that the two things he had done in succession were not tolerated by his father. If he could not come up with a solution, he would definitely end up like the second prince.
Not only will he lose his throne as a prince, but even his children, wives and concubines will be demoted to commoners, and his descendants will never be able to enter the centre of power again.
And now the only thing he can show off is his ability to fight.
It’s ridiculous to say that I have been targeted for this reason for a long time, but now I have to rely on this ability to find a way to survive for my wife, concubines and children.
Trying hard to suppress the sadness in his heart, the eldest prince knelt at the feet of Emperor Jingwen with cold sweat.
“I know I am guilty. I dare not ask for forgiveness from you, my father. I only ask you to give me a chance to atone for my sins.”
“Beiting is so arrogant that he assassinated the emperor, framed the prince, and instigated the queen’s son to cause chaos in the government. His crimes are extremely heinous and unforgivable. I, your son, will go to the battle and will not return unless I die.”
The eldest prince was extremely decisive and his meaning was very clear. He was willing to use his own life in exchange for the survival of his wives, concubines and children.
At the end, the eldest prince could only beg.
“I know I shouldn’t expect things I don’t deserve, but this son’s offspring are innocent. I only ask for mercy from your Majesty. Don’t expel Yan’er and the others from the capital. Leave them a way out.”
Unlike the second prince, the eldest prince has been fighting outside for many years, and the generals of the Beiting royal family hate him to the core. Without the protection of Emperor Jingwen, once Ye Yan and his children lose power and are expelled from the capital, they will definitely die.
How many people in this world can really not care about their own children?
Emperor Jingwen remained silent for a long time.
Just when the eldest prince was getting extremely nervous, perhaps he was not destined to die, as a message suddenly came from Wu Yi outside.
“Your Majesty, an army has secretly gathered at the border of Beiting. There seems to be some unusual movement. I am here to report this.”
If the Great Zhou is really in chaos this time, now is a good opportunity to attack it.
Even if they could not completely take over the Great Zhou, they could still cooperate with their princesses from both inside and outside, attack from both sides, force the officials of the Great Zhou to compromise, and push the puppet Thirteenth Prince of their choice to the throne, so as to achieve the goal of controlling the Great Zhou.
The eldest prince’s gaze became more and more urgent.
Emperor Jingwen was silent for a while, and finally waved his hand weakly, which was considered as… letting the eldest prince go.
Emperor Jingwen now has too many people at his disposal, and with General Xu and General Fang in the past, the eldest prince will never be able to trust the people around him.
The eldest prince is no longer capable of causing any trouble. The only fate that awaits him is to die on the battlefield.
If his achievements are great enough, Ye Yan and his brothers can be saved. If he is passive and lazy and deliberately delays military intelligence, Ye Yan and his brothers will die.
Knowing that his father always keeps his word, the eldest prince has no choice but to try his best to fight for a future for his descendants.
Despite this, the eldest prince still wanted to express his gratitude.
“Thank you for your grace, father. May you live long, may you live long.”
Born into the royal family, the king is the king, the ministers are the ministers, the father is the father, and the son is the son. Once you sit in this position, no one can escape, and your hands will be covered in blood until you die.
As the saying goes, it’s lonely at the top. After being an emperor for too long, he gradually became a lonely man, and all he could see were power and benefits.
After the eldest prince left, he looked at the devastation in the dining hall and thought of the fourth prince who had died in vain. From the crown prince to now, including the thirteenth prince, Emperor Jingwen had lost five sons in a row, four of whom he had placed high hopes on. In addition to this position under him, Emperor Jingwen had also made arrangements for them.
Seeing his children dying one after another, even Emperor Jingwen could not bear it any longer.
The despair of the crown prince, the pleading of the eldest prince, the questioning of the second prince, the tears shed by his words, and the confused eyes of the fourth prince all flashed before Emperor Jingwen’s eyes one after another. Emperor Jingwen’s body shook, and he felt a sweetness in his throat and spat out a mouthful of blood.
When Ye Shuo outside heard Eunuch Wang’s urgent call, he came to the dining hall and saw his stepfather collapsed.
The other side.
Princess Huyan never imagined that the old emperor of the Great Zhou was already prepared.
When she saw the leader of the Iron Guard, she knew that her plan had been seen through by the old emperor. When the old emperor left Shangjing, he had already arranged troops in advance and was preparing to catch them in a trap!
What illness? It was just a play arranged by the old emperor.
Princess Huyan saw that her soldiers had failed to break through the commander’s encirclement after several charges, and more and more people were rushing around. She knew that it was impossible to do anything, so she gritted her teeth and said, “Retreat!”
It will be too late if you don’t leave now!
As for the palace, Princess Huyan had already arranged people. Now there was a fire in the palace where she lived. When the fire was out, no one would be able to identify who was inside.
How could Princess Huyan let her best years be wasted in the harem of the old emperor of the Great Zhou?
The old emperor was really cruel, locking Princess Huyan up for so many years. She was no longer as pretty and graceful as before, and now she looked haggard and her body had already decayed.
And all of these were the work of the old emperor.
But the old emperor didn’t know that even if he was imprisoned and not allowed to see outsiders, what would happen? His son came to her without her even asking him to do so. She just said a few nice words and he did whatever she asked. He was more obedient than a dog.
But now that the plan has been exposed, the old emperor’s son is probably going to die.
Princess Huyan was furious when her years of planning were shattered.
When Princess Huyan led her men to evacuate towards Beiting, not long after, they received news that the Shenyin Guards at Zilu Peak had been wiped out by the Great Zhou’s secret guards.
The person who delivered the message hesitated for a moment and asked, “Should we still send someone to rescue the little prince?”
After all, this is the chess piece they have cultivated for so many years. It would be a pity to give up just like that.
However, Princess Huyan did not hesitate at all: “Why save him?”
“He’s just a piece of trash. If he dies, he dies. Why make such a fuss?”
Princess Huyan’s tone was extremely cold, and she treated the child she had watched grow up as casually as if she were throwing away a piece of waste paper.
This was the case when Princess Huyan was in the Beiting royal court, and the people under her command did not find it strange at all.
Princess Huyan was so busy that she had no time to care about the life or death of a useless person.
Princess Huyan felt a slight stomachache while walking. At first, she thought it was because she was in poor health and too tired from the journey, so she didn’t take it seriously.
However, as she walked, the abdominal pain not only did not go away, but became more severe.
Seeing that the land and grassland of Beiting were already within reach, after several days of fermentation, Princess Huyan felt so heartbroken that she couldn’t even get on her horse.
In the end, Princess Huyan died only a few dozen miles away from the Beiting territory.
She was almost able to go home.
Princess Huyan treated the Thirteenth Prince as her own dog, but she forgot that dogs can also bite people.
Those who have humiliated him will die, and those who have deceived him will also die.
If it succeeds, she will die. If it fails, and he dies, she will die even more.
Besides, she should be happy that she could die for him.
Since she keeps saying that she can die for me, then let her die.

chapters.title: Chapter 210: Establishing a Crown Prince
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {330+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
“Father! Father!”
The noise in the dining hall was also heard, and soon all the princes and concubines gathered there.
Wu Yi’s eagle eyes kept scanning the group of people in front of him to prevent anyone from taking the opportunity to commit murder.
This is what it’s like to be an emperor. You have to be cautious at everything, always sober and alert, because you never know if the person standing in front of you is plotting to kill you.
After a while, the imperial physician and the abbot of Bailu Temple arrived one after another.
Both of them are top doctors, and they can see that Emperor Jingwen is in bad condition.
While taking Emperor Jingwen’s pulse, Wu Yi once again drove everyone out and forbade them to approach.
After all, she and Emperor Jingwen had been married for many years, so Concubine Rong was naturally worried when she saw this, but she couldn’t show it. Now that the queen was imprisoned, Concubine Rong was the highest-ranking among all the people present. If even she panicked, the palace people below would probably be in chaos.
So no matter how nervous the imperial concubine was inside, she always looked calm.As his cheap father fell, Ye Shuo’s head began to throb with pain.
In his heart, although his stepfather could not be compared with his father at all, twenty years had passed and one should have developed feelings for a cat or a dog, let alone a grown-up person.
There are so many truths and lies between him and his stepfather, and it is hard to tell what is going on.
Because of his stepfather’s identity as the emperor, Ye Shuo believed that although he would never be able to be defenseless and treat him wholeheartedly, ultimately, Ye Shuo did not want him to die.
It would be great if everyone could survive, but it’s a pity that no matter who it is, they will end up in this situation sooner or later.
The cruelty of God lies in the fact that those who experience birth, ageing, sickness and death can only watch helplessly.
While waiting, the matter of the Fourth Prince also needs to be dealt with.
When the Sixth Prince first entered the Six Ministries, he was personally guided by the Fourth Prince. Whether it was deliberate attempts to win him over or for other reasons, the Fourth Prince’s body has not yet been buried, and the Sixth Prince cannot turn a blind eye.
Even though the Fourth Prince had the same goal as him, and the two of them eventually turned from brothers into enemies, since both were dead, the Sixth Prince naturally wouldn’t care so much.
When a person dies, it is like a lamp going out, and all the past will eventually disappear.
But the Sixth Prince still has a son to take care of, and Ye Jin is weak, so the Sixth Prince dare not ask anyone else to do it. The situation is chaotic right now, so he is naturally worried about his only son.
But if I take him with me… Ye Jin is still young after all, and I’m afraid that coming into contact with the dead will scare him.
The Sixth Prince was hesitating, but when he turned around, he saw that his son had fallen into Xiaojiu’s hands again.
Xiaojiu’s method of stealing children has become more and more sophisticated.
Seeing that Xiao Jiu was holding him, his son felt that the atmosphere around him was not right, so he didn’t dare to make a fuss. His little face turned red, and he kept whispering in resistance: “Uncle Jiu, put me down!”
Oh my god, who would hug someone so casually like him!
However, Ye Jin’s rejection was like tickling, and soon, under Ye Shuo’s suppression, the child could not move.
As if noticing his gaze, Ye Shuo said casually: “Go if you want to, I’m here.”
Although Xiaojiu liked to make trouble, he didn’t have any bad intentions. The Sixth Prince paused, then clasped his fists, and quickly helped Concubine Xian to deal with the Fourth Prince’s affairs.
Fortunately, it is winter now and the mountains are cold, so there is no need to ask people to transport ice up.
Concubine Xian was so grief-stricken that she could not control herself, but because of the matter concerning Emperor Jingwen, she could not cry out loud. Now that the Sixth Prince had arrived, Concubine Xian felt a little relieved.
Perhaps it was because the Fourth Prince looked too scary with his eyes open. The palace servants around him were all trembling with fear, and their hearts were filled with terror.
The Sixth Prince took a deep breath, stretched out his hand, and slowly closed the Fourth Prince’s eyelids.
At this point, the life of the Fourth Prince finally came to an end.
The other side.
Inside the room, the imperial physician and the abbot tried their best to give Emperor Jingwen medicine and acupuncture. During this time, Wang Ziquan and others came and went, bringing in seven or eight bowls of medicine alone. The whole Bailu Temple was filled with a strong smell of medicine.
However, even so, it took three full hours, and it was almost dawn before Emperor Jingwen was rescued.
“How is my health?”
Just when the imperial physician and the abbot were struggling with how to tell the princes and concubines outside, they heard a hoarse voice coming from behind them.
It turned out that Emperor Jingwen, who in their eyes would be in a coma for at least three days, woke up early.
Normally, if one encounters such a serious situation, it would take at least two or three days before one can gradually regain consciousness. But now, Emperor Jingwen opened his eyes in less than half a day, which shows how strong his heart is.
The imperial physician knelt down and saluted without hesitation. As for the abbot standing beside him, he clasped his hands together and chanted “Amitabha”.
The imperial physician couldn’t help but look at the other person.
The abbot is a highly accomplished monk who is not involved in worldly affairs. Emperor Jingwen granted him special permission that he does not need to kneel when meeting the emperor, and his status is transcendent. But it is different for the imperial physician. Whenever something goes wrong with the emperor, the imperial physician will certainly not be in good shape, and his family may even be implicated.
In this situation, how could the imperial physician have the courage to speak?
Although the abbot was not a secular person, he was not completely ignorant of the secular world. He sighed in his heart and then said, “Amitabha, in reply to the emperor’s words, the emperor was stabbed last time and his heart meridian was injured. If he hadn’t met a master to treat him, I’m afraid his life would be in danger.”
Fortunately, Emperor Jingwen received timely treatment as soon as he was injured, otherwise he would not have survived until now.
“Although His Majesty has recovered from his injuries, he still has roots. He should avoid extreme joy, sorrow, or anger. If he does this too often, his life may be in danger. His Majesty’s health is no longer what it used to be, and he has suffered a series of setbacks recently, so…”
If he had been taken good care of and had continued to take medicine, there wouldn’t have been any serious problems. However, too many things have happened recently, and even Emperor Jingwen, as the emperor, cannot avoid them.
It may be that it is precisely because he is the emperor that things will be even worse.
The Crown Prince, the Second Prince, the Fourth Prince, the Eldest Prince, the Thirteenth Prince… one after another, even the strongest person could not bear it, not to mention that Emperor Jingwen already had a hidden illness, and now I’m afraid that no medicine would be able to work. At most, it would just delay time.
Monks do not tell lies, the abbot said it clearly.
Thinking that once the emperor died, it would surely cause fighting among all parties, and the people would suffer, the abbot could not help but feel compassion and subconsciously chanted the Buddha’s name: “Amitabha.”
Even Emperor Jingwen fell silent after hearing this.
As an emperor, who wouldn’t want to live forever? Even ordinary people have a fear of death and a desire to survive.
So Emperor Jingwen asked, “Is there any way to save?” As long as there was a glimmer of hope, Emperor Jingwen would do everything he could, no matter what.
The abbot paused and shook his head.
“It has nothing to do with medicine. No matter how good the medicine is, it can’t heal a broken heart.”
The imperial physician standing by broke out in a cold sweat upon seeing this.
For a moment, Emperor Jingwen wanted to laugh and cry at the same time, blaming God for being blind and hating fate for being unfair. He had clearly already sat in the supreme position, so why didn’t he give himself an endless life?
As a monarch, you are the ruler of all people. Why can’t you control your own destiny?
So hateful!
He hated it so much!
“Cough cough cough…”
Emperor Jingwen was so excited that he started coughing uncontrollably. The imperial physician and the abbot immediately became nervous when they saw this. The abbot in particular hurriedly said, “Your Majesty, have you forgotten what I just said? Don’t be sad or angry, otherwise it will only speed up the process, Your Majesty!”
Seeing that things were hopeless, Emperor Jingwen finally calmed down and had to compromise with God.
“In this case, how long do I have left in this world?”
It was not until this time that Emperor Jingwen realised that he still had so many things to do.
Now that the crown prince is gone, such a huge Zhou Dynasty must choose a new heir. Otherwise, once he is gone, the Zhou Dynasty will inevitably be in chaos.
However, the abbot was not sure: “Maybe it will take a year or two, or maybe… in the next moment.”
Everything depends on when the main vein connecting to Emperor Jingwen’s heart will be completely severed.
Upon hearing this, Emperor Jingwen’s first reaction was to summon Wang Ziquan to his side.
“Your Majesty!” Wang Ziquan had served him for many years. Seeing this scene, he knelt down with a plop, and couldn’t help but feel sad.
“Why are you crying? I’m not dead yet.”
Emperor Jingwen took a deep breath and issued the first imperial decree.
“Pass on my order, summon all the generals to appear before me, and all other officials are on standby. From now on, attack Beiting at all costs.”
Now, everything that happened was caused by Beiting. Beiting was really going too far!
No matter what, Emperor Jingwen could not tolerate it any longer.
Then, Emperor Jingwen said, “Come here, get some paper and pen.”
Since he might die at any time, in order to ensure that the Great Zhou would not fall into chaos after his death, Emperor Jingwen could only find a successor quickly.
However, the matter of appointing a crown prince was a state secret, and even Wang Ziquan could not be present.
Upon seeing this, the imperial physician and the abbot immediately stepped back before Emperor Jingwen could pick up the brush. The three of them lowered their heads, not daring to look any further.
Emperor Jingwen pondered for a long time before finally putting pen to paper.
Now there are only a few princes left who are of the right age. The eldest prince is rebellious, the second prince was demoted to a commoner, the crown prince… the crown prince died early, the fourth prince was assassinated, and the fifth prince… Thinking of the fifth prince, Emperor Jingwen shook his head.
Although this boy is not as vicious as his brother, he is not broad-minded. He is impulsive and irritable. He has a quick wit but a hot temper. He is not a suitable candidate for the crown prince.
The Seventh Prince is a man of deep thoughts, but he has no one to support him. Even if he succeeds in ascending to the throne, he will be pulled down immediately.
As for the Eighth Prince, he had been extremely intelligent since childhood and did his job well. It was a pity that the incident with the First Prince had just happened. He and the First Prince were born of the same mother. This alone was enough to make Emperor Jingwen hesitate.
Xiaojiu’s words… As soon as Emperor Jingwen thought of his son, he immediately crossed his name off the list without hesitation.
If Xiaojiu takes the throne, the Great Zhou will be hopeless. And most of the important officials who taught him will probably retire and return home.
The princes after that were too young to be included in the reference.
During the month when he was missing, in addition to the eldest prince, another son performed extremely well. From all perspectives, he was the most suitable candidate at the moment.
After considering for a while, Emperor Jingwen finally wrote the word “six” on the imperial edict.
Although the Sixth Prince was not registered under the name of the Imperial Concubine, he had lived in Qiuwu Palace for ten years after all. When he was in the palace, the Sixth Prince’s wife often visited the Imperial Concubine.
The Sixth Prince must have some feelings for the Imperial Concubine and the others. If he ascends the throne in the future, it will be a good thing for them.
However, this alone was not enough. Imperial Concubine Guifei and Xiaojiu had only titles but no power. They seemed to be enjoying a prosperous life on the surface, but after he left, the situation would soon be completely different.
The power in the palace changes over time, and after all, a new emperor appoints new ministers.
Without his protection, how could the three of them, mother and children, survive?
Through the gap in the window, he saw his youngest son, whose face had turned blue from the cold and who was holding a child in a daze. To be on the safe side, Emperor Jingwen finally wrote a third imperial edict.

chapters.title: Chapter 211: Training
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {330+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
In the past, Emperor Jingwen did not have a deep impression of his son, the Sixth Prince. He only knew that he did a good job in the Ministry of Personnel and was a very capable prince. That was why he deliberately kept the Sixth Prince in Shangjing when he went on a southern tour.
What really made Emperor Jingwen take a new look at the Sixth Prince was that the Sixth Prince shone brilliantly during his disappearance and turned the tide single-handedly, which made Emperor Jingwen realize that this son was not just capable.
As for the second and third imperial edicts, especially the third one, Emperor Jingwen planned to wait until his death before handing them over to Xiaojiu, to prevent Xiaojiu from getting them too early and taking advantage of the situation.
Emperor Jingwen believed that his youngest son was fully capable of accomplishing this.
As for the second imperial edict, although it cannot be made public for the moment and cannot clearly state who the emperor prefers to succeed the throne, he can still let out a little rumour.
It is true that He Xiang and most of the civil officials are standing behind the Sixth Prince, but they do not have the military power. The military power is still in the hands of Emperor Jingwen, so Emperor Jingwen is not as afraid of them as he is of the eldest prince.
No matter how powerful the civil officials are, as long as they are not connected with the military generals, there is no need to worry too much.
After reading through history, Emperor Jingwen could not find many examples of civil officials who successfully plotted rebellion. I just don’t know whether the Sixth Prince saw this clearly and did it on purpose, or it was just a coincidence or luck.
Since he has real power and will not arouse my suspicion, if it is the former, then this guy’s scheming is too terrifying.However, despite thinking this in his heart, Emperor Jingwen did not seem worried at all. Instead, he was very happy.
It is better to be smart than to be stupid. Emperor Jingwen certainly hopes that his successor will be as smart as possible.
The smarter a person is, the more he knows what he can and cannot do. He doesn’t need to remind them. They can find the way that suits them best by themselves, without them even having to say much.
Throughout the entire process, all Emperor Jingwen needed to do was to assess whether he was qualified and whether he had the ability to shoulder the heavy burden of a country.
What happens next depends on what the Sixth Prince decides to do.
I have been in this position for so many years, it’s time to take a break.
He personally placed the two imperial edicts into a wooden box and sealed it with yellow wax. Then Emperor Jingwen whispered a few words to Wu Yi, and soon Wu Yi disappeared with the two boxes.
Even Wang Ziquan didn’t know where the secret guards would put the two wooden boxes.
Seeing his youngest son shivering in the cold outside, Emperor Jingwen finally waved his hand and said, “Tell them that I’m fine now. Tell those people outside to go back first.”
“yes.”
Wang Ziquan accepted the order and went out.
Outside, Ye Shuo had superb internal skills and he was also young. Twenty years old was the time when his energy was at its peak. If he was alone, he wouldn’t be so cold, but he had no choice but to hold a lump of ice in his arms, so wouldn’t he be cold?
Although Ye Jin is very young, he doesn’t have the temper of a child, and his hands and feet are very cold.
Ye Shuo remembered that Ye Yan and his friends had no problem running around the palace in thin clothes in the middle of winter, as stubborn as a lump of iron. Even Ye Xun, who was a bit more elegant, would not go to such an extent.
Ye Shuo took a lot of effort to warm the child in his arms.
Feeling the warmth all around, Ye Jin’s young heart was filled with emotion at this moment. He felt that the Ninth Prince was not like what he had imagined, with his mind full of playing.
The Ninth Prince is also a very considerate and gentle person.
Gradually, Ye Jin stopped struggling.
However, before he could be happy for long, he saw the Ninth Prince secretly tugging at the hem of the Seventh Aunt’s clothes while no one was paying attention.
Girls are prone to colds. What if she gets hurt by kneeling all night?
Seeing Jianjian turn around, Ye Shuo spoke in a voice that only the two of them could hear: “Do you want it? I just covered it.”
“?”
Jianjian was a little confused at first and didn’t know what he meant. She followed his gaze and saw her little nephew with a red face and sweat all over. It took her a while to react.
Jianjian: “…”
Any child who falls into his hands will be in big trouble.
Ye Jin was stunned for a moment, then his eyes widened instantly.
However, at this moment, there was a “creak” sound, and the door of a room not far away was opened, and Ye Shuo, Jian Jian and others were instantly worried.
Without caring about anything else, the two of them looked over subconsciously.
When he heard that his adoptive father was fine, Ye Shuo subconsciously breathed a sigh of relief, and the same went for Jian Jian beside him.
Jianjian had never experienced what Ye Shuo had experienced before. She was held in the arms of Emperor Jingwen when she was only a few months old. Later, Emperor Jingwen taught her to read and write personally. In addition, children are naturally close to their parents, so Jianjian’s feelings for Emperor Jingwen are naturally much deeper than Ye Shuo’s.
Wang Ziquan looked around and took in everyone’s expressions at that moment.
“My dear ladies and princes, the emperor has ordered that you all drink some hot tea and go to rest.”
After enduring such a night, everyone felt a little exhausted.
After Eunuch Wang left, Ye Shuo hurried to help his mother. The imperial concubine was now exhausted, her legs were numb and painful, and she could hardly walk.
In the end, Ye Shuo and Jian Jian supported her on both sides and returned to her room.
Then Ye Shuo did not go to find the Sixth Prince, but took Ye Jin to sleep.
It’s okay for adults, but it’s really pitiful that the children have to hold on for such a long time.
Ye Jin felt very awkward and embarrassed when he saw this, but Ye Shuo did not give him any chance to resist. He quickly stripped off his clothes, leaving only his underwear, and then stuffed him into the quilt.
There was no way. Since he had promised the Sixth Prince, he would naturally not let his nephew out of his sight.
It’s just sleeping on the same bed, what’s the big deal? Many people have slept with Ye Shuo. When he was a child, Ye Shuo even slept in the same quilt with his father.
Ye Jin felt cold all over at first, and then a person like a stove came close to her, and in a short while, the quilt felt warm.
Ye Jin still remembers that when he slept with his father, even with several hand warmers placed around, it would take an hour or two for the quilt to be completely warm. Sometimes it was so cold in winter that the back half of the quilt would be ice-cold all night.
It was the first time that Ye Jin felt so comfortable. For a moment he hesitated whether to get closer, but he was really shy.
Just when Ye Jin was struggling, a pair of big hands pulled him closer, tucked the quilt on one side of him, and said something that was so familiar to everyone: “What are you staring at? Go to sleep!”
Ye Jin closed his eyes subconsciously.
However, although Ye Shuo said this, his eyes were wide open and he didn’t feel sleepy at all.
There are all kinds of thoughts in his mind, so noisy.
It would be nice if people never grew up in their whole life.
It was noon in a blink of an eye. Ye Jin woke up and saw the Ninth Prince bringing in hot vegetarian noodles: “Eat quickly, I’ll take you to find your father later.”
Such a long time has passed, and the Fourth Prince’s affairs must have been dealt with.
Just as Ye Shuo expected, when Ye Shuo brought little Ye Jin over, the Sixth Prince had already ordered the monks to clean the Fourth Prince’s body and change him into clean clothes, and then, with the approval of Concubine Xian, placed the Fourth Prince in the coffin.
Until now, Concubine Xian still cannot accept the news of her son’s death. Her eyes are red and swollen, and she is on the verge of collapse.
Women in ancient palaces were restricted by etiquette and often regarded their husbands and sons as the pillars of their lives. In such an environment, Concubine Xian inevitably placed all her hopes on the Fourth Prince.
Now that the Fourth Prince died so easily, how could Concubine Xian bear it?
Not to mention her, even Ye Shuo found it difficult to accept.
Ye Shuo is already a mentally mature adult. To be honest, his relationship with the Fourth Prince is not that deep. It is just a brotherly relationship at most.
Even if the Fourth Prince died in the fight for the throne, it was what he wanted. If you want to get something, you have to pay a price. Ye Shuo would not be so upset.
The reason why Ye Shuo found it hard to accept was that the Fourth Prince died because of his kindness.
To die for doing good is so absurd and ironic.
He had worked so hard, he had survived the pain of a broken leg, and he had successfully rehabilitated despite the great pain, all of which Ye Shuo had watched happen. He still had so many ambitions that had not been realised, and at the moment before his death, he still had infinite visions for the future.
He had persevered despite such difficulties, so why did he collapse here?
Ye Shuo couldn’t figure it out no matter how hard he tried.
But all Ye Shuo could do was to burn some incense for the Fourth Prince at the end.
A few days later, Emperor Jingwen was able to get out of bed.
Emperor Jingwen’s injury was in his heart, and there was no visible abnormality from the outside, but everyone knew that the emperor was seriously injured and dying.
We also learned that Emperor Jingwen seemed to have appointed a successor on the night he fell ill, and it seemed that the successor was the Sixth Prince.
Emperor Jingwen seemed unaware of the undercurrents and handed over the task of collecting grain and fodder to him. His attitude became increasingly ambiguous.
In the past, such an important matter would have been supervised by Emperor Jingwen himself, or at least handed over to his trusted ministers. But now, the Sixth Prince has been chosen. It has to be said that this is an incredible signal.
The Sixth Prince understood it almost instantly.
All my planning and careful steps were worth it. Finally, I waited for this day.
Under the gaze of all the princes, the Sixth Prince forced himself not to reveal any clues and said as calmly as possible: “I will follow my father’s order.”
Emperor Jingwen was satisfied when he saw this.
My son is indeed very smart. Perhaps I can entrust more things to him in the future.
Ye Shuo on the side had almost guessed something and sighed in his heart. No matter what, Xiao Ming had finally achieved his wish.
The matter came to a temporary end. With an order from Emperor Jingwen, a group of people set off to return to Shangjing. By that time, the bodies of the Beiting people outside Shangjing City had already been cleared away.
After a busy time, Ye Shuo returned home exhausted.
Yao Zhi, who had been helping Ye Shuo protect his nephew in the prince’s mansion, had never been out and had no idea what was happening outside.
After seeing him, Yao Zhi knew it was time for her to leave.
But before leaving, she still had some things to say.
“Tell your fourth brother to remember to take good care of his leg. Maybe the condition won’t be so serious in the future.”
“Also, don’t overwork yourself, stand less and sit more, and be careful when you sleep at night so you don’t press yourself down.”
“Oh, by the way, I wrote down the acupuncture points and prescriptions in advance. You can take them to the imperial physician for a checkup when the time comes.”
“…No.”
Looking at the prescription and medicine bottle in her hand, Ye Shuo suddenly felt bitter: “My fourth brother…can’t use it anymore.”
Yao Zhi was stunned: “Why?”
Then she remembered something: “If you have found a better doctor, it doesn’t matter if you don’t use these things.”
“no.”
Ye Shuo opened his mouth and it took a long time before he said the following sentence.
“My fourth brother…is no longer with us.”
With a “bang”, the medicine bottle in Yao Zhi’s hand fell to the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 212: Pity
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {330+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
How could it be? How could he die?
The Fourth Prince was such a grown man, he just went out for a trip, how could he just die?
He was not a fragile child, he was a healthy adult!
Yao Zhi was speechless for a long time, shocked to the point of being speechless. After a while, she stuttered and asked, “How, how come he’s gone? Is it because of illness?”
But before they set off, Yao Zhiming had clearly just checked the Fourth Prince’s pulse.
Until now, Yao Zhi still holds out a glimmer of hope.
The Thirteenth Prince has now been escorted to the capital and will be executed soon. The Fourth Prince will also be buried soon. This matter itself is no secret.
After a moment of silence, Ye Shuo said, “Killed by Thirteenth Brother.”
Almost instantly, Yao Zhi felt a chill running through her bones.Behind the royal glamour, there is a darkness that others cannot fathom. Yao Zhi has seen too much of it these days.
Even though Yao Zhi had been in the martial arts world for many years and had seen many lives disappear before her eyes, she still found it hard to accept the news when she suddenly heard it.
Really… it was too sudden.
After a long while, Yao Zhi opened her mouth with some difficulty: “Has it always been like this?”
In fact, it has been like this from beginning to end.
But fortunately, Ye Shuo had been able to handle it in the past, so he said: “Not really…”
However, one’s own eyes and personal experience cannot deceive others.
Yao Zhi couldn’t imagine what kind of life he had led in the past twenty years.
Last time it was the crown prince, this time it’s the fourth prince, will it be his turn next time?
Ye Shuo seemed to see her worry and quickly said, “Don’t worry, I will protect myself.”
Ye Shuo’s goal was different from that of his other brothers. From the beginning to the end, he just wanted to live a good life, to be a leisurely prince and enjoy all the happiness in the world.
Ye Shuo does not have such great ambitions, nor such high pursuits, so he is relatively less dangerous.
“I am now a prince and I am favoured by my father. My brothers will not do anything to me.”
In the past, the crown prince was the emperor’s most beloved son, but what happened?
Because of Ye Shuo, Yao Zhi unconsciously understood so much.
The more he said this, the more worried Yao Zhi became, and she hesitated for a moment.
To be honest, the former Ninth Prince’s Mansion, now the Prince Rui’s Mansion, is completely different from what she had imagined. The Prince Rui’s Mansion is very clean, without so many messy things, and the servants are all very obedient. She has lived here for so long and has not seen any usurpation of power. It is not as complicated as she had imagined. The rejection in Yao Zhi’s heart gradually lessened.
Yao Zhi was in a dilemma: “If I leave, what if someone assassinates you?”
Ye Shuo answered without hesitation: “There are so many guards in the yard, ordinary people can’t get in at all.”
“Besides, it’s not like I don’t have any skills myself.”
Forget it, he has only just learned how to wield a sword skillfully.
Yao Zhi asked again: “What if someone poisoned you?”
Ye Shuo: “I am a prince, who dares?”
However, he was clearly worried about Ye Xun’s safety, and he specifically asked me to take care of him before leaving, which shows that such a thing is not impossible.
Every time Yao Zhi said something, Ye Shuo would refute her, and finally Yao Zhi became anxious.
But Ye Shuo seemed not to notice it and was still saying something.
“Don’t worry, I can do it alone.” In order to prove that what he said was true, Ye Shuo wanted to show her his recent training results on the spot.
“I have already learned everything you taught me. If you don’t believe me, just look.”
“You fool!” How could a person who usually looked quite smart suddenly become so stupid?
Yao Zhi was so angry that she pushed him out without mercy. In the end, she still felt that it was not enough, so Yao Zhi closed the door.
No matter how Ye Shuo shouted outside, she remained unmoved.
Ignoring the “knock knock knock” sounds outside, Yao Zhi bit her lower lip and finally put the packed bag back.
Yao Zhi decided not to leave.
Because I really don’t want him to die…
Ye Shuo outside was completely unaware and no one opened the door for a long time. About half an hour later, Ye Shuo left with drooping shoulders.
Yao Zhi secretly watched his back through the crack in the door, and couldn’t help but stomped her feet.
“Fool!”
Then, it was time to fight a war with Beiting.
Now that his father has spoken, the Sixth Prince will naturally try his best.
Especially after the rumour of appointing a crown prince came out, this was the first task his father entrusted to him, and he had to do it perfectly.
The Sixth Prince had no time to rest at all and immediately became busy after returning to Shangjing.
The Sixth Prince was not very proficient in matters of war, as his father would take care of everything. All he had to do was calculate the amount of silver he would need to spend and prepare food and fodder for the march.
These two things are easy to say, but difficult to do.
It was a huge undertaking to feed so many people. It also involved a series of steps, such as transportation, grain collection, and grain purchase. If any of these steps went wrong or the timing was not right, people would start dying within a few days.
Sometimes what determines the outcome of a war is not the strength of the two sides, but the logistical supply. If the logistical supply cannot keep up, the soldiers will have to fight on an empty stomach, and their strength and morale will inevitably decline, making it very difficult to win.
Although there are many educated people nowadays, there are very few who are good at maths. It is even more difficult to find someone with outstanding arithmetic skills.
The Sixth Prince searched all six ministries and finally found a perfect candidate in the Ministry of Revenue.
That person was originally just a minor official of the seventh rank. He was summoned to the Ministry of Revenue because of his unparalleled arithmetic ability. As long as the annual accounts passed through his hands, there would be no mistakes. He was also very good at telling real and fake account books, and knew the prices of all kinds of commodities in the market. Any watered-down account would not escape his eyes.
In addition, he also has his own calculation system, and only he can understand the Arabic numerals he talks about.
After the Sixth Prince found him, he set questions on the spot to test him.
The matter of war concerns the foundation of the country and must be handled with extreme caution. Therefore, the difficulty of the questions set by the Sixth Prince can be imagined.
The Sixth Prince originally thought that it would take him an hour to fully understand it. Given how complicated it was, one hour was already quite fast.
The Sixth Prince had even tried it himself, and it took him about three hours to completely solve it. But after all, he was not an accountant, so if he could complete it within an hour, the Sixth Prince would consider employing him.
However, what the Sixth Prince did not expect was that it did not take an hour at all. In even less than the time of an incense stick, the other party had already come up with the answer.
“If I have calculated correctly, the total cost will be 113,652 taels and 7 coins and 42 copper coins.”
The man was very respectful, but it shocked the Sixth Prince.
After several verifications, it was confirmed that the number was correct, but what the Sixth Prince didn’t understand was how he could add up so many fragmented numbers so quickly.
It was such a thick accounting book that the Sixth Prince had to waste a lot of paper to get the result, but he was able to get the result after just a glance at it. It was really shocking.
But what the Sixth Prince didn’t know was that some people were born with a keen sense of numbers, and with some training they could achieve mental arithmetic.
Not only was the young man good at mental arithmetic, he was also extremely good at using an abacus. No matter how huge the number was, if he couldn’t do mental arithmetic, an abacus would be enough.
And the money for food and fodder needed for the war was not even enough to require him to use an abacus.
The Sixth Prince made the decision without hesitation and immediately included him in the army.
Of course, to be on the safe side, the Sixth Prince only asked him to take charge of some simple tasks at the beginning, and let him get the hang of it slowly. If he can really play a role, his future will naturally be limitless.
The young man naturally knew that his chance to show himself had come.
In the past, young people felt disappointed that their seniors who graduated with them or graduated only two or three years earlier than them had already become outstanding people and were now doing well in the court.
The most powerful one among them had already started to manage the salt administration, while he was still just a minor official of the seventh rank. Such a gap between them made the young man too ashamed to face his two teachers. He was even more ashamed to admit where he graduated from and who his teacher was.
But he really had no other extraordinary abilities. If his teacher had not told him in the letter that arithmetic was a very important subject and told him not to give up, the young man would have just planned to become an accountant in the future.
Even when he was in the Ministry of Revenue, he was still doing the work of an accountant.
The young man had already accepted his fate, but this day finally came, and it proved that the teacher’s words were never wrong.
The young man let out a long breath and said, “I will obey your orders and will not let the Sixth Prince down.”
Seeing this, the Sixth Prince was naturally very satisfied.
However, Ye Shuo felt that this was not enough, Beiting was really going too far this time. Everything was caused by Beiting, so many lives were lost, and if he didn’t make them pay the price, Ye Shuo would find it hard to let go of the hatred in his heart.
Distilled liquor has huge profits. Over the years, Ye Shuo has accumulated a terrifying amount of wealth.
Not only was Ye Shuo prepared to take the lead immediately if the national treasury was in short supply, he also ordered several caravans to start dumping large amounts of liquor into Beiting, as if he would not stop until Beiting’s foundation was destroyed. In addition, the army in Lucheng had been trained for so long, and it was time to put it to use.
Ye Shuo also wanted to see what the scene would be like when an army that was well-fed and trained with modern special forces methods faced off against an ancient army. He hoped that he would not be disappointed.
Since Emperor Jingwen has made up his mind to teach Beiting a long lesson, the people under him will naturally be more efficient.
On the third day, the army was ready to go and divided into different batches, marching towards Beiting one after another.
Then, there were matters concerning the Queen and the Thirteenth Prince.
The Queen and the Thirteenth Prince colluded with Beiting and intended to overthrow the Great Zhou. They are truly despicable. Even the Queen’s status and the son of the Queen’s status cannot protect them.
During the morning court session, the king’s uncle lost control of himself and fell to the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 213: Death
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {330+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
The king’s uncle had been arrogant and domineering in the capital city for so many years, but in the end, all three clans were executed.
The Duke of Zhen’s family, who were hated by the emperor from the very beginning, are still doing well until now. It has to be said that this is really a trick of fate.
The one who had always been feared did not die, but the one who was specially pulled out to fight in the ring died first.
However, this was the result of Emperor Jingwen showing mercy. Otherwise, considering the Thirteenth Prince’s treasonous behaviour, it would not be excessive to execute all nine generations of his clan.
Then, it was the matter of deposing the queen.
Regardless of whether the Queen knew about it or was involved in it, she cannot escape responsibility for the Thirteenth Prince’s actions.
As the saying goes, when one prospers, all prosper; when one suffers, all suffer. In the harem, mothers and children have always influenced each other.
After ordering his men to drag the crying uncle out, Emperor Jingwen looked around and asked, “My dear ministers, do you have any objections?”
“this……”Originally, the matter of deposing and enthroning the empress was a state affair. The empress was the mother of a country. Even if the emperor disliked her, she could not be deposed at will. But unfortunately, the empress made a serious mistake this time. Since she was colluding with Beiting, no matter how high her status and position were, it would be useless.
The discussion gradually died down, and everyone looked at each other and said, “We, the officials, have no objection.”
So the matter was settled.
But even though there was no objection, it was only limited to the issue of deposing the queen.
Once the queen is deposed, the matter of appointing a new queen will be put on the agenda. I just don’t know which queen in the palace will be so lucky to sit in this position.
The ministers didn’t think much about it, and a person subconsciously popped up in their minds –
Concubine Rong.
Over the years, no matter how many times the palace selected beauties or how many new people entered, the most favoured one was always the imperial concubine.
Beauties in the palace come and go, but the imperial concubine remains forever.
If Emperor Jingwen had been a little more foolish, the imperial concubine would have been labeled a beauty who brought disaster. Fortunately, no matter how much Emperor Jingwen loved her, he would not break the rules, nor would he delay court affairs because of the imperial concubine.
As for the imperial concubine, she rarely acted unreasonably. At most, she was a little extravagant in her daily life, but with the support of the Duke of Zhen’s Mansion, it was still acceptable.
Just when everyone thought that Emperor Jingwen would make the imperial concubine the new queen and were ready to persuade him, they saw that Emperor Jingwen quickly changed the subject and had no intention of continuing it.
Emperor Jingwen had no intention of appointing a new queen. After all, at this time, the birth of a new queen would definitely cause another storm.
Because of the fight for the throne, the court has been in turmoil for too long. It’s time to take a break.
If the turmoil caused by the establishment of the new queen cannot be successfully quelled before his death, there will inevitably be another round of turmoil after his death.
The imperial concubine has a simple personality, Xiaojiu is not as cunning as his brothers, and Jianjian is still young. Even if he gave them the power, they would never be able to keep it. Therefore, giving them power at this time is not helping them, but harming them.
Just let the mother and her two children live a life of rich leisure for the rest of their lives.
Emperor Jingwen had no intention of registering the Sixth Prince under the name of the Imperial Concubine. In his opinion, if the Sixth Prince had feelings for the Imperial Concubine, he would treat the Imperial Concubine as his mother without the title. If he had no feelings, even if he forced him, it would only backfire.
When Emperor Jingwen was the crown prince, the previous emperor had asked him to recognize the current empress dowager, the then queen, as his mother. What was the result? After he ascended the throne, the empress dowager knew that she had violated a taboo and never left Changchun Palace for the rest of her life.
The most important thing is, if the imperial concubine becomes the empress dowager, her doting on Xiaojiu will definitely sow the seeds of disaster.
The doting of the concubine dowager on the youngest son is completely different from the doting of the empress dowager on the youngest son. The former is just the favoritism of the concubine and a family affair, while the latter is a state affair.
So after thinking about it, I decided to just forget it.
Obviously, the Sixth Prince was also clear in his mind. It was true that the Sixth Prince had feelings for the Imperial Concubine and Xiaojiu, but he did not want the Imperial Concubine to take the position of the Queen. In this way, Xiaojiu would become a real legitimate son.
Even if some things were not Xiaojiu’s original intention, it would be difficult to explain them clearly.
The Sixth Prince really didn’t want to see this happen, so he just maintained the status quo.
After the morning court session, Ye Shuo soon heard the news. Ye Shuo couldn’t help but secretly look at his mother.
If I remember correctly, his mother had aimed to become the queen in her early years. The reason why his mother didn’t get along with the queen was that she felt that the queen, who was inferior to her in every way, sat in that position, but she didn’t?
I remember that his mother wanted him to be the emperor. It can be said that she was very ambitious. I just don’t know if his mother has given up this idea after so much time has passed.
Noticing that her son was looking at her furtively, the imperial concubine asked in confusion, “Why are you looking at me like that?”
After hesitating for a moment, Ye Shuo tentatively spoke out what was in his mind.
“Mom…Aren’t you angry at all?”
His mother has been in the palace for more than 20 years, but the position of imperial concubine under her butt is as good as welded. It is still the same as it was at the beginning.
After her son’s reminder, the imperial concubine suddenly remembered that she once had such ambitions.
But the problem is that the imperial concubine is the kind of person who wants good things but doesn’t want to work hard, and instead hopes that pie will fall from the sky.
When Ye Shuo was just born, the imperial concubine did want to make some good plans for him, but as time went by, that enthusiasm gradually faded.
The imperial concubine felt that her current life was pretty good, and if she could maintain it until she died of old age, she would be very lucky.
Perhaps it’s because of what she saw about the Crown Prince and others, especially seeing Concubine Xian who was heartbroken and in tears every day, that the Imperial Concubine is now quite content.
As long as her son and daughter are safe, she has nothing else to ask for.
So the imperial concubine said: “If there is no, then there is no, what can I do about it.”
As for Jianjian, she is not stupid. If her mother suddenly became the queen, then she would be worried.
Although Jianjian is still young, she has already developed a sensitivity to the court. Because of her brother, if their father really gives them power, they will not be able to keep it at all, and it will be easy for trouble to arise.
Jianjian doesn’t think she has the ability to turn the tide when the time comes.
If I rely on my brother… forget it, I might as well rely on my mother. At least she won’t do anything rash.
It was rare for the three of them to reach a consensus on this. After all, they already had the title of the imperial concubine, the prince, and the princess. How much higher could they go? People should be content.
Soon, the events of Qiuwu Palace reached the ears of Emperor Jingwen.
Seeing that they had no special reaction to this matter, Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but feel relieved, but also a little bit of guilt.
Logically speaking, the imperial concubine has served him wholeheartedly for many years and gave birth to a pair of lovely children for him, so he should give her some honour. However, there are some things that he cannot do as he wishes.
The position of queen was out of the question, but being an imperial concubine was not a problem.
So when Emperor Jingwen issued an order to reward the Sixth Prince’s mother, he also promoted the position of the Imperial Concubine.
The Sixth Prince naturally knew that his father was thinking about him, and he also knew that his father was thinking about the future lives of the Imperial Concubine, Xiao Jiu, and Jian Jian. However, the Sixth Prince was no longer at the age where he longed for his father’s love.
Compared to this illusory favour, power is more important.
As soon as this decree was issued, the imperial concubine, who was already in great favour, became even more popular.
I don’t know if it was a coincidence, but the day after she was conferred the title of Imperial Noble Consort was the day when the Queen and the Thirteenth Prince were sentenced to death.
The Queen and the Prince were of noble status, so the servants of the Imperial Household Department and the court officials naturally did not have the qualifications. In the end, it was Prince Su who came in person, bringing poisoned wine and white silk.
Compared to the crazy queen, the Thirteenth Prince was very calm and did not look like a thirteen-year-old child at all.
He couldn’t bear to live a day like this any more, and death was a relief for him.
The Thirteenth Prince was even somewhat happy that he could take all those whom he had not dared to resist before to the underworld.
Just as he thought, when he came back, Princess Huyan was long gone, leaving only a charred corpse.
Based on the Thirteenth Prince’s familiarity with Princess Huyan, he remembered every detail about her by heart. At just one glance, he knew that it was not her.
Princess Huyan failed to fulfil her promise to him to take him away from here and to share life and death with him.
But it didn’t matter. He had known for a long time that she was lying to him, and he would make sure that anyone who dared to deceive him would die a miserable death!
After so many days, the poison in the princess’ body should have taken effect long ago. I guess it must be a very painful experience.
Without waiting for Prince Su to speak, the Thirteenth Prince picked up the poisoned wine in front of him and drank it all in one gulp.
Seeing that he had no shame on his face until now, Prince Su couldn’t help but frown: “Don’t you feel any guilt at all?”
After all, he was just a child. After the poisoned wine entered his stomach, the Thirteenth Prince became nervous. Quietly wiping the sweat stains on his palms, he said casually: “Of course I regret it.”
Prince Su heaved a sigh of relief, but the next moment, he said, “I regret not killing enough of them all.”
Only the Fourth Prince was killed. It was such a loss. It was really such a loss.
“If I had a strong body, the ending would definitely be different. What a pity.”
Seeing the Thirteenth Prince’s regretful look, Prince Su frowned even tighter, and his voice became heavier: “Do you know that those people you are talking about are your father and your brothers!”
“Really? Then where were my father and brothers when I was suffering?”
From the beginning to the end, no one helped him even a little. To the Thirteenth Prince, they were just strangers, no, worse than strangers.
Everywhere he looked, they were all accomplices, all his enemies!
Since the Thirteenth Prince did not regard Emperor Jingwen as his father, he naturally would not regard the Great Zhou as his own country. He wished he could destroy this place, destroy the palace in front of him.
The Thirteenth Prince even secretly decided that if he succeeded, he would kill his father and all his brothers!
He would cut off their heads with his own hands, chop them all into pulp, and then throw them out to feed the dogs!
Prince Su didn’t know what he had been through over the years, so he naturally thought he was ugly at this moment.
Now that things have come to this, there is really no need to say anything more to avoid wasting time.
After a while, when the effect of the medicine took effect, the Thirteenth Prince felt as if his intestines and internal organs were twisted together and he was in excruciating pain.
So this is the taste of death. Perhaps only at this moment did the Thirteenth Prince seem like a real prince, rather than a dog at the mercy of others.
Listening to his mother’s crazy cursing and screaming, the Thirteenth Prince laughed heartily for the first time in his life.
When blood began to seep out of his eyes, nose, and ears, the Thirteenth Prince had only one thought left in his mind at the moment of death –
Finally, it’s coming to an end…
very nice.
I hope that in his next life, he can be like the Ninth Prince.

chapters.title: Chapter 214: Liar
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {330+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
Compared to the Thirteenth Prince, the Queen was in a much more embarrassed state.
The Thirteenth Prince had had enough of such a life. Death was a relief for him, but it was different for the Queen. She still had many things she wanted to do. Her goals had not been achieved yet. She had not suppressed the Imperial Concubine, and her son had not sat on the throne. How could she die?
When Prince Su came over, the Queen subconsciously struggled.
It is easy to say “to die” but hard to do it.
People’s desire to survive is so strong that no one can resist this instinct unless they are willing to do so.
No matter how much the queen wanted to maintain her dignity, she could not remain truly indifferent when faced with something that frightened her.
Prince Su sighed when he saw this, “Sister-in-law, you are really making things difficult for me.”
Prince Su had no opinion on his sister-in-law. The first one was good, but the next one was not bad either. When the new queen was appointed, the princess came to pay her respects and said she was a dignified and virtuous queen. But I don’t know what happened in these years to make her become like this.
Hearing Prince Su’s voice, the Queen subconsciously clenched her palms. Her long nails almost pierced into her flesh due to her nervousness: “I didn’t know about Thirteen’s affairs before.” She didn’t even know when the Princess of Beiting had become involved with her son.Thinking of this, the queen was filled with hatred.
However, the emperor had never come since returning from Zilu Peak, and the queen was imprisoned in her own palace, with no way to appeal for justice.
When Prince Su heard this, he naturally knew what she meant, and he also knew that the current queen wanted to cut off her relationship with the Thirteenth Prince.
But unfortunately, it was too late. Moreover, colluding with Beiting was a capital crime punishable by the extermination of nine generations of the clan. How could one get away with it by simply saying “I didn’t know”?
Prince Su paused and said, “Sister-in-law, please go on your way.”
The last glimmer of hope was shattered, and the queen finally fell into complete despair.
Under the control of several palace servants, the queen was eventually forced to drink poisoned wine.
When the poison took effect, the pain was so unbearable that the queen felt as if her internal organs were being smashed. She couldn’t help but scream.
Prince Su on the side couldn’t bear to watch any longer. In order to save the Queen’s final dignity, Prince Su led the palace servants to retreat and then waited quietly in the yard.
With a “creak”, the room was sealed immediately, completely cutting off the queen’s possibility of escape.
The only person left in the whole room was the dead Thirteenth Prince.
Perhaps it was because of the pain, or perhaps because of the deep hatred in her heart, the queen could not help but punch and kick the Thirteenth Prince, who had long since died. While kicking him, she cursed him crazily: “Debt collector! Unlucky star!”
If I had known this would happen, why would I have given birth to him? I didn’t want him to bring trouble to myself and my mother’s family.
The Thirteenth Prince didn’t move, just staring at her with his wide eyes.
“If I had known this would happen, I should have drowned you as soon as you were born!” She regretted it, she regretted it so much!
At first the queen still had some strength, but gradually, she couldn’t even stand up.
At the last moment, thoughts and images flashed through the queen’s mind, and without exception, all of them showed the appearance of Concubine Rong.
Concubine Rong challenged him, Concubine Rong was arrogant and domineering, Concubine Rong successfully gave birth to a prince…
Why, why did the beautiful but extremely vulgar imperial concubine get everything she wanted!
They both gave birth to a son against the emperor’s will, so how could she be so lucky? It was obvious that the emperor hated the Zhen family the most at the beginning, so why were they the ones who died in the end?
Why! Why! Why!
Oh my God, you are not fair!
In the end, the queen died in resentment and hatred.
Although the Thirteenth Prince had long since stopped making any sound, a closer look revealed that the corners of his lips were slightly raised, as if he was smiling…
He waited until dark, then ordered his men to open the door and go back inside.
Because the queen struggled desperately before her death, the tables, chairs, benches and various furnishings in the room fell to the ground, and the luxurious bedroom was in a mess.
Looking at the Thirteenth Prince’s clothes, they were all torn by the Queen, and there was blood in the gaps between her fingernails.
Neither the mother nor the son could close their eyes.
Looking at this scene, Prince Su finally sighed deeply, then ordered the palace servants to wrap the two men with a straw mat and prepare a coffin. He then had them hurriedly dragged out of the palace while it was getting dark, and then buried them in a random place outside of Shangjing City.
The queen had put in so much effort and done so many things over the years, but in the end, it was all in vain.
Maybe it was just bad timing, or maybe it was just bad weather, because it started to rain after a short while.
The other side.
In contrast to the Queen’s Palace, Qiuwu Palace is full of joy and bustle.
The Imperial Concubine was not a good person from the beginning. After so many years, she is still the same. Her essence has not changed much. She is gentle only to close relatives like Ye Shuo and Jian Jian. The Imperial Concubine may never like the Queen in her entire life.
According to the imperial concubine’s previous temperament, it was good of her not to allow people to set off two strings of firecrackers when she learned of the queen’s death. Now that her two children have grown up, she has become a little calmer, but she still does not feel sad.
If there is nothing, there is nothing. The imperial concubine cannot pretend to be so.
So after listening to it, the imperial concubine just sighed twice, feeling a little complicated, but she quickly put it behind her.
Today was the auspicious day for Noble Concubine to be promoted to Imperial Noble Concubine, but because it was raining, Noble Concubine Rong really didn’t want to make trouble, so she just set up a table in her own palace.
There were no outsiders in the entire Qiuwu Palace, only four people, Imperial Concubine Ye Shuo, Jian Jian, and Emperor Jingwen.
People like Xu Chongyi and the Sixth Prince and his wife, after sending their gifts, left very tactfully.
Under the warm candlelight, for a moment, this place really feels like home.
After dinner, seeing that the rain outside had not stopped but was getting heavier, Rong Guifei, no, now she should be called Rong Huang Guifei, could not help but said, “Why don’t you stay at the palace tonight and stay the night.”
Although Ye Shuo had left the palace several years ago, the imperial concubine had always kept his room and asked palace servants to clean it from time to time so that he could move in at any time.
Upon hearing this, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but look at his adoptive father standing beside him.
To be honest, Ye Shuo was not willing to wade back through the water. Although he had an umbrella and other things, it was inevitable that his clothes would get wet. However, this matter was not up to him after all. He was already twenty years old, and it was not justifiable for him to continue living in the palace. Unless his adoptive father allowed it, no one would dare to gossip about it.
Seeing his son looking at him like this, Emperor Jingwen cleared his throat and finally nodded.
At worst, I can just stay in the Imperial Concubine’s Palace today. It’s not a big deal.
After getting the approval of his stepfather, Ye Shuo whispered a few words to Xiao Luzi, who nodded. Then he asked someone to go to the palace to reply to Miss Yao, saying that the prince would not be coming back today.
The imperial concubine standing by couldn’t help feeling a little jealous when she saw this.
Her son was very attentive, yet he had to specially tell the girl about such a small matter. The imperial concubine suddenly felt as if the son she had raised for so many years would soon belong to someone else.
But even though she felt jealous, the imperial concubine was still more curious.
After all, she was the first girl her son fell in love with. Although her family background did not meet the imperial concubine’s expectations at all, the imperial concubine did not object from the beginning.
To be honest, the Imperial Concubine had heard the name “Miss Yao” countless times during this period of time, but she had never had the chance to meet her. In addition, a lot of things had happened recently, so the Imperial Concubine really didn’t have this opportunity.
Besides, the marriage has not even started yet, and yet she is summoned into the palace. If it doesn’t work out, who knows what others will say about her.
His son is a prince and a man, so he may not care, but it is different for girls.
Now the Imperial Concubine couldn’t help it any longer. She wanted to pretend that she didn’t care, but in fact, the urgency in her eyes was almost exposed: “What kind of person is Miss Yao?”
Ye Shuo touched his chin, thought for a moment, and said, “She is someone who can protect this son.”
“She is very good at martial arts and medicine. When this son is with her, he feels very safe. It’s as if with her around, he will never worry about being bullied.”
Emperor Jingwen on the side: “…”
“Cough!!!” Emperor Jingwen couldn’t help but cough loudly. He really couldn’t understand how his son had the nerve to say such nonsense as asking a girl to protect him.
Does he still have any shame?
As soon as these words came out, even the Imperial Concubine was suddenly entangled.
If her son said that the girl was pretty, the imperial concubine would worry that he was bewitched by the female enchantress outside.
If her son said that the girl had a good temper, the imperial concubine would not be able to help but wonder if the girl was pretending, or if she had used some means to curry favour with the powerful.
But his son said he could protect him…
How can a girl protect a man?
The Imperial Noble Consort was spoiled by her brothers since she was a child, and she felt that all men in the world should be like her father and brothers. But…it turns out that her son is a useless piece of paper?
As if he didn’t notice the change in his mother’s expression, Ye Shuo couldn’t help but count on his fingers: “Not only that, she also tolerates this son’s temper. Even if this son is unreasonable, she won’t get angry. She will apologise to this son and comfort him.”
“She would also go to the cliff to pick delicious fruits for this son. When this son just said he wanted to eat crabs, she walked dozens of miles along the mountain road to buy a large basket for him. She also helped this son look after his nephew. Since she came to the palace, this son no longer needed guards. She was enough. She could also help this son carry things and heavy objects when he went to the street every day.”
“Oh, by the way, she also teaches this son sword skills every day…”
According to what he said, ordinary noble ladies really could not satisfy him. Most of the noble ladies in big families were pampered. What they wanted was a considerate and gentle husband, not a child like him who needed someone to worry about and coax him everywhere.
After hearing this, the Imperial Concubine felt that this girl named Yao was too miserable. If she encountered such a thing, she would probably be so angry that she would die.
Then, a thought unconsciously flashed through the Imperial Concubine’s mind –
Could it be that the girl named Yao was deceived by her own son?

chapters.title: Chapter 215: Accomplishment
chapters.content:
(T/L NOTE: Everyone thank the buyers of {330+} chapters, that you got to read these bonus chapters!)
The more I think about it, the more I feel that this is the case, because how can a normal man and woman be like this?
Isn’t this pure upside down? Fortunately, the girl is willing.
The Imperial Concubine didn’t expect that her son would be like this when facing her, and would still be like this when he was with girls.
Subconsciously, the Imperial Concubine blurted out: “How could you do this?”
Ye Shuo was stunned: “Ah? Why can’t I?”
The Imperial Noble Consort then remembered that she seemed to have never taught him the normal way to get along with girls. But the Imperial Noble Consort did not mean to not teach him. She thought that these things would come naturally when people reached a certain age, so she did not take it to heart at all.
Only now did the Imperial Concubine realise the seriousness of the matter.
My son doesn’t know how to love others, let alone what it means to be gentle and considerate. He doesn’t even understand the principle of protecting the girl he likes!
The Imperial Concubine couldn’t help but gasp.If you think about it carefully, it makes sense. This child has been spoiled by me since he was young. How can he suddenly become smart?
The Imperial Noble Consort looked anxiously at Emperor Jingwen, because Emperor Jingwen had been with the girl for a whole month, and what happened between them must have been visible to him. Subconsciously, the Imperial Noble Consort wanted to confirm it with Emperor Jingwen.
God help me, don’t let that be true.
However, precisely because he had seen it with his own eyes, Emperor Jingwen could not lie.
At first, the girl had no idea who they were, but under the circumstances, she still worked hard without complaint.
As an emperor, Emperor Jingwen naturally disdained to lie. Apart from the difference in their status, Emperor Jingwen even disdained to make up for his son in this regard.
After a long silence, Emperor Jingwen said, “…it’s even more excessive.”
“He also wants girls to go hunting in the mountains and fishing in the rivers for him. The prey must be plump and the fish must be big enough.”
Oh my God! How could a girl do such a dangerous thing?
